dervis-irab:58-60.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلِكَ نَتْلُوهُ عَلَيْكَ مِنَ الْآياتِ): a resumptive clause, brought to explain what preceded concerning ʿĪsā. ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause نتلوه is the khabar (predicate); عليك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also permissible for the demonstrative to be the mubtadaʾ and the clause نتلوه to be in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, with من الآيات a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar. (وَالذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ): conjoined to الآيات, and الحكيم is a naʿt (adjective). (إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسى عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): resumptive speech, brought as a preface to mentioning the dispute of the delegation of Najrān, who came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him about the matter of ʿĪsā, peace be upon him. إنّ and its noun; عيسى is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and عند الله is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl. (كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar; آدم is a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa because it is a diptote, as has preceded. (خَلَقَهُ مِنْ تُرابٍ): the clause is explicative of the likeness of ʿĪsā to Ādam, with no grammatical position; خلقه is a verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the fāʿil (agent) is "he", referring to Allah, and من تراب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلقه. (ثُمَّ قالَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ): ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; قال is a past verb and له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قال; the clause كن (the complete kāna) is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); and His saying فيكون is conjoined, and it is the narration of a past state (ḥikāyat ḥāl māḍiya). (الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ): a resumptive clause, brought to establish that the firm truth upon which no change comes is from your Lord. الحق is a mubtadaʾ and من ربك is the khabar. It is also permissible for الحق to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "what We have narrated to you is the truth", with من ربك a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فَلا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "eloquent" fāʾ), i.e. "if you know this — and you do know it — then do not be…", and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position. لا is prohibitive and تكن is an incomplete imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you" (أنت), and من الممترين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The intent of the prohibition «لا تكن من الممترين» is either to further rouse him ﷺ to steadfastness and tranquillity — far be it from him to be one who doubts — or that the address is to others, out of gentleness toward them.

dervis-irab:61-63.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَاجَّكَ): he disputed with you, argued with you, and contended with you in argument. Al-muḥājja is of the mufāʿala pattern, and it only occurs between two or more.
(تَعالَوْا): تعال is an imperative verb according to the more correct view, and its lām is always with fatḥa. Its origin is a request to come forward from a high place, as a good omen and as a permission to the one called, since it is from ʿuluww (height) and rifʿa (elevation). So when you command a single person you say: تعال. Then its use was widened and it was used for a mere request to come. They faulted Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī for an error because he gave its lām a kasra with the yāʾ of address, in his saying:
أيا جارتا ما أنصف الدهر بيننا ... تعالي أقاسمك الهموم تعالي
(O neighbour, fate has not been fair between us; come, let me share the cares with you, come.)
It may be answered on his behalf that it is a poetic licence.
(نَبْتَهِلْ): al-mubāhala and al-ibtihāl originally mean mutual cursing. Its triliteral verb is بهله بهلًا, of the naṣara pattern: he cursed him. The active participle is bāhil, the feminine bāhila, after which an Arab tribe was named. Then the word developed and came to be applied to every supplication, whether for good or for evil, even if it is not cursing. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī used this word in Risālat al-Ghufrān, where he said, in the course of his discussion of the Khurramiyya, a sect of heretics (zanādiqa): «فعلى معتقدي هذه المقالة بهلة المبتهلين» ("so upon those who hold this doctrine be the bahla of the mubtahilūn"). Al-buhla, with ḍamma or fatḥa on the bāʾ, is the curse, i.e. "the curse of the cursers", and this meaning is the one intended in the verse.

* I'rab:
(فَمَنْ حَاجَّكَ فِيهِ): the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); حاجك is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as "he" (هو), and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) حاجك, and the pronoun refers to ʿĪsā or to the truth in general. The clause is resumptive, brought to explain the ruling on mubāhala and its conditions as derived from the Book and the Sunna. The gist of what the imams said about it is that after the Prophet ﷺ it is not permissible except in a matter that is important in the Sharīʿa, in which confusion and obstinacy have arisen that cannot be repelled except by mubāhala. (مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to حاجك, i.e. from that time; ما is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the clause جاءك is the ṣila (relative clause); من العلم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being of knowledge". (فَقُلْ: تَعالَوْا نَدْعُ أَبْناءَنا وَأَبْناءَكُمْ وَنِساءَنا وَنِساءَكُمْ وَأَنْفُسَنا وَأَنْفُسَكُمْ): the fāʾ is connective; قل is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun implied as "you" (أنت); تعالوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. The clause قل is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of «ما» [Translator's note: so in the source; the conditional noun here is مَن]. The clause تعالوا is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); ندع is an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to the request, and its fāʿil is "we" (نحن); أبناءنا is a mafʿūl bihi, and أبناءكم and what follows it are conjoined to His saying «أبناءنا». He attached them to him ﷺ, though the matter concerns only him and the one he was engaging in mubāhala, because that is more emphatic in indicating self-confidence and faith in the victory of his argument; otherwise he would not have exposed the pieces of his liver [i.e. his children] and his family to destruction. But the mubāhala did not take place, and the delegation went back with the excuse of consulting their people, without going into it, as is explained in the books of history, so refer to them. (ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ فَنَجْعَلْ لَعْنَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكاذِبِينَ): ثم is a conjunction of delay; نبتهل is an imperfect verb conjoined to ندع, jussive; the fāʾ is a conjunction of immediate succession and نجعل is conjoined to نبتهل, the fāʿil of both being "we"; لعنت الله is a mafʿūl bihi, and على الكاذبين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نجعل, or in the position of an accusative as being in the place of the second object. (إِنَّ هذا لَهُوَ الْقَصَصُ الْحَقُّ): resumptive speech, brought to establish what was mentioned before. إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and القصص is the khabar; or هو is a mubtadaʾ and القصص its khabar, the clause being the khabar of إنّ; الحق is a naʿt (adjective) of القصص. (وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ): the wāw is resumptive; ما is negative; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and إله is genitive in form and a mubtadaʾ. It is permissible for the khabar to be omitted, i.e. "for us" (لنا). إلا is a particle of restriction, and الله is a badal (substitute) from the position of إله, which is nominative. It is also permissible for الله to be the khabar of إله. The clause is resumptive. (وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): the i'rab of its like has preceded shortly. (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِالْمُفْسِدِينَ): the fāʾ is resumptive and the clause is resumptive; إن is conditional; تولوا is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of a jussive as the protasis. فإنّ: the fāʾ is connective; إنّ and its noun, and عليم is its khabar; بالمفسدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عليم, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis.

* Benefits:
The scholars stated explicitly that «لعنة» is written with an open tāʾ (لعنت) here and in Sūrat al-Nūr only; elsewhere it is written with the tāʾ marbūṭa, according to the well-known rule.

dervis-irab:64-64.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ): resumptive speech, brought to examine the controversy that arose about Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him, at the arrival of the delegation of Najrān. قل is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is "you"; يا is a vocative particle and أهل الكتاب is a muḍāf (construct) vocative (munādā). (تَعالَوْا إِلى كَلِمَةٍ سَواءٍ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكُمْ): the clause is accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). The i'rab of تعالوا preceded a little earlier; إلى كلمة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تعالوا; سواء is a naʿt (adjective); بيننا is an adverb of place attached to سواء, because it has been treated like maṣdars (verbal nouns), as preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara; and بينكم is conjoined to بيننا. (أَلَّا نَعْبُدَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ): أن and what is within its scope form an interpreted maṣdar that is a badal (substitute) from «كلمة», or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), implied as "it is" (هي). أن is maṣdar-forming and لا is negative; نعبد is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), implied as "we" (نحن); إلا is a particle of restriction and الله is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). In the language, al-kalima is applied to a meaningful sentence. (وَلا نُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْئاً): the wāw is a conjunction, لا is negative, and نشرك is conjoined to نعبد; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نشرك, and شيئا is a mafʿūl bihi or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); discussion of this i'rab has preceded. (وَلا يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنا بَعْضاً أَرْباباً مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; يتخذ is an imperfect verb conjoined to لا نعبد and لا نشرك; بعضنا is the fāʿil, بعضا its first object and أربابا its second object; من دون الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of «أربابا». (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَقُولُوا اشْهَدُوا بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and what follows it is resumptive speech with no grammatical position, brought to establish the answer to them. إن is conditional; تولوا is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), i.e. "they turned away". فقولوا: the fāʾ connects the apodosis, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). اشهدوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of an accusative as the maqūl al-qawl. بأنا: the bāʾ is a preposition; أنّ is a particle resembling the verb, نا is its noun and مسلمون its khabar; أنّ and what follows it are in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اشهدوا.

dervis-irab:108-109.t:
* I'rab:
(تِلْكَ آياتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوها عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ): a resumptive statement, brought to explain what comprised the bliss of the righteous and the punishment of the disbelievers. The demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (آيات الله) is its khabar (predicate); the clause (نتلوها عليك) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, i.e. "bound up with the truth", so the preposition and its genitive noun (بالحق) are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl as well. (وَمَا اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ ظُلْماً لِلْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative mā; (الله) is its noun, and the clause (يريد) is in the position of the accusative as its khabar; (ظلما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (للعالمين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «ظلما»; (العالمين) is genitive with the yāʾ in place of the kasra because it is treated like the sound masculine plural. (وَلِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ): the wāw is resumptive; (لله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ما) is a relative noun, the postponed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, which has no grammatical position; and (ما في الأرض) is conjoined to «ما في السموات». (وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إلى الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ترجع); (ترجع) is a passive imperfect verb, and (الأمور) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

* Rhetoric:
(Repetition — al-takrīr): in this verse is the device of repetition. The scholars of Arabic differed over the reason why Allah the Exalted repeated His name overtly in His words «وإلى الله ترجع الأمور» when His name had already come overtly before in His words «ولله ما في السموات وما في الأرض». One of the Basrans said: that is comparable to the Arabs' saying "As for Zayd, Zayd went", and as the poet said:
ألا لا أرى الموت يسبق الموت شيء ... نغص الموت ذا الغنى والفقيرا
(I see nothing that outstrips death; death has troubled both the rich and the poor.)
So he used an overt noun where a pronoun was expected. One of the Kufan grammarians said: that is not comparable to this verse of poetry, because the place of "death" in the verse is a place for a kināya, i.e. a pronoun, and that is not so in the Qur'anic verse, because His words «ولله ما في السموات وما في الأرض» are a statement having nothing to do with His words «وإلى الله ترجع الأمور»; for the meaning of each of the two statements is distinct from the meaning of the other, each being self-sufficient and not needing the other, whereas what the poet said, "I see not death", needs the completion of the statement about it. This second view is, in our opinion, the more preferable, because the meanings of the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the clarity it contains, are not directed towards anomalous speech and meanings, when it has a sound, existing interpretation in eloquent speech and in obvious meanings.

dervis-irab:110-110.t:
* I'rab:
(كُنْتُمْ خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ لِلنَّاسِ): a resumptive statement, brought to explain the state of this nation in its superiority over other nations, and to make the believers firm in what they are upon of inclining towards good and turning away from wrong. (كان) and its noun, and (خير أمة) is its khabar (predicate). It has also been said: (كان) is complete (tāmma), i.e. "you were found and created the best nation", but the first is preferable. (أخرجت) is a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هي"; (للناس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أخرجت); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a second khabar of (كنتم). It has been said: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it has been said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of (أمة); the views are of equal weight. (تَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ): the clause is a third khabar of (كنتم) or accusative as a ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī chose that it be resumptive, explaining their being the best nation, as you say: "Zayd is generous; he feeds people, clothes them and sees to what benefits them". I hold that it is explicative, with no grammatical position. (تأمرون) is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بالمعروف) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تأمرون); and likewise (وتنهون عن المنكر). (وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ): the clause is conjoined. (وَلَوْ آمَنَ أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ لَكانَ خَيْراً لَهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought as an answer to a question whose gist is: how did He say that, when there is no good in anything other than faith such that it could be said that faith is better than it? (لو) is conditional; (آمن) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; (أهل الكتاب) is the fāʿil; the lām occurs in the apodosis of (لو); (كان) is a defective past verb, its noun a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring back to the maṣdar (verbal noun), namely "faith", indicated by its verb; (خيرا) is the khabar of (كان); (لهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خيرا»; and the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (مِنْهُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ): the clause is resumptive, brought as an answer to what arises from the conditional (لو), which indicates the absence of faith. (منهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (المؤمنون) is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (أكثرهم) is a mubtadaʾ and (الفاسقون) is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
(Correspondence — al-muqābala): in the verse is the device of muqābala, for the antithesis (ṭibāq) is multiplied: between (تأمرون) and (تنهون), between (المعروف) and (المنكر), and between «المؤمنون» and «الفاسقون». Discussion of muqābala has preceded.

dervis-irab:65-66.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لِمَ تُحَاجُّونَ فِي إِبْراهِيمَ): resumptive speech to complete the story of the dispute concerning Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. يا is a vocative particle and أهل الكتاب is a muḍāf (construct) vocative (munādā). لم: the lām is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun whose alif was dropped after the preposition, as will come in the Benefits section; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تحاجون. تحاجون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); في إبراهيم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تحاجون. A muḍāf must be taken as omitted, i.e. "concerning the religion of Ibrāhīm", because disputing is not about persons themselves. (وَما أُنْزِلَتِ التَّوْراةُ وَالْإِنْجِيلُ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ما is negative; أنزلت is a past verb in the passive, التوراة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and الإنجيل is conjoined to التوراة; إلا is a particle of restriction; من بعده is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزلت, so it is an "emptied" exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). (أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and astonishment, and it enters upon something implied, which is what is conjoined to by this conjunction, i.e. "Do you not reflect, so that you do not understand the falsity of your claim?" (ها أَنْتُمْ هؤُلاءِ حاجَجْتُمْ فِيما لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ): the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh); أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and هؤلاء the khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, brought to show the falsity of their claim. The clause حاججتم is resumptive, brought to explain the clause before it. The meaning is: "You are these foolish persons, and the sign of your foolishness is that you have gone deep into wrangling and arrogance over what has no benefit in it." فيما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حاججتم; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of علم, and when it was fronted it was parsed as a ḥāl; علم is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative ما. (فَلِمَ تُحَاجُّونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and the i'rab of لم تحاجون preceded shortly. (فِيما لَيْسَ لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ): فيما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تحاجون; ليس is an incomplete past verb; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of ليس; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and علم is the postponed noun of ليس. (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يعلم is the khabar. وأنتم: the wāw is a conjunction and أنتم is a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, and the clause لا تعلمون is the khabar.

* Benefits:
1- Know that the basic rule is to join the hāʾ of tanbīh to the demonstrative, because the definiteness of demonstratives, in their original coinage, comes from what accompanies them of the speaker's physical pointing, with the hand or another limb. So a particle was brought at their beginning by which the speaker alerts the addressee, so that he turns to him and looks at whatever thing he is pointing to of what is present. It is often separated [from the demonstrative] by «أنا» and its sisters, as in: ها أنا ذا, ها أنتم أولاء, ها هو ذا, and rarely by something else. What is meant by your saying "ها أنا أفعل" is not that you are making yourself known to the addressee and informing him that you are not someone else, for this is absurd; rather the meaning in it, and in "ها أنت ذا تقول" and "ها هو ذا يفعل", is expressing astonishment at the occurrence of the content of the verb mentioned after the demonstrative from the speaker, the addressee or the absent person. The clause after the demonstrative is necessary to explain the astonishing matter, and it has no grammatical position since it is resumptive. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said:
«The origin of ها أنتم is أأنتم; the first hamza was replaced with hāʾ because it is its sister.»
Al-Naḥḥās said: this is a good view. Some said: it [the clause] is a ḥāl, i.e. "here you are, saying", and the ḥāl here is necessary because the benefit depends on it; the governor of the ḥāl is the particle of tanbīh or the demonstrative. What we hold is that what we established is preferable, and that the resumptive reading is the more likely, since what is meant is not "you are the one pointed to in the state of your saying".
How wonderful is this noble language!
2- When they join «ما» in interrogation [to a preposition], they drop its alif for several reasons. First, to distinguish between it and its being a particle. Second, because of its joining to the preposition, so that it became as if part of it, to indicate the strength of the connection. Third, for lightness, because «ما» occurs often in speech. They kept the fatḥa to indicate that what was dropped is of its kind, as they did in علام؟ إلام؟ حتام؟ بم؟ عم؟ فيم؟ and مم؟ It is said that a certain commoner asked one of the grammarians, saying to him: بما توصيني؟ ("With what do you counsel me?"), keeping the alif in «ما»; so he said: "With the fear of Allah, and dropping the alif from «ما»."

dervis-irab:67-68.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الحنف): inclining; what is meant is inclining away from all religions to the upright religion.

* I'rab:
(ما كانَ إِبْراهِيمُ يَهُودِيًّا وَلا نَصْرانِيًّا): resumptive speech which He, glory be to Him, brought to clear Ibrāhīm of what they tried to attach to him. ما is negative; كان is an incomplete past verb, إبراهيم its noun and يهوديا its khabar (predicate); the wāw is a conjunction, لا is negative, and نصرانيا is conjoined to «يهوديا». (وَلكِنْ كانَ حَنِيفاً مُسْلِماً): the wāw is a conjunction and لكن is lightened and inoperative; كان is an incomplete past verb, its noun is "he" (هو), حنيفا is its first khabar and مسلما a second khabar. (وَما كانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): conjoined to what preceded; من المشركين is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar of كان. (إِنَّ أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِإِبْراهِيمَ): إنّ and its noun; الناس is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and بإبراهيم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أولى. The clause is resumptive. (لَلَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ): the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and الذين is the khabar of إنّ; اتبعوه is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). (وَهذَا النَّبِيُّ): the wāw is a conjunction [conjoining] to الذين, and النبي is a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative. (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the wāw is a conjunction and الذين is a relative noun conjoined to هذا النبي, and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila. (وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), ولي is the khabar, and المؤمنين is a muḍāf ilayhi.

dervis-irab:69-71.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَلْبِسُونَ): with kasra on the bāʾ, i.e. you mix.

* I'rab:
(وَدَّتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ): ودت is a past verb and the tāʾ is for the feminine; طائفة is the fāʿil (agent), and من أهل الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of طائفة. The clause is resumptive, brought to speak about the Jews who invited a number of the Companions, among them Ḥudhayfa, Muʿādh and ʿAmmār, to their religion. An important discussion of the meaning of ودت will come in the Benefits section. (لَوْ يُضِلُّونَكُمْ): لو is maṣdar-forming; يضلونكم is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). لو together with what follows it is interpreted as an accusative maṣdar, because it is the object of ودت; the implied meaning is "they wished for your misguidance". (وَما يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ما is negative; يضلون is a verb and its fāʿil; إلا is a particle of restriction and أنفسهم is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَما يَشْعُرُونَ): conjoined to the previous clause. (يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ): a resumptive clause, brought to emphasise the feebleness of their minds. يا is a vocative particle and أهل الكتاب is a muḍāf (construct) vocative. لم: the lām is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun in the position of a genitive by the lām; the alif of ما was dropped because it occurs after a preposition, as preceded shortly. تكفرون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the preposition and genitive noun fronted before it are attached to it; بآيات الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تكفرون. (وَأَنْتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; أنتم is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); تشهدون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar (predicate); the clause أنتم تشهدون is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl. (يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لِمَ تَلْبِسُونَ الْحَقَّ بِالْباطِلِ): a third resumptive clause, brought to emphasise the feebleness of their minds; the i'rab of its like has preceded. (وَتَكْتُمُونَ الْحَقَّ): the wāw is a conjunction; تكتمون is an imperfect verb, the wāw is the fāʿil, and الحق is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ): its i'rab has preceded.

* Benefits:
«ودّ» is used in the sense of "to wish" (tamannā), and then لو or أن is used with it, and sometimes both are combined, so that one says: وددت لو أن فعل ("I wished that he had done"). The maṣdar is al-wadāda and the noun from it is wudd, and the two may overlap as maṣdar and noun. Al-Rāghib said: when ودّ is in the sense of "to love", it is never permissible to bring «لو» in with it. ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā said: when «ودّ» is in the sense of "to wish", it is suitable for the past, the present and the future; and when it is in the sense of love and will, it is suitable only for the past, because will is like a calling-for of the act. When it is for the present and the future, أن and لو are permissible; and when it is for the past, أن is not permissible, because أن is for the future. [Translator's note: the source text appears internally inconsistent here — it first says ودّ in the sense of love/will suits only the past, then reasons that will is a calling-for of the act; translated as written.]

dervis-irab:72-74.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَجْهَ النَّهارِ): its beginning. The face (al-wajh) is called wajh because it is the first thing of a person that appears to whoever sees him. The poet said:
من كان مسرورا بمقتل مالك ... فليأت نسوتنا بوجه نهار
(Whoever is glad at the killing of Mālik, let him come to our women at the face [i.e. the beginning] of the day.)
And he said:
وتضيء في وجه الظلام منيرة ... كجمانة البحري سلّ نظامها
(She shines in the face of the darkness, radiant, like the pearl of the diver whose string has been drawn out.)

* I'rab:
(وَقالَتْ طائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to speak about another kind of the Jews' deceptions. Twelve rabbis of the Jews of Khaybar conspired, and some of them said to others: "Enter the religion of Muḥammad at the beginning of the day with the tongue, without belief in the heart, then disbelieve at the end of the day, to bring doubt into the breasts of Muḥammad's Companions; perhaps that will lead to their turning back from their religion." قالت is a past verb, طائفة is the fāʿil (agent), and من أهل الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of طائفة. (آمِنُوا بِالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). آمنوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; بالذي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا; the clause أنزل is the ṣila (relative clause); أنزل is a past verb in the passive, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as "it" (هو); على الذين آمنوا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل, and the clause آمنوا is a ṣila. (وَجْهَ النَّهارِ): an adverb of time attached to آمنوا. (وَاكْفُرُوا آخِرَهُ): the wāw is a conjunction; اكفروا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, conjoined to آمنوا; آخره is an adverb of time attached to اكفروا. (لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ): the clause of hope is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "hoping for their turning back from their religion". لعلّ and its noun, and the clause يرجعون is its khabar (predicate). Then He followed it with the rest of their saying, so it falls within its scope. (وَلا تُؤْمِنُوا إِلَّا لِمَنْ تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; تؤمنوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil; إلا is a particle of exception. لمن: the lām is a preposition and من is a relative noun in the position of a genitive by the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of an accusative by exception from something omitted, implied as: "Do not believe — i.e. acknowledge and make known — that anyone is given the like of what you were given, to anyone of the people, except to your partisans, not others." تبع is a past verb and its fāʿil is "he"; the verbal clause is the ṣila, and دينكم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (قُلْ: إِنَّ الْهُدى هُدَى اللَّهِ): the clause made up of قل and what is said — namely إنّ with its noun and its khabar — has no grammatical position because it is parenthetical. (أَنْ يُؤْتى أَحَدٌ مِثْلَ ما أُوتِيتُمْ): أن and what is within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), genitive by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تؤمنوا. أحد is the nāʾib fāʿil of يؤتى and مثل is the second object; ما is a relative noun in the position of a genitive by annexation, and the clause أوتيتم is the ṣila. (أَوْ يُحاجُّوكُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ): أو is a conjunction; يحاجوكم is an imperfect verb conjoined to يؤتى, and the sign of its accusative is the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi; عند is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl, and ربكم is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (قُلْ إِنَّ الْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ): قل is an imperative verb and its fāʿil is "you"; إنّ and its noun, and بيد الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; إنّ and what is within its scope form a nominal clause in the position of an accusative as the maqūl al-qawl. (يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ): the clause يؤتيه is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl. يؤتي is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil is "he"; the hāʾ is the first object of يؤتي; من is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as the second object of يؤتي, and the clause يشاء is the ṣila. (وَاللَّهُ واسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), واسع a first khabar and عليم a second khabar. (يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ): the clause is a third khabar. يختص is an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil is "he", i.e. Allah the Exalted; برحمته is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يختص; من is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause يشاء has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ): the wāw is a conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ and ذو الفضل is the khabar, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the wāw in place of the ḍamma because it is one of the five nouns; الفضل is a muḍāf ilayhi and العظيم is a naʿt of الفضل.

* Benefits:
There has been much discussion of this verse and disagreement over its i'rab and its explanation; some parsers brought the possible analyses in it to nine, without arriving at a decisive one free of objections.

What al-Wāḥidī says:
Al-Wāḥidī, one of the great scholars occupied with questions of i'rab, said: «This verse is among the difficult passages of the Qur'an, and the hardest of it in i'rab and interpretation. I have reflected on the statements of the people of tafsīr and of [the books of] maʿānī on this verse, and I did not find a view that runs consistently through the verse from its beginning to its end while explaining the meaning and keeping the construction sound.»

What al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī says:
Al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī, known as al-Samīn, said: «Know that people, the exegetes and the parsers have differed on this verse in several ways.» Al-Samīn mentioned the nine analyses. Since our book aims at what is easiest, closest to reason and furthest from artificiality, we have confined ourselves in the I'rab section to what we presented there, and we considered it closest to what we aimed at; al-Zamakhsharī chose it in his Kashshāf. But we consider it useful to record what Abū Ḥayyān said, and then follow it with what Ibn Hishām said.

What Abū Ḥayyān says:
Abū Ḥayyān al-Andalusī said in his tafsīr al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ, after a long discussion:
«The statement admits several readings:
1- That the meaning is: Do not give true credence and belief except to one who comes with the like of your religion, for fear that anyone be given of prophethood and honour the like of what you were given, and for fear that they argue against you, by your having believed them, before their Lord [Translator's note: so in the source, «ربهم»] if they did not persist in it. This statement, on this meaning, is the fruit of envy and disbelief despite knowing the truth of the prophethood of Muḥammad ﷺ.
2- That the implied form is أن لا يؤتى, with لا omitted because the speech indicates it; and that this [negated content] falls within the scope of إلا, not being implied as entering before it. The meaning is: Do not believe anyone in anything except one who follows your religion, by virtue of the negation of anyone's being given the like of what you were given, and the negation of their arguing against you before your Lord — i.e. except with the negation of such-and-such.
3- That the implied form is بأن يؤتى, attached to تؤمنوا, and not falling within the scope of إلا. The meaning is: Do not believe that anyone is given the like of what you were given, except one who follows your religion, comes with its like and supports it, for that is not given to anyone other than you. And the meaning of أو يحاجوكم عند ربكم is "unless they argue against you", as you say: "I will not leave you or [i.e. unless] you pay me my due." This statement, on this meaning, is the fruit of their denying Muḥammad ﷺ, out of their belief that prophethood is only among the Children of Israel.
4- That the meaning is: Do not believe in Muḥammad and acknowledge his prophethood — since you have known its truth — except to the Jews who are of you; and أن يؤتى أحد مثلما أوتيتم is a description of the state of Muḥammad ﷺ. So the meaning is: conceal your acknowledgement that someone has been given the like of what you were given; or [else], for they — meaning the Arabs — will argue against you with the acknowledgement before your Lord.»
By my life, Abū Ḥayyān did excellently, but he confined himself to giving the meaning stripped of the i'rab.

What Ibn Hishām says:
Ibn Hishām said, in the course of his discussion of clauses: «The parenthetical clause is often confused with the circumstantial clause, and several things distinguish it from it. One of them is that it is non-declarative, like the imperative clause in «ولا تؤمنوا إلا لمن تبع دينكم قل: إن الهدى هدى الله أن يؤتى أحد مثلما أوتيتم». So Ibn Mālik and others gave it as an example, on the basis that «أن يؤتى أحد» is attached to تؤمنوا, and that the meaning is: Do not make known your belief that anyone is given of the books of Allah the like of what you were given, and that that "anyone" will argue against you before Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection with the truth and overcome you — except to the people of your religion, because that does not change their belief, unlike the Muslims, for that would increase them in steadfastness, and unlike the polytheists, for that would call them to Islam. The meaning of the parenthesis, then, is that guidance is in the hand of Allah, so if He decrees it for someone, their scheming will not harm him. The verse also admits another reading, namely that the speech is complete at the exception, and what is meant is: Do not make known the false faith [Translator's note: the source reads «لا تظهروا والإيمان», apparently with an extra wāw] which you profess at the beginning of the day and break at its end except to those who were of you, like ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, and then became Muslim; that is because their Islam was more vexing to them, and their return [Translator's note: the source has «رجوهم», apparently for رجوعهم] to disbelief was nearer in their view. On this reading «أن يؤتى» is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, and it is attached to something omitted and postponed, i.e.: out of dislike that anyone be given [the like], you contrived this plot.
This reading is preferable for two reasons. First, it agrees with the reading of Ibn Kathīr: أأن يؤتى with two hamzas, i.e.: "out of dislike that anyone be given, you said that". Second, in the first reading what precedes إلا governs what follows it, although it is not one of the three cases mentioned just before. The second of the things that distinguish it is [that the parenthetical clause may be] a supplication, as in the saying of ʿAwf ibn Muḥallim:
إن الثمانين، وبلغتها ... قد أحوجت سمعي إلى ترجمان
(Eighty years — and may you reach them — have made my hearing need an interpreter.)
or a declaration of transcendence, as in His saying, Exalted is He: «ويجعلون لله البنات، سبحانه، ولهم ما يشتهون», or an interrogative, as in His saying, Exalted is He: «فاستغفروا لذنوبهم، ومن يغفر الذنوب إلا الله ولم يصروا»» — to the end of this delightful discussion, which the dry style has muddied.

What al-Zamakhsharī says:
We cannot avoid mentioning the words of al-Zamakhsharī, which came in support of what we adopted in the i'rab. He said: «ولا تؤمنوا is connected to His saying أن يؤتى أحد, and what is between them is a parenthesis; i.e. do not make known your belief that anyone is given the like of what you were given except to the people of your religion, not others. They meant: keep secret your belief that the Muslims have been given the like of what you were given, and do not divulge it except to your partisans alone, not to the Muslims, lest it increase them in steadfastness, and not to the polytheists, lest it call them to Islam. أو يحاجوكم به عند ربكم is conjoined to أن يؤتى, and the pronoun in يحاجوكم is for أحد, because it has a plural meaning; [i.e.] and do not believe, [confiding it] to anyone but your followers, that the Muslims will argue against you on the Day of Resurrection with the truth and overcome you before Allah with the proof.»
We have almost gone beyond the condition of the book in summarising the views, so what we have presented is enough for us. Perhaps one of the scholars was right when he determined that this verse is the most difficult of the verses of these sūras, and the speech of Allah is greater, and the depth of our Arabic language is farther and deeper than can be fathomed.

dervis-irab:111-112.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ثُقِفُوا): its meaning has preceded; here it means "they were overtaken, overpowered and humbled". Among their sayings: "We sought him and we ثقفناه in such-and-such a place", i.e. we caught up with him. And "I ثقفت knowledge in the swiftest time" when you are quick in acquiring it. Abū Tammām was ثقفا لقفا (quick to grasp, quick to seize). (باؤُ): they returned.

* I'rab:
(لَنْ يَضُرُّوكُمْ إِلَّا أَذىً): a resumptive statement, brought to explain that their harm is cut short, occurring at intervals that are of no account. (لن) is a particle of negation, of the accusative and of the future; (يضروكم) is an imperfect verb, accusative by the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (أذى) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a harm limited to a temporary hurt which soon passes", so the exception is emptied (mufarragh). It has been said: the exception here is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), and Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī confined himself to this, saying: "This is of the disconnected exception which differs from the meaning of what precedes it, as is said: 'He complained of nothing except good' — and this is an expression reported from the Arabs by hearing." (وَإِنْ يُقاتِلُوكُمْ يُوَلُّوكُمُ الْأَدْبارَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (يقاتلوكم) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf the first mafʿūl bihi; [Translator's note: the source passes over the parsing of (يولوكم) itself and gives only its second object.] and (الأدبار) is the second mafʿūl bihi. (ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ): (ثم) is a conjunction of sequence with delay, and it has come here merely for resumption; (لا) is negative; (ينصرون) is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). In the section on rhetoric the secret of departing from conjunction with the jussive verb, as the context of the speech requires, will come; it is as if He said: "Then I inform you that they will not be helped." (ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ أَيْنَ ما ثُقِفُوا): the clause is resumptive, brought to establish the imposition of humiliation upon the Jews. (ضربت) is a passive past verb and the tāʾ is for the feminine; (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ضربت); (الذلة) is the nāʾib fāʿil; (أينما) is a jussive conditional noun, accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (ضربت); (ثقفوا) is a passive past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then it has been imposed upon them". (إِلَّا بِحَبْلٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ): (إلا) is a particle of exception, and the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as excepted from the most general of states, so it is an excepted element with the meaning of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. humiliation was imposed upon them in the most general of their states except in this state, namely their holding fast to a rope from Allah; (من الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective). On this view it is a connected exception (muttaṣil); others said: it is disconnected. Further explanation of this parsing will come in the section on benefits. (وَحَبْلٍ مِنَ النَّاسِ): conjoined to His words (بحبل من الله). (وَباؤُ بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (باءوا) is a conjoined past verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to the clause (ضربت); (بغضب) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (باءوا); and (من الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of (غضب). (وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَسْكَنَةُ): conjoined to what precedes; (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ضربت), and (المسكنة) is the nāʾib fāʿil of (ضربت). He repeated the clause as tawkīd (emphasis) of the humiliation imposed upon the Jews. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ): a resumptive clause, brought to explain the cause of imposing humiliation and wretchedness upon the Jews. The demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject), the reference being to what was mentioned of the imposition of humiliation and wretchedness and Allah's wrath. In (بأنهم), the bāʾ is a preposition, and (أن) and its noun; the interpreted maṣdar formed from (أن) and what falls within its scope is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the demonstrative. (كان) and its noun, and the clause is the khabar of «أنهم»; the clause (يكفرون) is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of (كانوا); and (بآيات الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يكفرون). (وَيَقْتُلُونَ الْأَنْبِياءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ): conjoined to what precedes; (الأنبياء) is the mafʿūl bihi, and (بغير حق) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (ذلِكَ بِما عَصَوْا وَكانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ): a resumptive statement, brought to explain the cause of the cause: their disobedience is the cause of their disbelief and their killing the prophets, and these two are the cause of the humiliation, wretchedness and wrath. The demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ; the bāʾ is a preposition and (ما) is maṣdariyya, i.e. "because of their disobedience", so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of «ذلك»; (كان) and its noun, and the clause (يعتدون) is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
These two verses comprise kinds of eloquence that have reached the loftiest limits of inimitability. Though the scholars of rhetoric, Allah's good pleasure be upon them, expatiated in bringing out their secrets, plumbing their depths and fathoming their hidden treasures, it has been granted to us to witness with our own eyes the fate of Palestine because of the Jews, and because of the deceptive, temporary success they attained. We shall first summarise what the scholars of rhetoric said, then follow it with what we ourselves have deduced and intuited of the inevitable end of the Jews.
1- In the first verse is a device called "the device of clarification" (fann al-īḍāḥ): it is that the speaker says something which on its face is ambiguous, then clarifies it in the rest of his speech. The difficulty which the clarification resolves may lie in the meanings of the rare words and in their parsing. On the face of this verse there are two difficulties, one from the side of parsing and the other from the side of meaning. As for the one from the side of parsing, it is the conjoining of what is not jussive to the jussive. The one from the side of meaning is that the beginning of the verse makes its closing (fāṣila) unnecessary, because their turning their backs at the time of fighting is evidence of their being forsaken, and being forsaken and being helped do not come together. The answer is that Allah, Glorified is He, informed the believers that this enemy of theirs, if he fights them, will be routed; then He wished to complete the promise by informing them that, along with his turning his back now, he will never be helped in the future; so he is forsaken forever, as long as he fights them.
Had it been confined to what is short of the fāṣila, the speech would not have fulfilled this intended meaning, because His words «وإن يقاتلوكم يولوكم الأدبار» do not give that whenever they fight them the matter will be so; for your saying «إذا جاء زيد أكرمته» ("When Zayd comes, I honour him") does not entail that whenever he comes, constantly and continually, honouring is upon you; it gives only that if he comes to you, you honour him for that coming. Since He, Glorified is He, knew that confining it to what is short of the fāṣila would not convey the permanence of this glad tiding to the end of time — and its permanence is what is intended — He said: «ثم لا ينصرون», and withheld the jussive from the verb, even though it is conjoined to a jussive, so that it would keep the meaning for which the imperfect form was coined, namely indicating the present and the future; and He intended resumption in the verb, not conjunction with what preceded. Allah, Glorified is He, wishes to put reassurance into the hearts of the believers who had pledged themselves to death, because martyrdom in the thick of battle and on the open plain of jihād is the beginning of a fresh new life, the life of glory and immortality, as the poet said:
إن تسل أين قبور العظما ... فعلى الأفواه أو في الأنفس
(If you ask where the graves of the great are: they are upon the lips or in the souls.)
We say: Allah, Glorified is He, wished to assure the believers who strive that victory would be their ally, so He followed the completed speech with a clause that makes the certainty clear, namely His words «ثم لا ينصرون», to convey permanence and continuity in jihād and not surrendering to the enemy, and to give them the glad tidings that their enemy is forsaken forever, that they must undertake fighting him at every time, and that they must not weaken if they imagine that their enemy has prevailed over them, for he must inevitably be forsaken in the days to come. The history of a nation is not reckoned by the reckoning of time, nor counted in a few years, and the life of nations and peoples is not like the life of individuals.
The second difficulty is that He conjoined the nominative imperfect verb to the jussive imperfect, and at first glance, or to those of mere superficial view, this appears contrary to what is preferable. But He departed from the jussive to the nominative so that it would be known that their not being helped is a covenant which Allah has bound upon Himself — and who is truer than Allah in speech or covenant? — and that the negation of help from them continues forever; no account is taken of the incidental cases and the temporary exceptional circumstances that present themselves to them over the long successive periods in which they are victorious. So He departed from the jussive which the context of the speech requires, as if He said: "Then I inform you, giving glad tidings, that they will never be helped in the future", as we indicated in the section on parsing.
2- The second device in this verse is "the device of suspension" (fann al-taʿlīq): it is that the speech is suspended for a time. For that reason the word «ثم» was chosen rather than the other conjunctions, because it indicates a delay befitting the imperfect verb's indication of the future, as if He said: "Then here is something higher in favour and loftier in the ranks of beneficence, namely that these Jews are a people who will not be helped at all, however much means come to them and however much aid is lavished upon them."
3- The third device in this verse is the device of semantic antithesis (al-muṭābaqa al-maʿnawiyya) between the victory of the believers and the forsaking of the disbelievers.
4- The fourth device in this verse is "the device of guarding" (fann al-iḥtirās): because if the speech had been conjoined with the wāw, for example, the short-sighted would have thought that they were promised victory only in that state and no other. So this thought was repelled by the word «ثم», which decides decisively, with no doubt clouding it, that the inevitable result is a resounding victory for the believers — lest some of those who do not like hastening towards death think that the promise of victory is in that state only, that war may go back and forth, and that their turn for victory may come. So He, Glorified is He, negated this possibility, and cut off the way for those who think so from seeking excuses for staying behind from jihād.
5- The fifth device is al-īghāl (pressing on), i.e. not stopping at the turning of backs even though the speech is complete; He completed it with what agrees with the rest of the verse-endings, along with that which completes the full meaning.
6- Then the second verse came, completing the devices which the two verses contain, in the following manner:
a- Metonymy (al-kināya), which here is a metonymy of attribution (nisba) — its mention has preceded — and it lies in humiliation and wretchedness being imposed upon them as a house or a dome is pitched over its people, as Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī said:
إن في ثوبك الذي المجد فيه ... لضياء يزري بكل ضياء
(In your garment, in which glory resides, is a radiance that shames every radiance.)
b- The representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya), in likening holding to the means of safety to holding a firm rope let down from a high place, so that one is safe from the consequence of falling, of being forsaken and of crashing.
If we add to the devices mentioned what distinguishes the two verses of "beauty of versatility" (ḥusn al-iftitān), "beauty of arrangement", "splendour of expression" and "purity of eloquence", it becomes clear to you to what extent they reached the inimitability and loftiness by which the Mighty Book of Allah is distinguished.

* Benefits:
The scholars of Arabic differed over what brought in the bāʾ in the words of Allah the Exalted: «إلا بحبل من الله وحبل من الناس». One of the Kufan grammarians, at their head al-Farrāʾ in his book «Maʿānī al-Qur'an», said: what brought in the bāʾ in His words "بحبل" is a concealed verb whose mention was omitted, and the meaning of the speech is: "Humiliation was imposed upon them wherever they were found, except that they hold fast to a rope from Allah", so he concealed it in that. Al-Farrāʾ cited as evidence the words of Ḥumayd ibn Thawr al-Hilālī:
رأتني بحبليها فصدت مخافة ... وفي الحبل روعاء الفؤاد فروق
(She saw me with her two ropes and turned away in fear; and on the rope was one of startled heart, timid.)
He said: he meant "I came forward with her two ropes". And the words of Abū al-Ṭamaḥān al-Qaynī:
حنتني حانيات الدهر حتى ... كأني خاتل أدنو لصيد
قريب الخطو يحسب من رآني ... ولست مقيدا أني بقيد
(The bending blows of time have bent me until I am as one stalking, creeping towards game; short of step, whoever sees me reckons — though I am not fettered — that I am in a fetter.)
He means "fettered with a fetter". [Translator's note: what follows is al-Ṭabarī's assessment of al-Farrāʾ's view, though the author does not mark the transition.] So he made necessary the operation of an omitted verb and the overt appearance of its complement while it is left out, and that is weak in the doctrines of Arabic and remote from the speech of the Arabs.
Up to where he says: One of the Basran grammarians said: His words «إلا نحبل من الله» [Translator's note: so in the source, a misprint for «إلا بحبل من الله».] are an exception standing outside the beginning of the speech. Al-Farrāʾ said: that is no harder than His words «لا يسمعون فيها لغوا إلا سلاما». Others of the Kufan grammarians said: it is a connected exception, and the meaning is: humiliation was imposed upon them wherever they were found, i.e. in every place, except in the place of a rope from Allah, as you say: "Humiliation was imposed upon them in the places except in this place." This one too sought the truth but missed the joint. That is because he claimed that it is a connected exception; and had it been connected as he claimed, it would have been necessary that, when they are found with a rope from Allah and a rope from people, wretchedness not be imposed upon them. That is not the description of the Jews, because wherever they are found — with a rope from Allah and a rope from people, or without a rope from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and without a rope from people — humiliation is imposed upon them, according to what we mentioned earlier from the people of interpretation. So had His words "except with a rope from Allah and a rope from people" been a connected exception, it would have been necessary that, when the people are found with a covenant and protection, humiliation not be imposed upon them; and that is contrary to the description with which Allah described them, and contrary to the description which they have. Thereby the unsoundness of this speaker's view too has become clear.

Ibn Jarīr's comment:
Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī said: But the view according to us is that the bāʾ in His words "except with a rope from Allah" was brought in because the speech before the exception requires the bāʾ in meaning. That is because the meaning of His words "Humiliation was imposed upon them wherever they were found" is: "Humiliation was imposed upon them in every place in which they were found." Then He said: "except with a rope from Allah and a rope from people", not by way of connection with the first, but by way of disconnection from it, and its meaning is: "but they are found with a rope from Allah and a rope from people", as is said regarding:
«وما كان لمؤمن أن يقتل مؤمنا إلا خطأ»: «خطأ», even though it is accusative by what governed what precedes the exception, is not an exception connected with the first in the sense of "except by mistake, for then he may kill him so"; rather, he may kill him by mistake. Likewise His words "wherever they were found, except with a rope from Allah": even though what brought in the bāʾ after (إلا) is the verb before (إلا) that requires it, the exception is not an exception connected with what precedes it in the sense that when the people are met, humiliation departs from them; rather, humiliation is fixed in every state, and its meaning is what we explained just now.
The time has come for us to conclude this discussion, which has grown somewhat long, and we praise Allah that He inspired us with what He did not inspire anyone before. Perhaps, had their lives extended to our days, they would have grasped it as we have grasped it and plumbed its depth as we have plumbed it. Perhaps it is part of a good conclusion to draw attention to an error into which some of the earlier imams fell — and Exalted is He who is free of error. Someone lacking in learning claimed that what is conjoined to the apodosis of a condition by «ثم» may not be made jussive at all. He said: because what is conjoined to the apodosis is an apodosis, and the apodosis of a condition occurs after it and immediately following it, while «ثم» requires delay; so how could its occurrence immediately after the condition be conceived? Hence it was not made jussive with «ثم».
This is unsound and plainly false, and we need cite as proof of its falsity nothing but the words of Allah the Exalted: «وإن تتولوا يستبدل قوما غيركم ثم لا يكونوا أمثالكم»: «لا يكونوا» is a jussive imperfect, conjoined to «يستبدل», which occurs as the apodosis of the condition, and the conjunction is (ثم). With this the string of this discussion is complete, which we present to the Arab and Islamic worlds so that they may rejoice, for victory is coming, and the disappearance of this misshapen statelet is a promise with which the verses came down. We quote this expression of al-Zamakhsharī, for it is the best that can be said: «And since it is in the nominative, the negation of help is an unconditional promise, as if He said: "Then their affair and their story, about which I inform you and of which I give you glad tidings after the turning of backs, is that they are forsaken, help and strength being negated from them; they will not rise after it with any success, nor will any matter go right for them." And it was as He informed, regarding the state of Banū Qurayẓa, al-Naḍīr, Banū Qaynuqāʿ and the Jews of Khaybar.» And Allah is the One who grants success to what is correct.

dervis-irab:75-75.t:
* Vocabulary:
(دينار): the dīnār is a kind of ancient gold coin; the plural is danānīr. Its origin is dinnār, with two nūns; the succession of two like letters was felt heavy, so they replaced the first of them with a weak letter for lightness, because of its frequent circulation in use. What shows this is its return to the two nūns when it is given a broken plural or a diminutive, so they said: danānīr and dunaynīr.
(الْأُمِّيِّينَ): plural of ummī; what is meant here is one who is not of the People of the Book. It is well known that the Jews held the blood, property and honour of the Arabs to be lawful.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ): a resumptive clause, brought to begin explaining their treachery in property after explaining their treachery in religion. The wāw is resumptive, and من أهل الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). (مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطارٍ يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ): من is a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); you may also parse it as an indefinite qualified noun, i.e. "people", and it is a postponed mubtadaʾ. إن is conditional; تأمنه is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is "you"; بقنطار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تأمنه. يؤده is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤده. The conditional clause and its apodosis are either the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, if من is a relative, or its naʿt (adjective), in the position of a nominative, if من is an indefinite qualified noun. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينارٍ لا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ): conjoined to the previous clause; its i'rab preceded word for word. (إِلَّا ما دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قائِماً): إلا is a particle of restriction; ما دمت is an incomplete past verb, the tāʾ is its noun and قائما its khabar; عليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قائما». The exception is "emptied" (mufarragh) from the general adverb, so it is an adverb. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قالُوا): a resumptive clause, brought to explain their treating the property of the Arabs as lawful. The demonstrative is in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the bāʾ is a preposition; أنّ and what follows it are in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar; the clause قالوا is the khabar of أنّ. (لَيْسَ عَلَيْنا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ): the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl). ليس is an incomplete past verb; علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to something omitted, in the position of an accusative as the fronted khabar of ليس; في الأميين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); سبيل is the postponed noun of ليس. (وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ): the wāw is resumptive; يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقولون; الكذب is a mafʿūl bihi by way of taḍmīn (implied meaning), so that the meaning of يقولون is "they fabricate". It is better to parse it as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), that maṣdar being a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "the lying saying". (وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); هم is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يعلمون is the khabar.

* Benefits:
(ما دام) is one of the sisters of kāna, and the condition for it to operate is that it be preceded by the adverbial, maṣdar-forming «ما». So if you say: لا أكلمك ما دام زيد قاعدا ("I will not speak to you as long as Zayd is sitting"), what is meant is the time of the continuance of his sitting. The «ما» in your saying ما دام is necessary and cannot be dispensed with, and the verb with it can only be past. ما زال is not like that: another negative particle may take the place of «ما», and the verb with the negative may be past or imperfect, as in ما زال, لم يزل and لا يزال. The root meaning of «دام» is stillness and fixity; one says: دام الماء, i.e. the water became still, and دوّمت الشمس when the sun stands still in the middle of the sky.

dervis-irab:76-77.t:
* I'rab:
(بَلى مَنْ أَوْفى بِعَهْدِهِ وَاتَّقى): resumptive speech, brought as an affirmation of what they denied by their saying: "There is no way against us regarding the unlettered", i.e. the Arabs. بلى is a particle of answer and confirmation like نعم; it most often occurs after an interrogative and is specific to affirmation, and more about it will come in its place in this book. من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); أوفى is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); بعهده is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) أوفى, and اتقى is conjoined to أوفى. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ): the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); إنّ and its noun, and the clause يحب is its khabar (predicate); المتقين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause فإن الله etc. is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من». (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمانِهِمْ ثَمَناً قَلِيلًا): resumptive speech with no grammatical position, brought to show the lying of the Jews when they swore, or sold a commodity and swore that they had been offered such-and-such for it. إنّ and its noun, and the clause يشترون is the ṣila (relative clause); بعهد الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يشترون, and the bāʾ enters upon what is given up; أيمانهم is conjoined to بعهد الله; ثمنا is a mafʿūl bihi and قليلا a naʿt (adjective). (أُولئِكَ لا خَلاقَ لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; لا is the lā of generic negation and خلاق is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar; في الآخرة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause لا خلاق لهم is the khabar of أولئك, and the demonstrative clause with what follows is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ. (وَلا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ): the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; يكلمهم is an imperfect verb, nominative; the hāʾ is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and الله is the postponed fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to the clause لا خلاق لهم. (وَلا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ): also conjoined. (يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ): the adverb is attached to ينظر. (وَلا يُزَكِّيهِمْ): conjoined to «ولا ينظر إليهم». (وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; عذاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ and أليم a naʿt; the clause is also conjoined.

* Rhetoric:
1- The implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) in "buying": i.e. they take in exchange, for what they covenanted and for the oaths they swore, the goods of this world; by that He meant their distortion of the Torah and their alteration of what came in it.
2- The metonymy (kināya) in His saying «ولا يكلمهم ولا ينظر إليهم» for displeasure and intense anger. The meaning of «ولا يكلمهم الله» is: with what would please them; «ولا ينظر إليهم»: He will not incline to them with any good, out of Allah's loathing for them — as one says: "Look at me, may Allah look at you", meaning "incline to me, may Allah incline to you with good and mercy" — and as is said to a man: "May Allah not answer you." Nothing hidden is hidden from Allah, as in the saying of Shumayr ibn al-Ḥārith al-Ḍabbī:
دعوت الله حتى خفت أن لا ... يكون الله يسمع ما أقول
(I called upon Allah until I feared that Allah was not hearing what I say.)

dervis-irab:78-78.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ): they twist them and turn them from the correct to the counterfeit. One says: لويت عنقه, i.e. I twisted it. The maṣdar is al-layy and al-layyān, and the root meaning of al-layy is twisting and turning over, from the saying: "So-and-so twisted so-and-so's hand". From it is the saying of Farʿān ibn al-Aʿraf al-Saʿdī about his son Munāzil:
تخون مالي ظالما ولوى يدي ... لوى يده الله الذي هو غالبه
(He wronged me, embezzling my wealth, and twisted my hand — may Allah, Who overpowers him, twist his hand.)
This verse is from some beautiful verses, and before it:
جزت رحم بيني وبين منازل ... جزاء كما يستنزل الدّين طالبه
(May the bond of kinship between me and Munāzil repay him, as the creditor exacts the debt.)
وما كنت أخشى أن يكون منازل ... عدّوي وأدنى شانىء أنا راهبه
(I never feared that Munāzil would be my enemy, the nearest hater I dread.)
حملت على ظهري وفديت صاحبي ... صغيرا إلى أن أمكن الطّر شاربه
(I carried him on my back and ransomed my companion while small, until his moustache was ready for trimming.)
وأطعمته حتى إذا صار شيظما ... يكاد يساوي غارب الفحل غاربه
(And I fed him until, when he became tall and strong, his withers almost matched the withers of the stallion.)
تخون مالي ظالما ... the verse.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنَّ مِنْهُمْ لَفَرِيقاً يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ بِالْكِتابِ): resumptive speech, brought to describe a group of them — such as Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, Mālik ibn al-Ṣayf, Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab, Abū Yāsir and Shuʿba ibn ʿAmr the poet — who used to twist their tongues and mouth it, distorting what was in it of the description of the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ and other things. The wāw is resumptive; إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of إنّ; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and فريقا is the postponed noun of إنّ. The clause يلوون is a naʿt (adjective) of «فريقا»; the pronoun is plural in consideration of the meaning, because it is a collective noun like رهط and قوم. The wāw is the fāʿil (agent), ألسنتهم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and بالكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يلوون. (لِتَحْسَبُوهُ مِنَ الْكِتابِ): the lām is the lām of reason (taʿlīl); تحسبوه is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of reason, and the nūn was dropped because it is one of the five verbs; the hāʾ is the first object of تحسبوه, and من الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun in the place of the second object. The implied أن and what follows it are in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يلوون. (وَما هُوَ مِنَ الْكِتابِ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ما is the Ḥijāzī negative that operates like ليس; هو is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as its noun, and من الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar. (وَيَقُولُونَ: هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, conjoined to يلوون; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and من عند الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَما هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ): its i'rab preceded word for word. (وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ): conjoined to what preceded; يقولون is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقولون; الكذب is a mafʿūl bihi or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and its i'rab preceded shortly. (وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; هم is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the clause يعلمون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The simile (tashbīh) in His saying «لتحسبوه»: i.e. they bend their tongues with something resembling the Book, so that you would think that resemblance is from the Book.

dervis-irab:113-115.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الآناء): the hours. Its singular is أنى, with fatḥa on the hamza and the nūn, on the pattern of عصا; or إنى, with kasra on the hamza and fatḥa on the nūn, on the pattern of معى; or أني, with fatḥa on the hamza and sukūn on the nūn, on the pattern of ظبي; or إني, with kasra on the hamza and sukūn on the nūn, on the pattern of حمل.

* I'rab:
(لَيْسُوا سَواءً): a resumptive statement, brought to explain the disparity among the People of the Book. (ليس) with its noun and its khabar (predicate); the pause is complete at (سواء). (مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ أُمَّةٌ قائِمَةٌ): the clause is also resumptive, brought to explain what He had stated in summary, and to enumerate the virtues of the believers among the People of the Book, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, Thaʿlaba ibn Saʿīd, Usayd ibn ʿUbayd and their like among the Jews who embraced Islam. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar; (أمة) is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) and (قائمة) is a naʿt (adjective). Al-Farrāʾ chose that (أمة) be nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of (سواء), and I do not know how that held up for him, given the weakening of the clause's structure it involves. (يَتْلُونَ آياتِ اللَّهِ آناءَ اللَّيْلِ وَهُمْ يَسْجُدُونَ): the clause (يتلون) is a second naʿt of (أمة); the wāw is the fāʿil of (يتلون); (آيات الله) is its object; (آناء الليل) is an adverb of time attached to (يتلون). In (وهم), the wāw is for the ḥāl (circumstantial); (هم) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يسجدون) is in the position of the nominative as its khabar. (يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): the clause is a third naʿt of (أمة); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يؤمنون); (اليوم) is conjoined to (الله), and (الآخر) is a naʿt of (اليوم). (وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَيُسارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْراتِ): three clauses conjoined to the clause (يؤمنون بالله). (وَأُولئِكَ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of the demonstrative. (وَما يَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَنْ يُكْفَرُوهُ): the wāw is resumptive; (ما) is conditional, in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (يفعلوا); (يفعلوا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the preposition and its genitive noun (من خير) are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; the fāʾ is connective; (لن) is a particle of the accusative; (يكفروه) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (لن); the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) and the hāʾ is a second mafʿūl bihi. The verb (كفر) has taken two objects because it includes the meaning of depriving and withholding. The clause (فلن يكفروه) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالْمُتَّقِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (عليم) is its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (عليم).

dervis-irab:116-117.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصر), with kasra on the ṣād: the cold wind, like الصّرصر. Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī said:
أوقد فإن الليل ليل قرّ ... والريح يا غلام ريح صر
(Kindle the fire, for the night is a night of cold, and the wind, O lad, is a freezing wind.)
More about it will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً): a resumptive statement, brought to mention one of the traits of the Jews, namely their love of wealth, their greed for it and their enmity for its sake — though the particularity of the discourse conveys its generality, for the discourse being about Banū Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr does not prevent it from including everyone who makes his habit the love of wealth and the casting away of every fine trait for its sake. (إن) and its noun; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause); (لن) is a particle of the accusative; (تغني) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (لن); (عنهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تغني); (أموالهم) is the fāʿil (agent); (ولا أولادهم) is conjoined to «أموالهم»; (من الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of His word (شيئا) and was placed before it; (شيئا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause (لن تغني) is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of (إن). (وَأُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أولئك) is a demonstrative, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (أصحاب النار) is its khabar; the clause is conjoined to the clause (لن تغني). (هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): (هم) is a mubtadaʾ; (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to His word (خالدون); (خالدون) is the khabar of «هم»; and the clause is a second khabar of (أولئك). (مَثَلُ ما يُنْفِقُونَ فِي هذِهِ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) [Translator's note: the source text here is damaged, reading «َثَلُ ما يُنْفِقُونَ…»; the verse words are restored from the Qur'an.]: a resumptive clause, brought to strike a parable explaining the manner in which their wealth, on which they relied to repel the harms befalling them, avails them nothing. (مثل) is a mubtadaʾ; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (genitive construct); the clause (ينفقون) is the ṣila; (في هذه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ينفقون); (الحياة) is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative, and (الدنيا) is a naʿt of (الحياة). (كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ فِيها صِرٌّ) [Translator's note: damaged in the source as «َمَثَلِ رِيحٍ فِيها صِرٌّ»; restored from the Qur'an.]: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element in the position of the nominative as the khabar of (مثل); (ريح) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; [Translator's note: the source then reads only "a postponed mubtadaʾ", evidently omitting the word (صر) that it refers to.] a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is a naʿt of (ريح).
