(أَصابَتْ حَرْثَ قَوْمٍ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَأَهْلَكَتْهُ) [Translator's note: damaged in the source as «َ صابَتْ…»; restored from the Qur'an.]: the clause (أصابت) is a second naʿt of (ريح); (حرث قوم) is the mafʿūl bihi of (أصابت); the clause (ظلموا) is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of (قوم); (أنفسهم) is the mafʿūl bihi of (ظلموا); and (فأهلكته) is conjoined to (أصابت). (وَما ظَلَمَهُمُ اللَّهُ وَلكِنْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ) [Translator's note: damaged in the source as «َ ما ظَلَمَهُمُ…»; restored from the Qur'an.]: the wāw is resumptive; (ما) is negative; (ظلمهم الله) is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil; (لكن) is lightened from the heavy (لكنّ), inoperative, merely for rectification (istidrāk); (أنفسهم) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi of (يظلمون); and (يظلمون) is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representative simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): He, Glorified is He, likened what they spent, in its uselessness and how little it avails, to tillage struck by the freezing wind. The original form of the speech is: "The likeness of what they spend in this worldly life is like the likeness of the tillage of a people who wronged themselves, and a wind containing frost struck it." But the arrangement in the stated parable was altered for a great benefit, namely putting first what is more important, because the wind, which is the likeness of the punishment, is — in the context of threat and menace — more important to mention than the tillage. So it was placed first out of concern for its mention, relying on the fact that upright tastes and natures can return the speech to its original form in the easiest way.
The jurists have adduced this verse as evidence that the charity of disbelievers does not benefit those who give it, because belief is the foundation and upon it is the reliance. This is the loftiest that eloquence can reach.
2- Completion (al-tatmīm): its mention has preceded. It is that the speaker brings a word which, if dropped from the speech, would diminish its meaning in itself or in its attributes. The tatmīm here is in the phrase «فيها صر», for it conveyed hyperbole, just as it conveyed embodiment and personification — as you say: "a cold chill", "a night of nights", "a day of days". Then He restricted the frost by containment, because the wind is unrestricted; then He restricted it by containment, and everything restricted is a container of its unrestricted counterpart, because the unrestricted is part of the restricted; thus embodiment and personification were achieved. This is among the choicest rhetorical subtleties, so hold fast to it, and may Allah protect you.

dervis-irab:79-80.t:
* Vocabulary:
(البشر): the human being, male and female, singular and plural; it has no singular from its own form, like القوم and الخلق.
(رَبَّانِيِّينَ): al-rabbāniyyūn is the plural of rabbānī. There are several views about it, the best known and soundest being what Sībawayh mentioned. He said: rabbānī is a relative adjective (nisba) from al-rabb (the Lord), and the alif and nūn in it are added in the nisba to indicate intensiveness, like raqabānī, liḥyānī and shaʿrānī for one with a thick neck, a long beard and much hair; this addition is not used apart from the nisba. But when they form the nisba from al-raqaba, al-liḥya and al-shaʿr without intensiveness, they say: raqabī, liḥawī and shaʿrī. This is a significant point, which we see holding consistently in every nisba intended for intensiveness; so it is correct to say ʿilmānī as a nisba to al-ʿilm (knowledge).

* I'rab:
(ما كانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُ اللَّهُ الْكِتابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ): resumptive speech, brought to show the fabrication of the Jews against the prophets, following their fabrication against Allah. ما is negative and كان is an incomplete past verb; لبشر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). أن is a maṣdar-forming particle of the accusative, and يؤتيه is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by إن [Translator's note: so in the source, for أن]; the hāʾ is the first object. أن and what is within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the postponed noun of كان. الله is the fāʿil (agent) of يؤتيه, الكتاب is the second object, and الحكم and النبوة are conjoined. (ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ): ثم is a conjunction of delay, and the clause يقول is conjoined to يؤتيه; للناس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقول. (كُونُوا عِباداً لِي مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). كان and its noun, and عبادا is its khabar; لي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «عبادا»; من دون الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَلكِنْ كُونُوا رَبَّانِيِّينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لكن is lightened from the heavy form and inoperative; كونوا is an incomplete imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is its noun and ربانيين its khabar. The clause كونوا ربانيين is in the position of the object of an omitted saying, i.e. "but he says: be…".
(بِما كُنْتُمْ تُعَلِّمُونَ الْكِتابَ): the bāʾ is a preposition and ما is maṣdar-forming, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ربانيين because of the flavour of the verb in it. كان and its noun, and the clause تعلمون الكتاب is the khabar of كنتم; الكتاب is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَدْرُسُونَ): conjoined to «بما كنتم», and the clause تدرسون is the khabar of كنتم. (وَلا يَأْمُرَكُمْ أَنْ تَتَّخِذُوا الْمَلائِكَةَ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ أَرْباباً): the wāw is a conjunction and لا is added to emphasise the negation in His saying «ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه»; يأمركم is an imperfect verb conjoined to يؤتيه, i.e.: it is not for a human being that Allah should give him what was mentioned and then he should command people to worship himself, or to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Placing the rectification (istidrāk) between the conjoined and what it is conjoined to is for hastening to establish the truth. It was also read with يأمركم in the nominative, as resumption and the start of new speech. More detail of its i'rab will come in the Benefits section. أن تتخذوا: the wāw is a conjunction [Translator's note: so in the source; there is no wāw here, and أن is the maṣdar-forming particle]; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb, accusative by أن, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. The interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يأمر. الملائكة is the first object; النبيين is conjoined to الملائكة, accusative with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; أربابا is the second object. (أَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالْكُفْرِ بَعْدَ إِذْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ): resumptive speech addressing the believers by way of astonishment at the state of others. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; يأمركم is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil is "he", and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; بالكفر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأمركم; بعد is an adverb of time also attached to يأمركم; إذ is an adverb of time annexed to «بعد» — it has passed that only time-words are annexed to it, as in حينئذ and يومئذ. أنتم is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مسلمون its khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's annexation to it.

* Benefits:
1- The negation of "being" in His saying, Exalted is He, «ما كان لبشر» is meant as the negation of its predicate, as in: ما كان لك أن تفعل هذا ("it was not for you to do this"), where what is meant is negating the act, not negating the being. This holds consistently in two kinds:
a- A kind in which the negation is on rational grounds, like the verse just mentioned, because Allah does not give the Book to one who says such a hideous saying.
b- A kind in which the negation is by way of propriety and possibility, like the saying of Abū Bakr: "It was not for the son of Abū Quḥāfa to go forward and pray in front of the Messenger of Allah", i.e. it was not proper for him, nor within his power. The basis for distinguishing between them is taste and acquaintance with the context of the speech and its import.
2- If you conjoin His saying «ولا يأمركم» to «يؤتيه», then «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), emphasising the meaning of the preceding negation. If you conjoin it to «يقول», two readings are permissible in it:
a- Redundancy: the meaning is: it is not for a human being that Allah should appoint him to call to His worship and to abandoning rivals, and then he should command people to be servants to him and command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords.
b- That it is not redundant. Its rationale is that the Prophet ﷺ used to forbid Quraysh from worshipping the angels, and the People of the Book from worshipping ʿĪsā; so when they said to him: "Shall we take you as a lord?", it was said to them: it is not for a human being that Allah should make him a prophet and then he should command people to worship him and forbid them from worshipping the angels and the prophets. It was also said that it is conjoined to His saying «ثم يقول», the implied form being: "nor is it for him to say". It was also read in the nominative, as resumption and the start of new speech.

dervis-irab:81-81.t:
* Vocabulary:
Al-iṣr: what is meant by it here is the covenant. The covenant was called iṣr because it is among the things that are yuʾṣar, i.e. tied and fastened. Al-iṣr is anything with which something is fastened.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ النَّبِيِّينَ): resumptive speech, brought to treat the covenant which Allah the Exalted took from the prophets and their nations. The wāw is resumptive; إذ is an adverb for past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted اذكر ("remember"), and its like has passed. The clause أخذ is in the position of a genitive by annexation; الله is the fāʿil (agent), ميثاق the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and النبيين a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (لَما آتَيْتُكُمْ مِنْ كِتابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ): the lām with fatḥa is the lām that prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), because taking the covenant contains the meaning of making someone swear. It was also said: it is the lām of commencement (ibtidāʾ) with which the oath is met. ما is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause آتيتكم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; من كتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and حكمة is conjoined to كتاب. (ثُمَّ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِما مَعَكُمْ): ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; جاءكم is a past verb and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi; رسول is the postponed fāʿil, nominative, and مصدق a naʿt (adjective). لما: the lām is a preposition and ما is a relative noun in the position of a genitive by the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مصدق. معكم is an adverb of place attached to something omitted with no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of the relative. (لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ وَلَتَنْصُرُنَّهُ): the wāw [Translator's note: so in the source; the particle meant is the lām] occurs in the answer to an implied oath. تؤمننّ is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; the original is لتؤمنوننّ, and when two quiescent letters met the wāw was also dropped — it is the fāʿil — and the ḍamma remained as an indication of it. The doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis, with no grammatical position; به is attached to تؤمننّ. لتنصرنه is conjoined to لتؤمنن and is like it in i'rab: the dropped wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi. The implied oath clause and its answer are the khabar (predicate) of ما. (قالَ أَأَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَخَذْتُمْ عَلى ذلِكُمْ إِصْرِي): an explicative clause with no grammatical position. قال is a past verb and its fāʿil is "he"; the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr) and emphasis, because interrogation in its real sense is impossible in His case. أقررتم is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); أخذتم is conjoined to أقررتم; على ذلكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخذتم; إصري is the mafʿūl bihi, and the yāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of a genitive by annexation. (قالُوا أَقْرَرْنا): the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position, and the clause أقررنا is in the position of an accusative as the maqūl al-qawl. (قالَ فَاشْهَدُوا وَأَنَا مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ): the clause is resumptive, brought to record the testimony to their affirmation. قال is a past verb and the fāʿil is "he". فاشهدوا: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "eloquent" fāʾ); اشهدوا is an imperative verb, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position. وأنا: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive; أنا is a mubtadaʾ; معكم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl; من الشاهدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar. The clause أنا معكم is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl, or resumptive with no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
1- This verse has greatly occupied the parsers, and we shall present a summary of the most important things said about it, taking the way of brevity.

What Sībawayh says:
Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about His saying: «وإذا أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم» [Translator's note: so in the source, «وإذا» for «وإذ»], and he said: «ما» is in the sense of الذي (that which). Al-Naḥḥās said in his commentary on Sībawayh's Kitāb: the implied form in al-Khalīl's view is "that which I gave you (آتيتكموه)", then the hāʾ was dropped because of the length of the noun, and the lām is the lām of commencement. Al-Akhfash held this, and «ما» is then in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ. His saying ثم جاءكم and what follows is a clause conjoined to the ṣila, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "confirming it".

What al-Mubarrad, al-Zajjāj and al-Kisāʾī say:
ما is conditional, and the lām of verification has entered upon it as it enters upon إن; لتؤمننّ is the answer of the oath, which is the taking of the covenant, since it is equivalent to making someone swear, as you say: "I took your covenant that you will surely do such-and-such"; and it stands in place of the apodosis. Al-Kisāʾī said: the apodosis is in His saying فمن تولى.

Ibn Hishām replies to Abū al-Baqāʾ:
Ibn Hishām said, in replying to Abū al-Baqāʾ: «As for Abū al-Baqāʾ, he said about «لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة» [to the end of] the verse: for whoever reads the lām with fatḥa, there are two readings of «ما». First, that it is a relative, mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is either من كتاب, i.e. "that which I gave you of the Book", or لتؤمننّ به, the lām being the answer of the oath, because taking the covenant is an oath; جاءكم is conjoined to آتيتكم, and the original is ثم جاءكم به, so the pronoun returning to ما was omitted; and the original is مصدق له, then the overt noun took the place of the pronoun; or the returning pronoun is the pronoun of استقر to which «مع» is attached. Second, that it is conditional, the lām preparatory (muwaṭṭiʾa), and the position of ما is accusative by آتيت, the second object being the pronoun of the addressee, and «من كتاب» is like «من آية» in «ما ننسخ من آية». There are several points in this:
a- His permitting من كتاب to be the khabar involves predicating about the relative before its ṣila is complete, because «ثم جاءكم» is conjoined to the ṣila.
b- His permitting لتؤمننّ to be the khabar while taking it as the answer to the taking of the covenant entails that it has a [grammatical] position, inasmuch as he made it a khabar, and that it has no position, inasmuch as it is the answer to the oath; and this is a contradiction. His due was to take it as the answer to an omitted oath and to take the two clauses [together] as the khabar. It may be said: what he meant by his saying "the lām is the answer of the oath because taking the covenant is an oath" is that taking the covenant indicates an implied oath clause, and the sum of the two clauses [is the khabar]; he only called «لتؤمننّ» the khabar because it is what indicates what is primarily intended, since it alone is the khabar in reality; and that there is no implied oath, but rather [Translator's note: the source repeats «بل»] «أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين» is the oath clause. It may be said [in reply]: had he meant this, he would not have restricted the indication to what he mentioned, given the agreement that the presence of an imperfect beginning with a lām with fatḥa and ending with an emphatic nūn is a decisive indication of an oath, even if taking the covenant or the like is not mentioned with it.
c- His permitting the returning pronoun to be the pronoun of استقر entails a singular pronoun returning to two things at once, for it returns to the relative.
d- He permitted the omission of the genitive returning pronoun although the relative is not genitive. If it is said: he was content with the second word به, so that it is like his saying:
لو أنّ ما عالجت لين فؤادها ... فقسا استلين به للان الجندل
(Had what I used to soften her heart — and it only hardened — been used to soften the solid rock, the rock would have softened.)
we say: on this reading he permitted the mentioned «به» to return to «the Messenger», not to «ما».
e- He called the pronoun of آتيتكم a second object, whereas it is the first object.»
2- The lām that prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam): it is the one that enters upon a condition. It is called muwaṭṭiʾa (preparatory) because it prepares what follows to be suitable as the answer to both the condition and the oath, so that the apodosis of the condition is then omitted because the answer of the oath indicates it.

dervis-irab:118-118.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِطانَةً): a man's biṭāna, with kasra on the bāʾ, and his walīja, is the one whom he acquaints with his secrets, trusting him and relying on his affection. It is likened to the lining (biṭāna) of a garment, which is the opposite of its outer face. In Mukhtār al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «A man's walīja is his intimate circle and his biṭāna». From it is the poet's saying:
وهم خلصائي كلهم وبطانتي ... وهم عيبتي من دون كل قريب
(They are all my sincere friends and my intimates; they are the keepers of my secrets, rather than any kinsman.)
(يَأْلُونَكُمْ): from ألا في الأمر, i.e. he fell short in the matter. It takes two objects because it includes the meaning of withholding; one says: لا آلوك نصحا, i.e. "I will not withhold advice from you". It has also been said: it is intransitive and does not take an object in the accusative. That will come in detail in the section on parsing.
(خَبالًا): al-khabāl, with fatḥa on the khāʾ, is corruption. Its origin is the illness and languor that afflict an animal, leaving it corrupted and disturbed. One says خبله with the light form and خبّله with the doubled form, so he is خابل and مخبّل; and so-and-so is mad and مخبّل.
(عَنِتُّمْ): al-ʿanat, with fatḥa on the ʿayn and the nūn: severe harm and hardship.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا بِطانَةً مِنْ دُونِكُمْ): a resumptive statement, brought to warn the believers against befriending the Jews, because of the ties of kinship and friendship between them; but its unrestricted sense is intended, for befriending the sinful colonizer is not permitted at all. The parsing of the vocative has preceded. (لا) is prohibitive; (تتخذوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بطانة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (من دونكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (بطانة), i.e. "being from other than you", or "from other than the members of your own kind". It may also be attached to (تتخذوا), so that the preposition and its genitive noun are in the place of the second mafʿūl bihi of (تتخذوا); on the first view, the second object of (تتخذوا) is omitted for concision, its implied form being "intimates" or "allies". (لا يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبالًا): the clause is resumptive, as though serving as an explanation of the state of the disbelieving, hostile intimate circle; it has also been said: it is a second naʿt of (بطانة). (لا) is negative; (يألونكم) is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi, and (خبالا) is the second mafʿūl bihi. If we say the verb is intransitive, then the kāf is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "they do not fall short for you", and (خبالا) is also accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in corruption"; you may also make it accusative as a tamyīz (specification), or as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَدُّوا ما عَنِتُّمْ): the clause is resumptive like the one before it; it has also been said: it is a third naʿt of (بطانة), and both are sound. (ودوا) is a verb and its fāʿil; (ما) is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what falls within its scope as a maṣdar which is the mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "they wished your hardship, your harm and the misfortune of your trust". (قَدْ بَدَتِ الْبَغْضاءُ مِنْ أَفْواهِهِمْ): the clause is also resumptive, or it is a fourth naʿt of (بطانة). (قد) is a particle of realization; (بدت) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif which was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (البغضاء) is the fāʿil; (من أفواههم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (بدت), while Abū al-Baqāʾ attached them to an omitted element in the accusative as a ḥāl. The meaning of hatred appearing from their mouths is that they utter what betrays the hatred rooted in their natures and traits. [Translator's note: the source has «ينسبون», which appears to be a misprint for «ينبسون» ("they utter"); translated accordingly.] (وَما تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ أَكْبَرُ): the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive, so the clause is a ḥāl clause or resumptive; (ما) is a relative noun, the mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (تخفي) is the ṣila (relative clause); (صدورهم) is the fāʿil of (تخفي); and (أكبر) is the khabar (predicate) of «ما». (قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ الْآياتِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ): the clause is resumptive, conveying a reason, brought to establish that the successive signs deserve to bring you to befriend the friends of Allah and to be hostile to His enemies. (قد) is a particle of realization; (بينا) is a past verb and its fāʿil; (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (بينا); (الآيات) is the mafʿūl bihi; (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is the noun of (كنتم); the clause (تعقلون) is the khabar of (كنتم); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being "then never show them affection".

* Rhetoric:
1- The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya) in His word (بطانة), for it is originally the well-known lining of a garment; then it was borrowed for a man's intimate and close friend, to whom he discloses his inner self and the stirrings of his breast.
2- Al-infiṣāl: it is that the speaker says something which gives the impression of being known and obvious, but it contains a matter beyond that, of more distant aim and loftier reach. That is in His words «من أفواههم», for it is known that a man expresses what he conceals with his mouth; the infiṣāl in that is the recording against them that they cannot restrain words from escaping their tongues which betray the feeling of hatred and resentment.
3- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq) between (بدت) and (تخفي).

* Benefits:
The scholars of grammar and rhetoric differed over the parsing of the clauses occurring after (بطانة). We have allowed that they be resumptive, by way of giving the reason for the prohibition of taking them as intimates from outside your kind and the members of your people. Al-Zamakhsharī went along with this, saying: «The better and more eloquent is that they be resumptive, and it is permissible that they be successive adjectives.» Al-Wāḥidī rejected this view because of the absence of a conjunction, and claimed that one does not say: "Do not take a companion who harms you, who loves parting from you." Yet it appears to me that the naʿt may be multiple without a conjunction, just as the khabar may be multiple, as in «الرحمن، علم القرآن، خلق الإنسان، علمه البيان».

Between Ibn Hishām and al-Rāzī:
Ibn Hishām followed up Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī regarding this verse, saying, in his own words: «Imam Fakhr al-Dīn made a slip in the exegesis of this verse, for he asked: What is the wisdom in placing «من دونكم» before «بطانة»? And he answered that the focus of the prohibition is «من دونكم», not «بطانة», and that is why the more important was placed first. But the recitation is not as he stated.»

Abū Ḥayyān erred, and al-Ṣafāqusī and al-Ḥalabī followed him:
Ibn Hishām continued in his follow-up, saying: The like of this is that Abū Ḥayyān, in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ, explained the word «زبرا» after the words of Allah the Exalted «وَتَقَطَّعُوا أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ», whereas it is only in Sūrat al-Muʾminūn, and he left explaining it there; and two men who summarised a parsing from his exegesis followed him in this slip.
I say: by the two men who shared Abū Ḥayyān's slip, Ibn Hishām meant al-Ṣafāqusī and Shihāb al-Dīn al-Ḥalabī, known as al-Samīn.

dervis-irab:119-119.t:
* Vocabulary:
(العض): the pressing of the teeth against one another; and عضه بأسنانه: he seized it with his teeth. One says عضضت, with kasra on the ḍād, أعض, عضا and عضيضا. Al-ʿaḍḍ is always with ḍād, except with "time" or the like, in their saying عظ الزمان, i.e. it became severe, and عظت الحرب, i.e. the war became severe, for in these the two letters interchange. The ʿayn and the ḍād, when they are the first and second radicals of a word, have a strange particular property: they convey the meaning of severity and harm and what falls within their meaning. Al-Akhṭal said:
ضجوا من الحرب إذ عضت غواربهم ... وقيس عيلان من أخلاقها الضجر
(They cried out against war when it bit their withers; and Qays ʿAylān — complaint is among its traits.)
Al-ʿaḍb is reviling and cutting, and the severity and harm in both are not hidden; سيف عضب is a cutting sword; شاة عضباء is a ewe with a broken horn; عضده: he strengthened his back and helped him, and the believer is معضود (supported) by Allah's granting of success — Allah the Exalted said: «سنشد عضدك بأخيك»; داء معضل is a difficult illness that cannot be resolved, and he has a مرض عضال (an incurable disease) which has defeated the physicians and baffled them (أعضلهم); and أعضل الأمر (the matter became intractable). Dhū al-Iṣbaʿ married, then came to his clan asking them for her dowry, and they refused him, so he said:
واحدة أعضلكم أمرها ... فكيف لو درت على أربع
(One woman's affair has baffled you — so how would it be had I gone round to four?)
And so-and-so is a ʿuḍla of the ʿuḍal, i.e. a calamity among calamities. This is among the most wondrous things one hears about this noble language.
(الْأَنامِلَ): plural of أنملة, which is the tip of the finger.

* I'rab:
(ها أَنْتُمْ أُولاءِ تُحِبُّونَهُمْ وَلا يُحِبُّونَكُمْ): a resumptive clause, brought to alert the believers to their error in befriending the Jews. (ها) is for alerting and rebuke; (أنتم) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (أولاء) is its khabar (predicate). It has preceded that the demonstrative must be mentioned because of the presence of «ها», which is for alerting. The clause (تحبونهم) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, or resumptive, as though serving as an explanation of their error and their poor choice of intimates; and the clause (ولا يحبونكم) is conjoined to the clause (تحبونهم). Al-Jalāl and others parsed (أولاء) as one addressed in the vocative, i.e. "O these", so that the clause (تحبونهم) is the khabar. (وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْكِتابِ كُلِّهِ): it is sound for the wāw to be a conjunction, so that the clause is conjoined to the clause (تحبونهم), and it is sound for the wāw to be circumstantial, so that the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (بالكتاب) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (تؤمنون), and (كله) is tawkīd (emphasis) of (الكتاب). In this is the utmost censure of them, because showing pure friendship to one who does not love you is a matter that calls for blame and censure. Abū Ḥayyān, however, rejected the wāw being circumstantial, because when an affirmative imperfect occurs as a ḥāl, the circumstantial wāw does not enter upon it: you say "جاء زيد يضحك" ("Zayd came laughing"), and "ويضحك" is not permissible. He concluded by saying: but the preferable is what we mentioned, that it is for conjunction. (وَإِذا لَقُوكُمْ قالُوا آمَنَّا): the wāw is resumptive; (إذا) is an adverb for the future time including the meaning of condition; the clause (لقوكم) is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (genitive construct); the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and the clause (آمنا) is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَإِذا خَلَوْا عَضُّوا عَلَيْكُمُ الْأَنامِلَ مِنَ الْغَيْظِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb for the future time; the clause (خلوا) is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa; (خلا) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif which was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil (agent); the clause (عضوا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (عضوا); (الأنامل) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (من الغيظ) is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as a tamyīz (specification), i.e. "in rage". It may also have the meaning of the lām, conveying the reason, so that the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "because of rage". (قُلْ مُوتُوا بِغَيْظِكُمْ): the clause is resumptive; the clause (موتوا) is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying; and (بغيظكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "bound up with your rage" [Translator's note: the source reads «يغيظكم», a misprint for «بغيظكم».]. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): the clause is resumptive, conveying the reason for the command to die; the easier view is that it is part of what is said, so that it is in the position of the accusative by the verb of saying. (إن) with its noun and its khabar; (بذات الصدور) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (عليم). The meaning of (ذات الصدور) is the things concealed and the stirrings of souls; (ذات) is the feminine of (ذي), meaning "the possessor of the breasts", and they were made "possessor of the breasts" because they never part from them.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse is the device of metonymy (al-kināya), and biting the fingertips is a metonymy for an attribute. It was the custom of the Arabs to express one who is enraged and regretful over what he has done by biting the fingertips and fingers, and their poems overflow with this expression. Abū Ṭālib said:
وقد صالحوا قوما علينا أشحة ... يعضون عضا خلفنا بالأباهم
(They have made peace with a people grudging towards us, who bite hard behind our backs upon their thumbs.)
2- And in the verse the imperative departs from its literal meaning to the meaning of an imprecation against them, that their rage may be perpetual.

* Benefits:
The Kufans held that demonstratives, when "approximation" (taqrīb) is intended by them, are among the sisters of kāna in needing a nominative noun and an accusative khabar, as in: "How should I fear injustice when this caliph is arriving (قادما)?" and "How should I fear the cold when this sun is rising (طالعة)?"; and likewise everything in which the noun occurring after the demonstrative has no second in existence, as in: "This is Ibn Ṣayyād, the most generous of people in giving drink" (أسقى الناس). So they parse "هذا" of approximation as a defective noun, the nominative as the noun of approximation and the accusative as the khabar of approximation. It is a logical view, and therefore we have presented it for information.

dervis-irab:82-83.t:
* I'rab:
(فَمَنْ تَوَلَّى بَعْدَ ذلِكَ): resumptive speech to answer the People of the Book who brought their dispute to the Prophet ﷺ. The fāʾ is resumptive; من is conditional, in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); تولى is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); بعد is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) تولى, and ذلك is a demonstrative in the position of a genitive by annexation. (فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ): the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); أولئك is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and الفاسقون is the khabar (predicate); or «هم الفاسقون» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is the khabar of أولئك. The two clauses of the protasis and its apodosis are in the position of a nominative as the khabar of «من».
(أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, and it has entered upon the fāʾ, which conjoins a clause to a clause. The meaning is: "Those are the defiantly disobedient; so is it other than the religion of Allah they seek?", then the hamza was placed between them. It is also permissible for it to be conjoined to something omitted, implied as: "Do they turn away, and so seek other than the religion of Allah?" Reference has preceded to [Translator's note: the source text appears to be incomplete here] — يبغون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعاً وَكَرْهاً): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أسلم; أسلم is a past verb, and the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). من is a relative noun, the fāʿil of أسلم; في السموات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to something omitted with no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause); الأرض is conjoined to السموات. طوعا and كرها are two maṣdars (verbal nouns), accusative as ḥāl, in the sense of "willing or unwilling", or as two mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute objects) of two omitted verbs; the first is preferable. (وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; إليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يرجعون. يرجعون was read with tāʾ and with yāʾ; it is an imperfect verb in the passive, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

dervis-irab:84-84.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَسْباطِ): plural of sibṭ, with kasra on the sīn, which is the child of one's child. It is mostly applied to a daughter's child, as opposed to ḥafīd, which is a son's child. The asbāṭ among the Jews correspond to the tribe (qabīla) among the Arabs.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ): resumptive speech, brought to ask the Prophet ﷺ to say, he and his Companions: "We believe in Allah". That is why the pronoun is singular in His saying «قل» and plural in His saying «آمنا». قل is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is "you"; آمنا is a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause آمنا is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) آمنا. (وَما أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنا): the wāw is a conjunction; ما is a relative noun conjoined to الله, and the clause أنزل علينا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. (وَما أُنْزِلَ عَلى إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْباطِ): the wāw is a conjunction and ما is a noun conjoined to the first ما; أنزل is a past verb in the passive, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as "it" (هو); the clause أنزل is the ṣila; على إبراهيم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل, and the names that follow are conjoined to إبراهيم. (وَما أُوتِيَ مُوسى وَعِيسى وَالنَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): conjoined to what preceded. أوتي is a past verb in the passive, موسى is the nāʾib fāʿil, and what follows it is conjoined to it; من ربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوتي. (لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ): لا is negative; نفرق is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun implied as "we" (نحن); بين is an adverb of place attached to نفرق; أحد is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أحد; the clause is circumstantial (a ḥāl). (وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; نحن is a mubtadaʾ (subject); له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «مسلمون»; مسلمون is the khabar (predicate) of نحن; the clause is either accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or resumptive with no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:85-89.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الْإِسْلامِ دِيناً فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ): resumptive speech, brought to begin speaking about the apostates who joined the disbelievers. They were twelve men who apostatised, left Medina and came to Mecca as disbelievers, among them al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd al-Anṣārī. The wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); يبتغ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as "he" (هو). غير: we have two readings for it: either it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يبتغ and دينا is a tamyīz (specification), or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of دينا and was then fronted before it; on this reading دينا is the mafʿūl bihi. فلن: the fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and لن is a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; يقبل is an imperfect verb in the passive, accusative (manṣūb) by لن; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يقبل. The clause لن يقبل منه is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of من. (وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ): the wāw is for conjunction; هو is a mubtadaʾ; في الآخرة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to الخاسرين; من الخاسرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of هو; the clause is conjoined to the apodosis. It is possible that the wāw is resumptive and the clause resumptive, serving as information about his state in the Hereafter. (كَيْفَ يَهْدِي اللَّهُ قَوْماً كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِيمانِهِمْ): resumptive speech, brought to speak about the apostates just mentioned. It was also said that it was revealed concerning the Jews, or that both these and those are meant. كيف is an interrogative noun whose meaning is denial and negation, i.e. "Allah does not guide", and it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl. يهدي is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ; الله is the fāʿil and قوما the mafʿūl bihi; the clause كفروا is a naʿt of قوما; بعد is an adverb of time attached to كفروا, and إيمانهم is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَشَهِدُوا أَنَّ الرَّسُولَ حَقٌّ): this conjunction is one of the subtleties, since it is not correct to conjoin it to كفروا, as appears at first glance, because the meaning would be corrupted. The more correct view is that it is conjoined to the verbal meaning in «إيمانهم», because its meaning is "after they believed in Allah"; so it is of the type "conjunction by assumed construction" (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-tawahhum).
It may also be said that the wāw does not require sequence, so it is conjoined to كفروا. It is also permissible for the wāw to be circumstantial (ḥāliyya) with «قد» implied after it, i.e. "having borne witness"; the first is sounder in meaning and further from weakness. أنّ with its noun and khabar — it and what is within its scope are in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "that the Messenger is true", so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to شهدوا. (وَجاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّناتُ): the wāw is a conjunction; جاءهم is a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and البينات is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to the clause شهدوا. It is permissible for the wāw to be circumstantial with قد implied, i.e. "having borne witness" [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause in question here is جاءهم البينات], so the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يهدي is the khabar; القوم is the mafʿūl bihi and الظالمين a naʿt of القوم. (أُولئِكَ جَزاؤُهُمْ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ): the clause is resumptive, brought to explain their recompense and their fate. أولئك is a demonstrative in the position of a nominative as a first mubtadaʾ; جزاؤهم is a second mubtadaʾ; أنّ and what is within its scope are the khabar of جزاؤهم, and the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of أنّ, and لعنة الله is the postponed noun of أنّ. (وَالْمَلائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; الملائكة is conjoined to الله, and الناس is also conjoined; أجمعين is a tawkīd (emphasis), genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. (خالِدِينَ فِيها): خالدين is a ḥāl, and فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خالدين. (لا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذابُ): the clause is a second ḥāl. لا is negative; يخفف is an imperfect verb in the passive; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخفف, and العذاب is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَلا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; هم is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ; ينظرون, i.e. "they are granted respite", is an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of «هم», and the clause is conjoined to the clause لا يخفف. (إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا): إلا is a particle of exception and الذين is the excepted; the clause تابوا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. (مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تابوا; ذلك is a demonstrative in the position of a genitive by annexation. (وَأَصْلَحُوا): the clause is conjoined to the clause تابوا. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "eloquent" fāʾ); إنّ and its noun, غفور its first khabar and رحيم its second khabar. Further, there is disagreement about the i'rab of the clause of exception [Translator's note: the discussion that follows concerns the clauses خالدين فيها / لا يخفف عنهم العذاب, as the reasoning shows]: most parsers parse it as an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila), i.e. a ḥāl from a ḥāl, because خالدين is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «عليهم»; others parsed it as a resumptive clause, and as such it is brought to explain their eternal stay in the Fire. It is worth mentioning that the one who repented was al-Ḥārith ibn Suwayd ibn al-Ṣāmit al-Anṣārī, when he regretted his apostasy and sent to his people, the Anṣār, saying: "Ask whether there is any repentance for me." His brother al-Julās sent him the verse, so he came to Medina and repented, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted his repentance [Translator's note: the source has «نوبته», a misprint for توبته].

dervis-irab:120-120.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ): a resumptive statement, brought to explain the extremity of their enmity and their versatility in the kinds of enmity. (إن) is conditional; (تمسسكم) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm); the kāf is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (حسنة) is a postponed fāʿil (agent); (تسؤهم) is the jussive apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَإِنْ تُصِبْكُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَفْرَحُوا بِها): a clause conjoined to the preceding clause, identical to it in parsing. (وَإِنْ تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا لا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئاً): the clause is also conjoined. (إن) is conditional; (تصبروا) is the protasis, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (تتقوا) is conjoined to (تصبروا); (لا) is negative; and (يضركم) is the apodosis. It was given the ḍamma to follow the ḍamma of the ḍād, as is the rule for the doubled verb, which has preceded. It may also be given the fatḥa because of its lightness, as in a second reading; and there is a third reading, namely يضركم with kasra on the ḍād and sukūn on the rāʾ, from ضاره يضيره, i.e. "harms him". The kāf is the mafʿūl bihi, (كيدهم) is the fāʿil, and (شيئا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "anything of harm". (إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ): a resumptive clause conveying a reason. (إن) and its noun; (محيط) is its khabar (predicate); (بما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (محيط); and the clause (يعملون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse is a beautiful implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya): touching (المس) was borrowed for the good thing, though it does not touch a person, to indicate that it is less firmly established than "striking" (الإصابة), as a hint that the disbelievers are aggrieved by whatever good befalls the believers, even if it merely presents itself to them or passes them by incidentally. But when the evil takes hold of you and overwhelms you, do not ask about the extent of their joy and delight. This is among the marvels of speech before which necks are cut short [i.e. which none can attain].

dervis-irab:121-122.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غَدَوْتَ): al-ghuduww is going out at the beginning of the day; one says غدا يغدو, i.e. he went out in the early morning. (غدا) is also used in the sense of (صار) "became", in which case it is defective, putting the noun in the nominative and the khabar (predicate) in the accusative. Likewise راح, عاد, رجع, آض, ارتد, قعد, تحول and استحال, all of which mean "became" and are joined to it in their operation. Labīd said:
وما المرء إلا كالشهاب وضوئه ... يحور رمادا بعد إذ هو ساطع
(Man is but like the meteor and its light: it turns to ashes after it was shining.)
So (يحور) here is defective, meaning "becomes"; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to (المرء), and (رمادا) is its khabar. In the noble ḥadīth: «If you relied upon Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out (تغدو) hungry in the morning and return full in the evening», i.e. they go in the morning hungry and return in the evening having eaten their fill, their bellies full. In the verse, however, it admits both meanings, as will come. (تُبَوِّئُ): you settle [them in place].

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ غَدَوْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ تُبَوِّئُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَقاعِدَ لِلْقِتالِ): the wāw is resumptive, or conjoining to something implied. In either case the clause is brought so that the Prophet ﷺ may remind his Companions of the day of Uḥud, so that they would remember what happened on that day in these exceptional circumstances of lack of patience, and how the Prophet went out early to Uḥud from the chamber of ʿĀʾisha, as will come in the section on benefits. The adverb is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, i.e. "remember". The clause (غدوت) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's iḍāfa (genitive construct) to it. The tāʾ is either the fāʿil (agent) of (غدوت) or its noun, in the view of those who make it operate like (صار). The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (غدوت) on the first view, and to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) on the second. The clause (تبوئ) is a ḥāl from the fāʿil of (غدوت) on the first view, or the khabar of (غدوت). (المؤمنين) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (تبوئ), and (مقاعد) is the second mafʿūl bihi of (تبوئ); (للقتال) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (مقاعد), i.e. "positions prepared for fighting". (وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and (سميع عليم) are its two predicates. (إِذْ هَمَّتْ طائِفَتانِ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ تَفْشَلا): (إذ) is an adverb for past time, a badal (substitute) of the first (إذ), i.e. "remember that time", which is the day of Uḥud. The clause (همت) is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa; (طائفتان) is the fāʿil of (همت); (منكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of His word (طائفتان); (أن) is a maṣdar-forming particle of the accusative; (تفشلا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (أن), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; and the alif of the dual is the fāʿil. (أن) and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (همت), because it is made transitive by the bāʾ; the implied form is "بأن تفشلا". You have two views of its position: the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the genitive. (وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّهُما): as for the wāw, you may make it circumstantial, so that the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, or you may make it resumptive. (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and (وليهما) the khabar. (وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (على الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتوكل); the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it entered for the meaning of condition, the meaning being "when the matter becomes grave and difficult, then rely"; and (المؤمنون) is the fāʿil.

dervis-irab:123-125.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بدر): the name of a watering place between Mecca and Medina. This water belonged to a man named Badr, and it was named after him. By it took place the battle bearing this name, on the seventeenth of the month of Ramaḍān, in the second year of the Hijra.
(فَوْرِهِمْ): al-fawr is haste and speed. It is a maṣdar from فارت القدر, when the pot boils; it was borrowed for speed, and then the state in which there is no delay, no slowness and no turning aside to anything was named by it.
(مُسَوِّمِينَ): marked with a clear mark. It has been read in the form of the active participle and in the form of the passive participle.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realization; (نصركم الله) is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a postponed fāʿil (agent); and (ببدر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (نصركم). The clause is resumptive, brought to console the believers for the harm that befell them in the battle of Uḥud, to remind them of Allah's favour, and to point out that their defeat at Uḥud was because of disobeying the Prophet regarding steadfastness and standing firm, that sweetness may be overtaken by bitterness, and that the Gardens are surrounded by hardships. (وَأَنْتُمْ أَذِلَّةٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; (أنتم) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (أذلة) is the khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa; (اتقوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) is the mafʿūl bihi; (لعل) and its noun, and the clause (تشكرون) is its khabar; and the clause of hope is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (إِذْ تَقُولُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): (إذ) is an adverb for past time, attached to (نصركم), or a badal (substitute) of the first «إذ», because the discourse here concerns the battle of Uḥud. The clause (تقول) is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (genitive construct), and (للمؤمنين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تقول). (أَلَنْ يَكْفِيَكُمْ أَنْ يُمِدَّكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ): the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl) of the Prophet ﷺ. The hamza is for rhetorical, disapproving interrogation, as though they were like those despairing of victory. (لن) is a particle of the accusative; (يكفيكم) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (لن); the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (أن) is a maṣdar-forming particle of the accusative; (يمدكم) is an imperfect verb, accusative by it; (أن) and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the fāʿil of (يكفيكم); and (ربكم) is the fāʿil of (يمدكم). (بِثَلاثَةِ آلافٍ مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ مُنْزَلِينَ): (بثلاثة): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يمدكم); (آلاف) is a muḍāf ilayhi; (من الملائكة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (ثلاثة آلاف); and (منزلين) is a second naʿt. (بَلى إِنْ تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا وَيَأْتُوكُمْ مِنْ فَوْرِهِمْ هذا): (بلى) is a particle of answer, affirming the negation in His words (ألن يكفيكم); the meaning is: the reinforcement with angels suffices you, but that is conditional on conditions that must be fulfilled, namely patience and piety. (إن) is conditional; (تصبروا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (تتقوا) is conjoined to (تصبروا), and (يأتوكم) is also conjoined; (من فورهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يأتوكم); and (هذا) is a demonstrative in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of (فوركم) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Qur'anic word is (فورهم).] or a badal from it. The whole clause is resumptive, brought to specify the conditions of the reinforcement. (يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِخَمْسَةِ آلافٍ مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ): (يمددكم) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi and (ربكم) is the fāʿil; (من الملائكة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of (خمسة آلاف); and (مسومين) is a second naʿt.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymy (al-kināya) in the words of Allah the Exalted «وأنتم أذلة», for the weakness of their condition and the smallness of their number and equipment: history records that they set out with groups of them taking turns on a single camel, and they had only one horse on the day of Badr.

dervis-irab:126-127.t:
* Vocabulary:
(طَرَفاً): by it He meant a side, or a group of them.
(يَكْبِتَهُمْ): He disgraces them and enrages them; from al-kabt, which is being struck with something hateful. It has also been said: it is throwing down on the face and the hands. On these two meanings the tāʾ is original, not a substitute for anything; rather, it is an independent root in itself. It has also been said that the tāʾ is a substitute for the dāl, its origin being كبده, when he struck him with something hateful that caused pain in his liver (كبد), as you say رأسته when you strike his head (رأس). This is indicated by the reading of some: أو يكبدهم, with the dāl. The Arabs sometimes substitute the tāʾ for the dāl, and perhaps Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī glimpsed this substitution and so matched two words in a remarkable matching when he said:
لأكبت حاسدا وأري عدوا ... كأنهما وداعك والرحيل
(So that I may crush an envier and sicken an enemy's insides — as though they were your farewell and the departure.)
Abū al-Ṭayyib noticed the substitution of the tāʾ for the dāl and took it as "لأكبد", and it suited him to bring "أري" from al-warī, which is the striking of the lung. One says: وراه الحب ريا وتورية, which is corruption of the inner body from grief or passionate longing. ʿAbd Banī al-Ḥasḥās said:
وراهن ربي مثلما قد ورنيني ... وأحمي على أكبادهن المكاويا
(May my Lord sicken their insides as they have sickened mine, and may I heat the branding irons upon their livers.)
From it is the noble ḥadīth: «That the inside of one of you be filled with pus until it corrupts it (يريه)…». This is among the rare feats of Abū al-Ṭayyib that cannot be matched.

* I'rab:
(وَما جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرى لَكُمْ): a resumptive statement, brought to explain the manner of the victory. The wāw is resumptive; (ما) is negative; (جعله الله) is a past verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a postponed fāʿil (agent); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (بشرى) is a second mafʿūl bihi if (الجعل) here has the meaning of "making into". You may also consider (الجعل) here as meaning "creating", so that it is transitive to one object, and (بشرى) is accusative as excepted from the most general of reasons, so it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), having fulfilled the conditions for the accusative; and (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (بشرى). (وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُكُمْ بِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is causal; (تطمئن) is an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن) after the lām of cause; and the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative, conjoined to (بشرى), and made genitive by the lām because one of the conditions of the accusative is lacking, namely identity of the agent: the agent of the "making" is Allah the Exalted, while the agent of the reassurance is the hearts. You may also attach the preposition and its genitive noun to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He did this so that your hearts may be reassured". (قلوبكم) is the fāʿil of (تطمئن), and (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تطمئن). (وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ): the wāw is resumptive; (ما) is negative; (النصر) is the mubtadaʾ (subject); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (من عند الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); and (العزيز الحكيم) are two adjectives of Allah the Exalted. (لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفاً مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): the lām is causal; (يقطع) is an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن) after the lām; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (نصركم) in His words «ولقد نصركم الله ببدر». It has also been said: to an omitted verb, its implied form being "He reinforced you and gave you victory". Abū Ḥayyān preferred that they be attached to the nearest thing mentioned, which is what governs His words «من عند الله», as though the implied form were: "Victory is only from Allah, not from anyone else, for one of two things: either cutting off a portion of the disbelievers by killing and capture, or by disgrace and turning back in failure." (طرفا) is the mafʿūl bihi; (من الذين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt; and the clause (كفروا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (أَوْ يَكْبِتَهُمْ فَيَنْقَلِبُوا خائِبِينَ): (أو) is a conjunction; (يكبتهم) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (يقطع); the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the fāʾ is a conjunction; (ينقلبوا) is conjoined to (يكبتهم) [Translator's note: the source misprints it as «بنقلبوا».]; and (خائبين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.

* Rhetoric:
The explicit, dependent metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-tabaʿiyya) in His words «ليقطع طرفا»: those of them who were killed and scattered are likened to a thing cut off, whose parts are scattered and whose order is disrupted.

dervis-irab:128-129.t:
* I'rab:
(لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ): a resumptive statement, brought to make the matter light for the Prophet ﷺ after what befell him in the battle of Uḥud. (ليس) is a defective past verb; (لك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (ليس); (من الأمر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and (شيء) is the postponed noun of (ليس). (أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ): (أو) is a conjunction; (يتوب) is an imperfect verb conjoined to a noun free of being construed as a verb, so it is accusative by a concealed (أن) after the conjunction, which is (أو) — this will come in the section on benefits; and (عليهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتوب). (أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ): conjoined to (يتوب). (فَإِنَّهُمْ ظالِمُونَ): the fāʾ is causal; (إن) with its noun and its khabar; and the causal clause has no grammatical position because it is in the status of a resumptive clause. (وَلِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ): the wāw is resumptive; (لله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (في السموات) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element which has no position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); and (ما في الأرض) is conjoined to (ما في السموات). (يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ): the verbal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl because it occurs after a definite noun. (لمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يغفر); (يشاء) is a nominative imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) being "هو", and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun; the clause (يعذب من يشاء) is conjoined to it, and (من) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; (غفور) is its first khabar and (رحيم) its second khabar.

* Benefits:
The imperfect verb is put in the accusative by an optionally concealed (أن) after a conjunction preceded by a noun free of being construed as a verb. The conjunctions specific to this are four: the wāw, the fāʾ, (أو) and (ثم). Of this is the saying of Maysūn bint Baḥdal:
ولبس عباءة وتقر عيني ... أحب إلي من لبس الشفوف
(Wearing a cloak with my eye content is dearer to me than wearing sheer fabrics.)
It is also permissible that «أو» have the meaning of «إلى» ("until"), so that the verb is accusative by an obligatorily concealed (أن) after (أو).

dervis-irab:130-132.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَأْكُلُوا الرِّبَوا أَضْعافاً مُضاعَفَةً): a resumptive statement, brought to prohibit usury (al-ribā) and to intensify the warning to the believers. Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: These are the most fearsome verses of the Qur'an, since Allah threatened the believers with the Fire prepared for the disbelievers. (لا) is prohibitive; (تأكلوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive (لا), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الربا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أضعافا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) and (مضاعفة) is a naʿt (adjective). The naʿt came to negate the paucity which the plural of paucity, on the pattern أفعال, expresses. It has also been said: the naʿt indicates the repetition of the doubling year after year. The hyperbole in this expression conveys rebuke. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (اتقوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) is its object; (لعل) and its noun, and the clause (تفلحون) is its khabar (predicate); and the clause of hope is a ḥāl. (وَاتَّقُوا النَّارَ الَّتِي أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكافِرِينَ): (اتقوا) is conjoined to what precedes; (النار) is the mafʿūl bihi; (التي) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as a naʿt; the clause (أعدت) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and (للكافرين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (أعدت). (وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أطيعوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) is the mafʿūl bihi and (الرسول) is conjoined to (الله); (لعل) and its noun; (ترحمون) is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of (لعل), and the clause of hope is a ḥāl.

dervis-irab:90-91.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِيمانِهِمْ): resumptive speech, brought to speak about the Jews who disbelieved in ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, and the Gospel after their belief in Mūsā and the Torah, then increased in disbelief by disbelieving in Muḥammad ﷺ and the Qur'an; it was also said that it is general. إنّ and its noun, and the clause كفروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; بعد is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) كفروا, and إيمانهم is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (ثُمَّ ازْدادُوا كُفْراً): ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; ازدادوا is a past verb, and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of a nominative as the fāʿil (agent); كفروا [Translator's note: so in the source, for كفرا] is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the fāʿil, i.e. "their disbelief increased". زاد is transitive to two objects, and its reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) is transitive to one only. (لَنْ تُقْبَلَ تَوْبَتُهُمْ): لن is an accusative particle; تقبل is an imperfect verb in the passive, accusative (manṣūb) by لن, and توبتهم is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. (وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الضَّالُّونَ): the wāw is a conjunction, or resumptive so that we do not need anything implied to conjoin a nominal clause to a verbal clause. It was also said that it is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), the meaning being: their repentance from sins will not be accepted while they are astray. أولئك is a demonstrative; هم is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as a second mubtadaʾ (subject), الضالون is the khabar of «هم», and the nominal clause is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the demonstrative; or «هم» is a detached pronoun with no grammatical position and الضالون is the khabar of أولئك. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَماتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ): a resumptive clause, brought to emphasise what preceded. إنّ and its noun; the clause كفروا is the ṣila of the relative, and ماتوا is conjoined to كفروا. وهم: the wāw is circumstantial, هم is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ and كفار the khabar; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمْ مِلْءُ الْأَرْضِ ذَهَباً): the fāʾ connects the answer because of the flavour of condition in the relative. The fāʾ entered here and did not enter in His saying «لن تقبل منهم» [Translator's note: so in the source; the earlier wording is «لن تقبل توبتهم»] because the fāʾ signals deservingness by the preceding description; here He said «وماتوا وهم كفار», and there He did not state this restriction explicitly. لن is an accusative particle; يقبل is an imperfect verb in the passive, accusative by لن, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ; من أحدهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقبل; ملء is the nāʾib fāʿil and الأرض a muḍāf ilayhi; ذهبا is a tamyīz. There has been disagreement about what puts it in the accusative, a disagreement that led al-Kisāʾī to prefer its being accusative by removal of the preposition, and perhaps that is preferable. (وَلَوِ افْتَدى بِهِ): the wāw conjoins to something omitted, and its ruling will come in the Benefits section; لو is a non-jussive conditional particle; افتدى is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied on the alif, and its fāʿil is "he"; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to افتدى. (أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the clause as a whole is a second khabar of إنّ. أولئك is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; عذاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative; أليم is a naʿt (adjective). (وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and ناصرين is genitive by من in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ.

* Benefits:
1- Conjunction by assumed construction (al-ʿaṭf ʿalā al-tawahhum): the majority of grammarians made conjunction by assumed construction a regular pattern. It is that you suppose the matter to run according to the basic form and conjoin to it, as in the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā:
بدا لي أني لست مدرك ما مضى ... ولا سابق شيئا إذا كان جائيا
(It has become clear to me that I cannot overtake what has passed, nor get ahead of anything when it is coming.)
conjoining سابق on the supposition of a redundant bāʾ in the khabar of ليس, i.e. لست بمدرك ولا سابق. And the saying of another:
مشائيم ليسوا مصلحين عشيرة ... ولا ناعب إلا ببين غرابها
(Ill-omened, they do not set a clan right, and their raven croaks only of separation.)
i.e. ليسوا بمصلحين ولا ناعب.
2- The grammarians of Basra claimed that الذهب is accusative because ملء is occupied with الأرض and الذهب comes after them both, so its accusative became like the accusative of the ḥāl. That is because the ḥāl comes after a verb that has been occupied with its fāʿil, so it is put in the accusative, just as the object that comes after the fāʿil is put in the accusative, [the verb] having been occupied with its fāʿil. They said: the like of His saying ملء الأرض ذهبا, as regards the accusative of ذهب, in ordinary speech is: لي مثلك رجلا ("I have your like as a man"), meaning "I have your like among men". They claimed that رجل is accusative because the annexation is occupied with the noun, so it is put in the accusative just as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is put in the accusative because the verb is occupied with the fāʿil.
3- A group of exegetes found difficulty in His saying, Exalted is He, «فلن تقبل توبتهم», given that repentance is accepted, as in the first verse and as in His saying, Exalted is He, «وهو الذي يقبل التوبة عن عباده», and elsewhere. So it was said: their repentance will not be accepted at death. Al-Naḥḥās said: this is a good view, as the Exalted said: «وليست التوبة للذين يعملون السيئات حتى إذا حضر أحدهم الموت قال: إني تبت الآن». It was also said: it is better to take the non-acceptance of repentance in this verse as referring to one who died a disbeliever without repenting, so it is as if death in disbelief was expressed by the non-acceptance of repentance; or [it refers to those who] repented in the Hereafter on seeing [Translator's note: the source has «معانية», a misprint for معاينة] the punishment, as is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: «ولو ترى إذ المجرمون ناكسو رءوسهم عند ربهم ربنا أبصرنا» etc., and by His saying, Exalted is He: «فلم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم لما رأوا بأسنا».
4- The wāw accompanying a condition calls for another condition to which the condition joined with the wāw is conjoined, and the usual practice in such a case is that what is stated draws attention to what is left unsaid by way of a fortiori. An example is your saying: أكرم فلانا ولو أساء ("Honour so-and-so even if he does wrong"). This wāw conjoins what is mentioned to something omitted, implied as: "Honour so-and-so if he does good and if he does wrong"; except that by making it obligatory to honour him if he does wrong, you drew attention to the fact that honouring him if he does good is all the more so. Ransoming oneself with the earth's fill of gold is worthy of acceptance; so if it is not accepted [Translator's note: the source has «يقل», a misprint for يقبل], then a fortiori ransom with less than that will not be accepted. This is among the subtle points and secrets of our language, which stop at no limit.

dervis-irab:92-94.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حِلًّا): al-ḥill, with kasra on the ḥāʾ, is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ḥalla; one says: حلّ الشيء حلالًا وحِلًّا ("the thing became lawful"). Masculine and feminine, singular and plural are the same when it is used as a description.

* I'rab:
(لَنْ تَنالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ): resumptive speech, brought to explain what benefits the believers and is accepted from them, following the explanation of what does not benefit the disbelievers and is not accepted from them. لن is a particle of negation, the accusative and the future; تنالوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of a nominative as the fāʿil (agent), and البر is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). حتى is a particle of limit and genitive; تنفقوا is an imperfect verb, accusative by an obligatorily implied أن after حتى, and the wāw is the fāʿil; مما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنفقوا; the clause تحبون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative «ما». Know that this verse came out metrical without intention, so it is not counted as poetry, because poetry according to the prosodists is what is versified intentionally. This verse is a complete line of the shortened (majzūʾ) ramal metre, and it comes in the following form:
لن تنالوا البرّ حتى ... تنفقوا مما تحبّون
Many verses that are metrical without the intention of poetry will come later.
(وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; ما is a jussive conditional noun in the position of an accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of تنفقوا; تنفقوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), and the wāw is the fāʿil; من شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تنفقوا. فإن: the fāʾ connects [what is] in place of the omitted apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), serving as its reason, and it has taken its place; the implied form is: "He will recompense you according to it and its amount, for He knows everything". إنّ and its noun, and عليم is its khabar (predicate); به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عليم. (كُلُّ الطَّعامِ كانَ حِلًّا لِبَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): resumptive speech, brought to refute the Jews' conjectures when they said to the Prophet ﷺ: "You claim that you are on the religion of Ibrāhīm, and Ibrāhīm did not eat the flesh of camels or their milk, while you eat and drink that; so you are not on his religion." كل is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause كان حلا is its khabar; كان is a past verb, its noun is "it" (هو) and حلا is its khabar; لبني إسرائيل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to His saying «حلا»; إسرائيل is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the fatḥa because it is a diptote, what prevents it [from full declension] being its being a proper name and foreign. (إِلَّا ما حَرَّمَ إِسْرائِيلُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ): إلا is a particle of exception; ما is a relative noun in the position of an accusative by exception from the latent noun of كان; the clause حرم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative; إسرائيل is the fāʿil, and على نفسه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حرم. What is meant by Isrāʾīl is Yaʿqūb. The clause of exception is circumstantial (a ḥāl). (مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تُنَزَّلَ التَّوْراةُ): the parsers differed about what من قبل is attached to; the apparent view is that it is attached to «حلا», as suits the meaning. أن and what is within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar annexed to قبل, and التوراة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِالتَّوْراةِ فَاتْلُوها إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): the clause is resumptive, brought to cut off their way of answering. The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "eloquent" fāʾ), because it discloses an implied condition, i.e. "if you are confident of your claims and insist on them, then bring the Torah". ائتوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; بالتوراة is attached to ائتوا; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). فاتلوها: the fāʾ is a conjunction; اتلوها is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of an accusative as the mafʿūl bihi. إن is conditional; كنتم is an incomplete past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, the tāʾ is its noun and صادقين its khabar; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by «فأتوا بالتوراة». (فَمَنِ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ): a resumptive clause, brought to describe the fabricators as wrongdoers. The fāʾ is resumptive; من is a non-jussive [Translator's note: so in the source, though it then parses the verb as jussive in position] conditional noun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ; افترى is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to «من»; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to افترى, and الكذب is the mafʿūl bihi. (مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to افترى or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ): the fāʾ connects the apodosis; أولئك is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ; هم is a second mubtadaʾ and الظالمون the khabar of «هم», and the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative; or هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) and الظالمون is the khabar of أولئك. The demonstrative clause and what follows it are in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من».

dervis-irab:133-134.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْكاظِمِينَ): active participle from كظم الغيظ (restraining rage), which is that one folds in upon oneself and holds back what is within it, holding fast to patience. Its origin is from كظم القربة, when one fills the waterskin and stops up its mouth so that what is in it does not spill out.

* I'rab:
(وَسارِعُوا إِلى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (سارعوا) is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (إلى مغفرة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (سارعوا); and (من ربكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (مغفرة). (وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّماواتُ وَالْأَرْضُ): (جنة) is conjoined to (مغفرة); (عرضها) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (السموات) is the khabar (predicate); (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات); and the nominal clause is a naʿt of (جنة). (أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ): the verbal clause is also a naʿt of (جنة); (أعدت) is a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is "هي"; and (للمتقين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أعدت). (الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ فِي السَّرَّاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ): the relative noun is a naʿt of (المتقين); the clause (ينفقون) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (في السراء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ينفقون); and (الضراء) is conjoined to (السراء).
