(وَالْكاظِمِينَ الْغَيْظَ وَالْعافِينَ عَنِ النَّاسِ): conjoined to (المتقين); (الغيظ) is the object of the active participle (الكاظمين); (العافين) is also conjoined; and (عن الناس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (العافين). (وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; (يحب) is an imperfect verb and (المحسنين) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
This verse comprises a device of great worth, namely pointed selection in simile (al-tankīt fī al-tashbīh). Its definition is that the speaker purposely mentions one thing rather than something else that could take its place, for the sake of a subtle point; and when it occurs in a simile it reaches the utmost. Here it is in the words of Allah the Exalted: «عرضها السموات والأرض». He intended to describe it as vast, so He singled out its width for mention rather than its length. He departed from mentioning the length only because what is settled in first impressions [Translator's note: the source has «البداءة», apparently for «البداهة», "intuition".] and in minds is that length is the stronger indication of vastness; so if its width is such as to contain the heavens and the earth, what then do you think of its length!

dervis-irab:135-136.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ إِذا فَعَلُوا فاحِشَةً): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; (الذين) is conjoined to (المتقين), i.e. "it has been prepared for the pious, for those who spend and for those who repent". It is also permissible that «الذين» be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is «أولئك», as will come. (إذا) is an adverb of the future; the clause (فعلوا) is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (genitive construct); and (فاحشة) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أَوْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ ذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ): (أو) is a conjunction; (ظلموا) is conjoined to (فعلوا); (أنفسهم) is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause (ذكروا الله) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا لِذُنُوبِهِمْ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (استغفروا) is conjoined to (ذكروا), i.e. they repented of them; and (لذنوبهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (استغفروا). (وَمَنْ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ): the wāw is resumptive; (من) is interrogative, and the meaning of the interrogative here is negation; it is in the position of the nominative as the mubtadaʾ; the clause (يغفر) is the khabar; (الذنوب) is the mafʿūl bihi; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (الله) is a badal (substitute) of the pronoun in (يغفر), i.e. of the latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent). (وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا عَلى ما فَعَلُوا وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ): conjoined to (استغفروا). (لم) is a jussive particle; (يصروا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; (على ما فعلوا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يصروا), and the clause (فعلوا) is the ṣila (relative clause). (وهم): the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يعلمون) is the khabar; and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of (يصروا). (أُولئِكَ جَزاؤُهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): (أولئك) is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (جزاؤهم) is a second mubtadaʾ and (مغفرة) is the khabar of (جزاؤهم); the second mubtadaʾ and its khabar are the khabar of the demonstrative. If we parse (الذين) as a mubtadaʾ, the clause is the khabar of the relative noun. (من ربهم) is a naʿt (adjective) of (مغفرة). (وَجَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها): (جنات) is conjoined to (مغفرة); the clause (تجري من تحتها الأنهار) is a naʿt of (جنات); (خالدين) is a ḥāl; and (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خالدين). (وَنِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعامِلِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (نعم) is an inflexible past verb for expressing praise; (أجر العاملين) is the fāʿil of (نعم), being annexed to a noun bearing the article (ال); and the one specified for praise is omitted, its implied form being "نعم أجر العاملين ذلك" ("excellent is the reward of the workers — that"), meaning forgiveness in the Gardens.

dervis-irab:137-138.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سُنَنٌ): ways; plural of sunna, which is the way and the custom. The meaning of their having خلت is their having passed. The origin of al-khuluww in the language is being alone: the empty (khālī) place is the one devoid of those in it. It is also used of time in the sense of passing, because what has passed is separated from existence and devoid of it; and likewise الأمم الخالية, i.e. the past nations.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ سُنَنٌ): a resumptive statement, brought to console the believers for the grief and dejection that befell them, and as a continuation of the details of the rest of the story of Uḥud; for no one attains good until he pays its dowry with sacrifice, patience and struggle. (قد) is a particle of realization; (خلت) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (من قبلكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (خلت); and (سنن) is the fāʿil (agent). (فَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, which is the one that occurs as the answer to an implied condition because the meaning follows from it, i.e. "if you are in doubt, then travel in the land so as to take heed from what you see of the traces of their destruction". (سيروا) is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (سيروا); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of an implied non-jussive condition. (فَانْظُروا كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (انظروا) is conjoined to (سيروا); (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as the fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); (كان عاقبة) is (كان) and its noun; (المكذبين) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the interrogative clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of (انظروا). (هذا بَيانٌ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدىً وَمَوْعِظَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ): a resumptive statement. Al-bayān here is the indication that serves to remove the doubt that has arisen. (هذا) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (بيان) is its khabar; (للناس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (بيان); (هدى) is conjoined to (بيان), and likewise (موعظة), which is a conjoining of the particular to the general; and (للمتقين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (موعظة) or to an omitted naʿt of it.

* Rhetoric:
The trope (al-majāz) in His words «فسيروا في الأرض»; the relation in this trope is what travelling in the land leads to: contemplating the traces on display and bringing to light the remains left by the ancients, from which insight should be drawn. Abū al-Ṭayyib glimpsed the heights of this lofty trope when he said:
تتخلف الآثار عن أصحابها ... حينا ويدركها الفناء فتتبع
(The traces outlast their owners for a while; then extinction overtakes them, and they follow.)
Then he asked:
أين الذي الهرمان من بنيانه؟ ... ما قومه؟ ما يومه؟ ما المصرع
(Where is he whose building the two Pyramids are? What was his people? What was his day? What was his downfall?)

dervis-irab:95-97.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بكة): a dialectal form of مكة (Makka). Makka was so called because it has little water; the Arabs say: ملك الفصيل ضرع أمه وأمكه [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended verb is مكّ] when the young camel sucks out the milk in its mother's udder. In al-Qāmūs there is what indicates that it was so called because it tamukku sins, i.e. effaces and removes them. As for Bakka, it was so called because it tabukku the necks of tyrants, i.e. humbles and destroys them. It was also said: from بكّه, when he crowded him; it was so called because of the crowding of people in it. The poet said:
إذا الشريب أخذته الاكه ... فخله حتى يبك بكه
(When the one who shares your watering is seized by the heat, leave him until he crowds in his crowding.)
Further, they mentioned many names for Makka, among them: Makka, Bakka, al-Bayt al-ʿAtīq, al-Bayt al-Ḥarām, al-Balad al-Amīn, al-Maʾmūn, Umm Raḥīm, Umm al-Qurā, Ṣalāḥ, al-ʿArsh, al-Qādis — because it purifies from sins — al-Muqaddasa, al-Nāssa with nūn and also with bāʾ (al-Bāssa), al-Ḥāṭima, al-Raʾs, Kawthāʾ, al-Balda, al-Binya and al-Kaʿba.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: صَدَقَ اللَّهُ فَاتَّبِعُوا مِلَّةَ إِبْراهِيمَ حَنِيفاً): resumptive speech, brought to allude to their lying, i.e. it is established that Allah is truthful in what He sent down and you are the liars. قل is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as "you" (أنت); صدق الله is a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). فاتبعوا: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "eloquent" fāʾ), i.e. "if you want salvation, after that has been established for you in the most complete way, then follow". اتبعوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn because its imperfect is one of the five verbs; the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of a nominative as the fāʿil; ملة is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), إبراهيم a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and حنيفا a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَما كانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ما is negative; كان is an incomplete past verb, its noun is a latent pronoun implied as "he" (هو), referring to Ibrāhīm, and من المشركين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of كان. (إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ لِلنَّاسِ لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ): resumptive speech, brought to indicate that the first mosque set up for mankind is al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, then Bayt al-Maqdis, and that the first to build it was Ibrāhīm, peace be upon him. إنّ and its noun; بيت is a muḍāf ilayhi; وضع is a past verb in the passive, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun implied as "it" (هو); للناس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to وضع, and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of بيت. للذي: the lām with fatḥa is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and الذي is a relative noun in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ; ببكة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to something omitted with no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. (مُبارَكاً وَهُدىً لِلْعالَمِينَ): مباركا is a ḥāl from the relative noun, or from the pronoun latent in what the preposition and genitive noun are attached to; هدى is conjoined to مباركا; للعالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to هدى, i.e. "guiding them". (فِيهِ آياتٌ بَيِّناتٌ مَقامُ إِبْراهِيمَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted in the position of a nominative as a fronted khabar; آيات is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) and بينات a naʿt of آيات; the clause is resumptive, explaining its blessing and guidance. مقام is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "among them is the Station of Ibrāhīm", or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ implied as "one of them", i.e. one of those clear signs is the Station of Ibrāhīm; the clause is resumptive.
You will see in the Benefits section an entertaining discussion, but what we have presented is preferable. (وَمَنْ دَخَلَهُ كانَ آمِناً): the wāw is resumptive; من is jussive conditional, in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and it may also be a relative. دخله is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʿil is "he", and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition, and its i'rab has preceded. كان is an incomplete past verb in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), its noun is "he" and آمنا is the khabar of كان. The protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of the conditional or relative من. (وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ مَنِ اسْتَطاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to make the Ḥajj obligatory. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; على الناس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to what the khabar — which is «لله» — is attached to; حج is a postponed mubtadaʾ and البيت a muḍāf ilayhi. من is a relative noun in the position of a genitive as a badal (substitute) from الناس — a substitute of part for whole, or of inclusion (ishtimāl) — the pronoun being omitted, i.e. "of them". Some parsed it as the fāʿil of «حج», and there is room for objection in this, the delightful details of which will come to you in the Benefits section. The clause استطاع is the ṣila of the relative; إليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt of سبيلا, and when it was fronted before it, it was parsed as a ḥāl. (وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ, or a relative noun; كفر is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, and its fāʿil is "he". The fāʾ gives the reason for the implied apodosis, i.e. "he will not harm Allah, for Allah is free of need of him". In any case, the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative, and [Translator's note: the source text is compressed here; the intended sense is: if من is a relative, the clause كفر is its ṣila; if conditional,] the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar. إنّ is a particle resembling the verb, الله is its noun and غني its khabar; عن العالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to غني.

* Benefits:
1- The grammarians have a long discussion in which disagreement flared among them, and the exegetes followed them, so they wandered in every valley until the intended meaning almost escaped them. Had they inclined towards ease, they would have chosen the reading we chose, and so given relief and found relief. But they plunged into discussion and exploited their strong grammatical capacities, and in their debates they produced what is delightful and enchanting. We shall present to you here a summary of those debates, as a historical record of the clash of opinions and a witness to the objectivity of thought.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: مقام is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) from آيات. The grammarians answered him, saying: this breaks the consensus of the grammarians, who established that an indefinite is not explained by a definite, and a sound feminine plural is not explained by a masculine singular. They said: nor is it permissible for it to be a badal from آيات, because they stated explicitly that when the substituted-for is multiple and the badal does not fulfil the number, cutting off (qaṭʿ) is obligatory. The supporters of al-Zamakhsharī answered them that he — i.e. al-Zamakhsharī — was a mujtahid, so he did not mind contradicting the consensus.

And Ibn Jinnī permitted breaking the consensus:
Ibn Jinnī said: it is permissible to break the consensus in the literary disciplines.

What Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī says:
Al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī said in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī, verbatim:
«His saying: "a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted", i.e. one of the readings of «مقام». Al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī said: and it is the preferred one. Al-Zamakhsharī said it is an ʿaṭf bayān, and he was answered that «آيات» is indefinite and «مقام إبراهيم» is definite, and disagreement [in definiteness] is not permissible in ʿaṭf bayān by the consensus of the Basrans and the Kufans. Al-Ṣafāqusī said: it is possible that al-Zamakhsharī used the term ʿaṭf bayān and meant by it the badal, as a group do, loosely. Likewise Ibn Hishām said in al-Mughnī: he may have expressed the badal by ʿaṭf bayān because of their kinship. This is supported by his saying concerning «أسكنوهن من حيث سكنتم من وجدكم» that «من وجدكم» is an ʿaṭf bayān of His saying «حيث سكنتم». And here is Sībawayh, the imam of the craft, calling the tawkīd (emphasis) a ṣifa (adjective).» We have only quoted this discussion — and it is a drop from an ocean — for enjoyment and exercise of the mind; parsing «مقام» as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, has spared us all this lengthiness.

2- The second debate, on «من استطاع»:
What we adopted — parsing «من» as a badal from «الناس» — is the preferred view. Some grammarians said: «من» is the fāʿil of حج, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that operates like its verb, and the maṣdar is annexed to its object. The grammarians answered this by [saying that it would mean] it is obligatory upon people that the capable among them perform the Ḥajj, and that is false. Al-Tāj al-Subkī answered on behalf of Ibn al-Sīd [Translator's note: so in the source], saying: there is nothing to prevent there being two things in the Ḥajj: a collective obligation (farḍ kifāya) upon all people that the capable among them perform the Ḥajj — so that if he does not perform it, all creatures are in sin — and an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn) upon the capable one. There is no need for all this artificiality and back-and-forth; that is [avoided] by parsing «من» as a badal from الناس. So reflect, and Allah will guide you.
Further, al-Kisāʾī parsed «من» as conditional, in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with its apodosis omitted, the implied form being: "whoever is able, let him perform the Ḥajj", or "it is upon him to undertake the Ḥajj in person".

[Continuation of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān]

dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الم): discussion of the openings of the surahs has preceded at the beginning of al-Baqara.
(التوراة والإنجيل): two foreign nouns; it is also said they are Arabic. On the view that they are Arabic, التوراة is derived from their saying ورى الزّند, when the fire-stick is struck and fire appears from it. Since the Torah contains light by which one comes out of misguidance into guidance, as one comes out by light from darkness into light, this book was called التوراة.
It is also said that it is derived from وريت في كلامي, from التورية (allusion), and it was called التوراة because it contains hints, intimations and indirect expressions. As for الإنجيل, on the view of those who hold it is Arabic, it is derived from النجل, which is widening; of this is their saying عين نجلاء, i.e. a wide eye. The Gospel was so named because it contains a widening (relaxation) that was not in the Torah.

* I'rab:
(الم) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); this has been discussed in detail before. (اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (إله) is its noun; (إلا) is an instrument of restriction; and (هو) is a badal (substitute) from the position of (لا) and its noun, according to the correct view, or from the omitted khabar [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «الخير» for «الخبر»], i.e. "there is no god existing except He"; and the clause is the khabar of «الله». The i'rab of the testimony of faith (kalimat al-shahāda) has been discussed in detail before. (الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ): a second and third khabar of «الله», or two khabars of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting". (نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ بِالْحَقِّ): the clause is a fourth khabar of «الله», or a second khabar if we make (الحي القيوم) two khabars of an omitted mubtadaʾ. (نزل) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; (عليك) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نزل); (الكتاب) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (بالحق) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الكتاب), i.e. "invested with the truth". (مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ): (مصدقا) is an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida); the lām is a preposition; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to His word (مصدقا); (بين) is an adverb of place attached to an omitted [verb that is the] ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (يديه) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive with the yāʾ because it is a dual, the nūn having been dropped because of the construct; and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. (وَأَنْزَلَ التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ) is conjoined to what precedes. (مِنْ قَبْلُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنزل). (هُدىً لِلنَّاسِ): a ḥāl from (التوراة) and (الإنجيل); it was not put in the dual because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "guiding".
(هدى) may also be parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "He sent down these two books for the guidance of people". (للناس) is attached to (هدى) [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «يهدى» for «بهدى»]. (وَأَنْزَلَ الْفُرْقانَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause (أنزل الفرقان) is conjoined to the clause (أنزل التوراة والإنجيل),
as a case of conjoining the general to the particular, i.e. the books that distinguish (tafruq) between truth and falsehood. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ) is a resumptive clause, to speak about the delegation of Najrān; the details are set out at length in the extensive works. (إن) and its noun; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; and (بآيات الله) is attached to (كفروا). (لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (عذاب) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; (شديد) is an adjective; and the nominal clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar of (إن). (وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقامٍ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; (عزيز) is the first khabar and (ذو انتقام) the second khabar. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَخْفى عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي السَّماءِ): (إن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يخفى عليه شيء) is its khabar; (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted adjective of (شيء); and (ولا في السماء) is conjoined to what precedes. (هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحامِ) is also a resumptive clause, brought to set out His knowledge, Glorified is He, and His awareness of what does not come under [visible] existence, namely the shaping of His servants in the wombs of their mothers. (هو) is the mubtadaʾ and (الذي) its khabar; the clause (يصوركم) is the ṣila of the relative noun; and (في الأرحام) is attached to (يصوركم). (كَيْفَ يَشاءُ): (كيف) here is a conditional instrument in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and it does not make the verb jussive because «ما» is not attached to it. The object of (يشاء) is omitted, its implied form being "your shaping"; and the clause is circumstantial. (لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): its i'rab has preceded; He repeated it to emphasise the statement. (الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): two khabars of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "He".

* Rhetoric:
1- Figurative usage (majāz) in His words «لما بين يديه», what is meant being "what is before it".
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq) between «الأرض» and «السماء».
3- Concision by omission (ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf): the object of «يشاء» has been omitted, for the sake of wonder and to show the power of Allah the Exalted.

dervis-irab:139-141.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَهِنُوا): you weaken. Its origin is توهنوا; the wāw was dropped because originally it occurred between a yāʾ and a kasra, since the verb وهن has fatḥa in the past and kasra in the imperfect.
(القرح): with fatḥa on the qāf, and also with ḍamma. It has been said: with fatḥa it is the wounds, and with ḍamma their pain; it has been read with both.
(نُداوِلُها): We turn them about among people, giving the turn now to these and now to those. One says: دالت له الدول (fortunes turned in his favour), دالت الأيام (the days alternated), and أدال الله بني فلان من عدوهم: Allah gave them the turn over their enemy.
Abū al-Baqāʾ al-Rundī said, lamenting al-Andalus:
هي الأمور كما شاهدتها دول ... من سره زمن ساءته أزمان
(Such are affairs, as you have seen them: alternating turns; whom one time has pleased, other times have grieved.)
(التمحيص): purifying and cleansing. (يَمْحَقَ): He destroys.

* I'rab:
(وَلا تَهِنُوا وَلا تَحْزَنُوا وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to what is understood from His words (فسيروا). (لا) is prohibitive; (تهنوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا); (ولا تحزنوا) is also conjoined. In (وأنتم), the wāw is circumstantial; (أنتم) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject); (الأعلون) is its khabar (predicate), nominative by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): (إن) is conditional; (كان) is a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is its noun and (مؤمنين) is its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then do not weaken"; and the conditional clause is resumptive. (إِنْ يَمْسَسْكُمْ قَرْحٌ فَقَدْ مَسَّ الْقَوْمَ قَرْحٌ مِثْلُهُ): a resumptive statement, also brought to console the believers. (إن) is conditional; (يمسسكم) is the protasis; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (قرح) is the fāʿil (agent) of (يمسسكم); and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then take comfort and console yourselves". Whoever parsed (فقد مس القوم) as the apodosis erred, because what is past in meaning cannot be an apodosis, and conditional dependence can only be in the future. In (فقد), the fāʾ is a conjunction and (قد) a particle of realization; (مس القوم) is conjoined to the omitted apodosis; (مس) is a past verb; (القوم) is a fronted mafʿūl bihi and (قرح) a postponed fāʿil; and (مثله) is a naʿt (adjective) of (قرح). (وَتِلْكَ الْأَيَّامُ نُداوِلُها بَيْنَ النَّاسِ): the wāw is resumptive; the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ and (الأيام) is a badal (substitute) of it; the clause (نداولها) is the khabar; the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; and (بين الناس) is an adverb of place attached (mutaʿalliq) to (نداولها). It is also permissible to parse (الأيام) as the khabar of the demonstrative, the clause (نداولها) being a ḥāl, governed by the meaning of the demonstrative, i.e. "He points to them while they are being alternated". (وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the wāw conjoins to the omitted thing given a reason, the implied form being "We did that so that they would take heed". In (وليعلم), the lām is causal; (يعلم) is an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن); (الله) is the fāʿil; (الذين) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi; (آمنوا) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). (وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنْكُمْ شُهَداءَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يتخذ) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (يعلم); (منكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتخذ), or to an omitted ḥāl because it was originally a naʿt of (شهداء); and (شهداء) is the mafʿūl bihi. (وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is parenthetical, and the clause is parenthetical between these successive reasons; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (لا يحب الظالمين) is the khabar. (وَلِيُمَحِّصَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the clause is conjoined to the preceding reasons; (الله) is the fāʿil; (الذين) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila. (وَيَمْحَقَ الْكافِرِينَ): conjoined to the preceding reasons.

dervis-irab:142-143.t:
* I'rab:
(أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ): (أم) is a disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) conjunction in the sense of (بل); its discussion has preceded. The speech is conjoined to what precedes by way of turning from consolation to rebuke, and the hamza implied within it is for disapproval. (حسب) is a past verb in the sense of (ظن) "thought", and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); (أن) and what follows it take the place of its two objects. The meaning is: do not think — or let it not occur to the mind of any one of you — that you will enter Paradise without struggle and patience. (الجنة) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension, or accusative by removal of the preposition. (وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial; (لما) is jussive; (يعلم) is a jussive (majzūm) imperfect verb; (الله) is the fāʿil; (الذين) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi; the clause (جاهدوا) is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; (منكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (وَيَعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ): the Seven read it with fatḥa on the mīm, so the wāw is of accompaniment (maʿiyya); (يعلم) is an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن) after the wāw of accompaniment; the fāʿil is "هو"; and (الصابرين) is the mafʿūl bihi. The negation has preceded it; and the negation of knowledge with respect to Allah is a metonymy for the negation of what is known, namely struggle and patience.
It is strange that one of the early parsers should be pedantic and say: the fatḥa is the fatḥa of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the verb is jussive, conjoined to the first «يعلم»; since another quiescent letter came after it, its last letter needed a vowel, and the fatḥa was preferable because it is the lightest. [That is strange] since it is not permissible to construe the Qur'an according to less preferable views. (وَلَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ تَمَنَّوْنَ الْمَوْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَلْقَوْهُ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realization; (كنتم) is the defective (كان) and its noun, and the clause (تمنون) is its khabar (predicate). The origin of (تمنون) is (تتمنون), one of the two tāʾs having been dropped. (الموت) is the mafʿūl bihi; (من قبل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تمنون); in (أن تلقوه), (أن) is a maṣdar-forming particle of the accusative, (تلقوه) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (أن), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ the mafʿūl bihi; and the interpreted maṣdar is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (قد) is a particle of realization; (رأيتموه) [Translator's note: misprinted in the source as «أيتموه».] is a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, the wāw being for lengthening the ḍamma. In (وأنتم), the wāw is circumstantial; (أنتم) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (تنظرون) is the khabar. A muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "the cause of death".

* Benefits:
The Muslims in the first generation wished for death, not so that the field would be left clear for their enemy, but to attain the honour of martyrdom while superiority and victory were assured. This is a necessary clarification, lest a pedant ask: How is it permissible to wish for martyrdom, when wishing for it involves the victory of a disbeliever over a Muslim? For the habit of the Companions, Allah's good pleasure be upon them, was martyrdom in the way of Allah; and we do not forget the weeping of Khālid ibn al-Walīd when death came to him, because he was dying in his bed. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa said when he set out for the battle of Muʾta:
لكنني أسأل الرحمن مغفرة ... وضربة ذات فرغ تقذف الزبدا
أو طعنة بيدي حران مجهزة ... بحربة تنفذ الأحشاء والكبدا
حتى يقولوا إذا مروا على جدثي ... أرشدك الله من غاز وقد رشدا
(But I ask the Most Merciful for forgiveness, and a wide-gashing blow that throws out froth; or a finishing thrust from the hands of one thirsting [for my blood], with a spear that pierces the entrails and the liver; so that they say, when they pass by my grave: "May Allah guide you, O warrior — and indeed he was rightly guided.")
The meaning of his words ذات فرغ is "wide", al-fargh being the bucket, i.e. it makes in my body something like a bucket full of water. And al-ḥarrān is the thirsty one, thirsting for my blood.

dervis-irab:98-99.t:
* Vocabulary:
(العوج): with kasra or fatḥa on the ʿayn; it is well known. But the Arabs distinguished between the two, following their native instinct in handling this noble language: they assigned the form with kasra to abstract things (maʿānī) and the form with fatḥa to concrete things (aʿyān). You say: في كلامه عِوَج ("there is crookedness in his speech"), with kasra, and في الجدار عَوَج ("there is crookedness in the wall"), with fatḥa.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ): resumptive speech, brought to censure those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah. قل is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is "you"; يا is a vocative particle for one at a middle distance, and أهل الكتاب is a muḍāf (construct) vocative (munādā). لم: the lām is a preposition and ما is an interrogative noun of disapproval in the position of a genitive by the lām; the alif of the interrogative ما was dropped because the preposition entered upon it; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تكفرون, and بآيات الله is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to تكفرون. The vocative clause is resumptive. (وَاللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ عَلى ما تَعْمَلُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and شهيد the khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to شهيد; the clause تعملون is a ṣila (relative clause), and the clause والله شهيد is circumstantial (a ḥāl). (قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لِمَ تَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): resumptive speech to emphasise the censure and rebuke; the i'rab of its like has preceded. (مَنْ آمَنَ): من is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of تصدون, and the clause آمن has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of «من». (تَبْغُونَها عِوَجاً): the clause is circumstantial. تبغونها is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; عوجا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) in which the maṣdar (verbal noun) has been put in place of the derived noun, i.e. "crooked". In this i'rab there is the hyperbole that they seek that the straight way be crookedness itself, by way of hyperbole, as in رجل صوم ("a man [who is] fasting itself"); and that is more forceful in censuring and rebuking them. It was also said: the hāʾ in تبغونها is a pronoun accusative by removal of the preposition. The wording of Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī is: «The meaning of His saying «تبغونها عوجا» is: you seek crookedness for it (تبغون لها عوجا)»; and on this is the saying of Suḥaym, the slave of Banū al-Ḥasḥās:
بغاك وما تبغيه حتى وجدته ... كأنك قد واعدته أمس موعدا
(It sought you while you were not seeking it, until you found it, as if you had made an appointment with it yesterday.)
He means: it sought you while you were not seeking it. One says: ابغني كذا, meaning "seek it for me"; and when they mean "help me seek it and seek it with me", they say: أبغني, with fatḥa on the hamza. This is the view of Sulaym [Translator's note: so in the source]. (وَأَنْتُمْ شُهَداءُ): the wāw is circumstantial; أنتم is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ and شهداء the khabar; the nominal clause is circumstantial. (وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): the wāw is also for the ḥāl; ما is the Ḥijāzī negative; الله is its noun, nominative; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and غافل is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the khabar of «ما»; عما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to غافل, and the clause تعملون is the ṣila of the relative ما.

dervis-irab:100-101.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تُطِيعُوا فَرِيقاً مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ): resumptive speech, brought to present one of the traits of the Jews, inspired by the racism by which they are distinguished. يا is a vocative particle for one addressed at a middle distance; أيّ is a vocative, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative; the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين is a badal (substitute), and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. إن is conditional; تطيعوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); فريقا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of His saying فريقا; the clause أوتوا الكتاب is a ṣila, and الكتاب is the second object of the passive أوتوا. (يَرُدُّوكُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمانِكُمْ كافِرِينَ): يردوكم is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf is the first object of يردوكم; بعد إيمانكم is an adverb attached to كافرين, and كافرين is the second object. (وَكَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ وَأَنْتُمْ تُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ آياتُ اللَّهِ): resumptive speech, brought to direct the censure and the sense of improbability to the manner of the disbelief, by way of hyperbole. كيف is an interrogative noun of disapproval, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); تكفرون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. وأنتم: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and أنتم is a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); تتلى is an imperfect verb in the passive, and the clause is the khabar (predicate); عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تتلى, and آيات الله is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَفِيكُمْ رَسُولُهُ): the wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction; فيكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and رسوله is a postponed mubtadaʾ. (وَمَنْ يَعْتَصِمْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ هُدِيَ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ; يعتصم is the protasis and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as "he" (هو); بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يعتصم. فقد: the fāʾ connects the apodosis and قد is a particle of verification; هدي is a past verb in the passive and its nāʾib fāʿil is "he"; إلى صراط is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to هدي, and مستقيم is a naʿt. The clause فقد هدي is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من.

* Benefits:
A historical glimpse:
The Jews have a deep-rooted tradition of sowing division among nations and peoples in order to secure for themselves their alleged sovereignty and superiority; it is one of the traits of the Jews inspired by the racism by which they are distinguished and which they vigorously propagate.
In connection with the revelation of this verse, history relates that Shās ibn Qays the Jew — an old man, advanced in years, deep in wrangling and enmity, who hated the Muslims and waited for misfortunes to befall them so as to bring them down and scatter their united ranks — this Shās passed by a group of the Aws and the Khazraj while they were in a gathering talking. He was enraged by what he saw of their affection and the good relations between them in Islam, after the enmity and hatred that had been between them in the Jāhiliyya. He said: "By Allah, we will have no stability with them if they unite." So he ordered a young Jew who was with him, saying to him: "Go to them, sit with them, remind them of the Day of Buʿāth and what happened in it, and recite to them some of the poems they used to recite to one another, aimed at stirring up grudges." (Buʿāth, with ḍamma on the bāʾ, is a famous day on which the Aws and the Khazraj fought, and victory on it was for the Aws.) The young Jew did what Shās ordered him, and at that the people quarrelled; the causes of dispute were revived anew; they boasted against one another, grew angry and exchanged insults, and called out: "To arms! To arms!", and they almost drew their swords. That reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he went out to them with those of the Muhājirūn and the Anṣār who were with him, and said: "O company of Muslims! Is it with the call of the Jāhiliyya, while I am among you, after Allah has honoured you with Islam, cut off from you the burden of the Jāhiliyya and joined your hearts together, that you return to what you were upon as disbelievers?" The people realised that it was a prompting of Satan and a plot of their enemy, so they threw the weapons from their hands, wept and embraced one another, then went away with the Messenger of Allah, hearing and obeying. There was never a day uglier at its beginning and more beautiful at its end than that day.

dervis-irab:7-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُحْكَماتٌ): their expressions have been made firm, their indications are clear, and they are protected from multiple possibilities and ambiguity.
(مُتَشابِهاتٌ): in them there is a possibility of interpretation. There is something puzzling in this word, for its singular is متشابه, and how can a thing resemble itself? Resemblance occurs only between two. Like it is يقتتلان (the two fight each other): the singular does not "fight mutually", for how can one fight mutually with himself? This objection was put to Taqī al-Dīn ibn Taymiyya, the famous imam, and he said to the one who asked him: «This is a good mind». Then he refrained from answering. What occurs to the mind is that the Arabs uttered words of this pattern without intending mutuality by them, as in their sayings طابقت النّعل (I made the sandal fit), عاقبت اللص (I punished the thief), خامرت الحبّ (love pervaded me) and عاقرت الخمر (I was addicted to wine). And if we suppose that the pattern has the original meaning of mutuality (mufāʿala), the answer is that resemblance can only be between two or more, and when resembling things are gathered, each one resembles the other; so since resemblance is sound only in the state of being gathered, it was described with the plural, because each one of its individual items resembles the other.

The wisdom in the ambiguous (al-mutashābih):
If it occurs to you to ask about the secret of inclining to mention the ambiguous in the Qur'an, and of turning away from making the clear ruling general, it is said: the Qur'an was originally revealed in the style of the Arabs, in their words and in accordance with their speech, and that is of two kinds: of it is the clear (al-muḥkam), which the hearer does not mistake and which does not escape understanding; and of it is what abounds in kinds of figurative usages, and varieties of metonymies, allusions and hints.
This second kind was more effective in their souls and more captivating to them; so the Qur'an was revealed cast in both styles, containing both kinds, so that the challenge would be more general and comprehensive. Had it all been revealed clear, they would not have hesitated to seek out points of attack, nor refrained from obstinacy, wrangling and objection, and they would have said: "Why was it not revealed in the kind we find beautiful and incline to?" That is from one side. From a second side, it is because of what distinguishes the ambiguous: taxing the intellect in extracting what is locked, fathoming the aims, and drawing back the curtain from delightful points that rise above superficial, primitive viewing; so that when Allah opens [it] to him [i.e. the reader] and he is able to plumb the depths of the ambiguous, his faith is firmer and his certainty too strong to be blown away by doubts.
(الزيغ): deviating from the truth and inclining to falsehood. When zāy and yāʾ occur as the first and middle radicals of a word, they convey this meaning. Oil was called زيت because it is a liquid that inclines (flows) quickly; and زاغت الشمس تزيغ means the sun declined. Compare others with this.

* I'rab:
(هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ) is a resumptive statement brought to detail the verses of the Book and that they are of two parts: a part that people understand, and a part they do not understand because of their shortcoming and inability. (هو) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) its khabar (predicate); the clause (أنزل عليك الكتاب) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (عليك) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل); and (الكتاب) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (مِنْهُ آياتٌ مُحْكَماتٌ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الكتاب); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (آيات) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; and (محكمات) is an adjective of (آيات). (هُنَّ أُمُّ الْكِتابِ): the clause is a second adjective of (آيات); (هن) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (أم الكتاب) is its khabar. A plural has been given a singular predicate because each one of them is like a single mother. (وَأُخَرُ مُتَشابِهاتٌ) is conjoined to (آيات محكمات). (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive, brought to detail [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «لتفضيل» for «لتفصيل»] people's stance towards it; (أما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (الذين) is the mubtadaʾ; (في قلوبهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (زيغ) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (فَيَتَّبِعُونَ ما تَشابَهَ مِنْهُ ابْتِغاءَ الْفِتْنَةِ): the fāʾ links the apodosis of (أما); the clause (يتبعون) is the khabar of (الذين), and the apodosis was dispensed with, the fāʾ sufficing; (ما) is a relative noun, the direct object; the clause (تشابه) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (منه) is attached to (تشابه); (ابتغاء) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); and (الفتنة) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَابْتِغاءَ تَأْوِيلِهِ) is conjoined to (ابتغاء الفتنة). (وَما يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ): the wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is negating; (يعلم) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; (تأويله) is a fronted direct object; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (إِلَّا اللَّهُ): (إلا) is an instrument of restriction, and (الله) is the postponed fāʿil (agent) of (يعلم). (وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ): grammarians and commentators have spoken much and at length about this verse. The decisive word on it is that the wāw may be a conjunction and (الراسخون) conjoined to «الله», the meaning being:
none is guided to its interpretation except Allah and His servants who are firmly grounded in knowledge and have mastered it. It is also possible for the pause to be complete at His words «إلا الله», the wāw being resumptive and (الراسخون) a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause (يقولون). On the first view the clause (يقولون) is circumstantial, i.e. "saying". From this difference in interpretation arose the division of the scholars into two groups: the people of interpretation (taʾwīl) and the people of the outward sense (ẓāhir). We [Translator's note: the source has «ولستا», presumably «ولسنا»] are not concerned with weighing and preferring among the conflicting opinions, but we shall give a glimpse of it in the section of Benefits. (آمَنَّا بِهِ كُلٌّ مِنْ عِنْدِ رَبِّنا): the two clauses are the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl); (آمنا) is a verb and agent; (به) is attached to (آمنا); (كل) is a mubtadaʾ, beginning with which is permissible because of the meaning of generality in «كل», and the tanwīn is a substitute for a word; and (من عند ربنا) — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar. (وَما يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّا أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ): the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; (ما) is negating; (يذكر) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; (إلا) is an instrument of restriction; (أولو) is the agent of (يذكر), nominative with the wāw because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; and (الألباب) is muḍāf ilayhi.

* Benefits:
1- Some devoted a separate book to this question because of the breadth of discussion about it. Al-Qāḍī al-Bayḍāwī, and al-Zamakhsharī before him, argued for their choice of pausing at «العلم» on the grounds that this spurs minds to thinking and creativity. The Ḥashwiyya said, in summary: pausing at His words, the Exalted:
«وما يعلم تأويله إلا الله» is obligatory, so that His words «والراسخون» are a new statement. For if one did not pause there but paused at His words «والراسخون في العلم», so that it is conjoined to His words «إلا الله», one would have to begin with His words:
«يقولون آمنا به», meaning by it "saying", which is a ḥāl; and that is false, because it must either be a ḥāl of «الله» and of those firmly grounded in knowledge — as though [Translator's note: the source has «كان كان», presumably «كأنّ»] Allah, Glorified is He, and those firmly grounded in knowledge said: "We believe in it; all is from our Lord" —
which is impossible in His case, the Exalted; or it is a ḥāl of those firmly grounded in knowledge only, in which case the conjoined item is singled out by the ḥāl to the exclusion of what it is conjoined to, which is also not permissible, because it contradicts the established rule in Arabic, namely that the conjoined item shares the ruling of what it is conjoined to. So it is established that pausing at His words «إلا الله» is obligatory. And if pausing there is obligatory, then Allah has addressed us with what we do not understand, which is the meaningless (al-muhmal). I say:
The cleverness in the sophistry of the Ḥashwiyya, built on fallacy, is not hidden: they permit address with the meaningless. [Translator's note: thus in the source; the reply that follows is to their second premise.] For it is permissible to single out the conjoined item with a ḥāl where there is no ambiguity, and this is frequent in the Qur'an. Of it is: «ووهبنا له إسحق ويعقوب نافلة», for «نافلة» is a ḥāl of the conjoined item only, namely «يعقوب», because نافلة is the grandson, and that is Jacob, not Isaac.

What al-Rāzī says:
Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī argued in Mafātīḥ al-Ghayb that the correct pause is at His words «إلا الله» by six arguments. The summary of the second is that the verse indicates that seeking interpretation is blameworthy, because of His words, the Exalted: «فأما الذين في قلوبهم زيغ» to the end of the verse; had interpretation been permissible, Allah would not have censured it. The summary of the fourth is that if the wāw in His words «والراسخون» were a conjunction, His words
«يقولون آمنا به» would become a beginning, which is far-fetched according to people of eloquence; rather it would have been more fitting for them to say: "and they say (وهم يقولون): we believe in it", or for it to be said: "and they say (ويقولون): we believe in it". For all of this we have accepted both views.

dervis-irab:8-10.t:
* I'rab:
(رَبَّنا لا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنا): the clause is the speech reported (maqūl) of an omitted verb of saying. (ربنا) is a vocative in construct; (لا) is prohibitive, here meaning supplication; (تزغ) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لا); the fāʿil (agent) is "you"; (قلوبنا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the adverb of time is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تزغ), and it is in construct with the adverb (إذ); (إذ) is an adverb of past time; and the clause (هديتنا) is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa). It was also said that (إذ) has left its adverbial function and means «أن», but its rule has not changed, for it is still bound to being put in construct with what follows. This is a fine view. (وَهَبْ لَنا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً): the wāw is a conjunction; (هب) is an imperative verb; (لنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (هب); (من لدنك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (لدن) is an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of the genitive by (من); the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (رحمة) is the direct object. (إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ): the clause gives the reason for the supplication and has no grammatical position. (إن) and its noun; (أنت) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (الوهاب) is the khabar (predicate) of (أنت); and the nominal clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar of (إن). (أنت) may also be parsed as a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, (الوهاب) being the khabar of (إن). (رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ جامِعُ النَّاسِ): (ربنا) is a vocative in construct; (إن) and its noun, and (جامع الناس) is its khabar; and the clause falls within the scope of the speech reported. (لِيَوْمٍ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جامع); (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (ريب) is its noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to its omitted khabar; and the clause (لا ريب فيه) is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of (يوم). (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعادَ): the clause gives the reason for the ruling, for it is in the context of seeking favour. (إن) and its noun; and the clause (لا يخلف الميعاد) is a direct object meaning the maṣdar, namely the promise [Translator's note: thus in the source; evidently the clause (لا يخلف الميعاد) is the khabar of (إن), and it is (الميعاد) that is the direct object, a maṣdar meaning "promise"], the wāw having been changed into yāʾ because it is vowelless and preceded by a kasra. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً): the clause is resumptive. (إن) and its noun; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (لن) is a particle of negation, the subjunctive and futurity; (تغني) is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by (لن), and the clause is the khabar of (إن); (عنهم) is attached to (تغني); (أموالهم) is the agent of (تغني); (ولا أولادهم) is conjoined to (أموالهم); and (من الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «شيئا», and when it was placed before it, it was parsed as a ḥāl according to the well-known rule. The implied sense is: wealth and children will not ward off from them anything of Allah's punishment. (شيئا) is a direct object, or in the place of the maṣdar, its implied form being "any sufficing (غنى)", so it would be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (وَأُولئِكَ هُمْ وَقُودُ النَّارِ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to establish the absence of sufficing; you may also make the wāw a conjunction and the clause conjoined to the khabar of (إن). (أولئك) is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (هم) is a second mubtadaʾ; (وقود النار) is the khabar of «هم»; and the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. (هم) may also be a separating pronoun and (وقود النار) the khabar of (أولئك); this has been established many times before.

* Benefits:
(لدن and لدى) are two adverbs of place and time, indeclinable on the sukūn. Most often (لدن) is put in the genitive by (من), as in the verse. When it is put in construct with the yāʾ of the first person, the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya) is required with it, as in لدني; and this nūn is sometimes left out, so one says لدني [Translator's note: the two forms are printed identically in the source; the intended forms are لَدُنِّي (with the protective nūn) and لَدُنِي (without it)].
It is put in construct with a single word and with a clause. «غدوة» (early morning) may occur after (لدن), in which case غدوة may be put in the genitive by construct, or it may be put in the accusative as tamyīz (specification), or as the khabar of an implied (muqaddar) كان together with its noun, i.e. "since the time was early morning". The difference between (لدن) and (لدى) is that (لدن) does not occur as a pillar ('umda, i.e. an essential element) of the sentence, whereas (لدى) does; so one does not say لدنه علم, but one says لديه علم ("he has knowledge").

dervis-irab:144-144.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الأعقاب): plural of عقب, which is the back of the foot (the heel); and turning back on one's heels (الانقلاب على الأعقاب) is retreating and fleeing.

* I'rab:
(وَما مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ): the wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to explain that the death or killing of Muhammad ﷺ does not necessitate weakness or slackness in his religion. (ما) is negative; (محمد) is the mubtadaʾ (subject); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (رسول) is the khabar (predicate). (قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ): the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of (رسول); (قد) is a particle of realization; (خلت) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; (من قبله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (خلت); and (الرسل) is the fāʿil (agent). (أَفَإِنْ ماتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلى أَعْقابِكُمْ): the hamza is for rhetorical, disapproving interrogation, and the fāʾ is for conjunction; it has come after the hamza though its rank is to come first, because the hamza has the right to the head of the clause. We mentioned earlier that al-Zamakhsharī and those who follow his approach imply between them an omitted verb to which the fāʾ conjoins what follows it, the implied form being: "Do you believe in him during his lifetime, and then if he dies you apostatize?" Both are sound. The benefit of the conjunction is the connection of the conditional clause with what precedes it in the sense of causation. (إن) is conditional; (مات) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (أو قتل) is conjoined to (مات); (انقلبتم) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and (على أعقابكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). Further discussion of this restriction will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَمَنْ يَنْقَلِبْ عَلى عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَنْ يَضُرَّ اللَّهَ شَيْئاً): the wāw is resumptive; (من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; (ينقلب) is the protasis; (على عقبيه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the fāʾ is connective for the apodosis; (يضر) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (لن); (الله) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (شيئا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause (فلن يضر) is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «من». (وَسَيَجْزِي اللَّهُ الشَّاكِرِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (يجزي) is a nominative imperfect verb; (الله) is the fāʿil and (الشاكرين) the mafʿūl bihi.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «وما محمد إلا رسول» is the device of restriction (al-qaṣr). Linguistically it means confinement; technically it is the singling out of one of two things over the other and its negation from anything else. It occurs as restriction of the thing described to the attribute, and the reverse. The verse is of the first kind, i.e. Muhammad ﷺ is restricted to messengership, not going beyond it to being far from perishing — based on the Companions' finding it unthinkable that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not remain with them. So it is as though they affirmed two attributes for him: messengership and not perishing; and he was singled out by restricting him to messengership. It is thus a case of bringing out speech not according to what the apparent situation requires. It is a restriction of singling out (qaṣr ifrād), as a refutation of one who claims two things, or one of the two without preference; and in any case it is of the category of reversal restriction (qaṣr qalb), because when they turned back on their heels it was as though they believed that he was a messenger unlike the other messengers in that he would die as they died, and that they were obliged to hold fast to his religion after him just as one is obliged to hold fast to their religions after them.

dervis-irab:145-145.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُؤَجَّلًا): fixed in time, neither brought forward nor deferred; from أجل الشيء or أجّله, with the light and the doubled form, i.e. he set for it a term (ajal) from which there is no escape.

* I'rab:
(وَما كانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): a resumptive statement, brought to confirm what preceded, namely that no soul will die except by the will of Allah, and that no one dies before reaching his term, even if he flings himself into danger and plunges into battles. The wāw is resumptive; (ما) is negative; (كان) is a defective past verb; (لنفس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (كان); in (أن تموت), the maṣdar formed from (أن) and what falls within its scope is its postponed noun; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (بإذن الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). It is an emptied exception from the most general of states, the implied form being: "It is not for it to die except being permitted." (كِتاباً مُؤَجَّلًا): (كتابا) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), serving to emphasize the content of the clause before it, because the meaning is "death has been written, a writing"; (مؤجلا) is a naʿt (adjective). Ibn ʿAṭiyya chose that it be accusative as a tamyīz (specification); it has also been said that it is accusative by way of incitement (ighrāʾ), but there is no call for this far-fetched contrivance. (وَمَنْ يُرِدْ ثَوابَ الدُّنْيا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْها): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to speak of those who left their posts and sought the spoils. (من) is conditional, in the position of the nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject); (يرد) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (ثواب الدنيا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (نؤته) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of (من) — the establishment of this has preceded; and (منها) [Translator's note: the source writes «وفيها», evidently for «منها».] is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نؤته). (وَمَنْ يُرِدْ ثَوابَ الْآخِرَةِ نُؤْتِهِ مِنْها): the parsing of this has preceded. (وَسَنَجْزِي الشَّاكِرِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (سنجزي) is a nominative imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) being "نحن"; (الشاكرين) is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:146-146.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رِبِّيُّونَ): devoted to the Lord (rabbāniyyūn), a relative adjective (nisba) from al-Rabb; its discussion has preceded. It occurs in the language with all three vowels on the rāʾ; the fatḥa is the regular form, while the ḍamma and the kasra are among the changes of the nisba.
(اسْتَكانُوا): they weakened and were humbled. Al-istikāna is brokenness and feebleness. The origin of this verb is استكن, from السكون, because stillness (sukūn) is abasement; its original form is (استكون): the fatḥa was transferred to the kāf, and then the wāw was changed into an alif.

* I'rab:
(وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ نَبِيٍّ قاتَلَ مَعَهُ رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ): (كأين) is declarative (khabariyya), in the sense of declarative (كم), and it is in the position of the nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject); (من نبي) is the tamyīz (specification) of (كأين), and its tanwīn is for multitude, i.e. "many of the prophets"; the clause (قاتل) is the khabar (predicate) of (كأين); (معه) is an adverb of place attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar; (ربيون) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَما وَهَنُوا لِما أَصابَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (ما) is negative; (وهنوا) is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). In (لما), the lām is a preposition and (ما) a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the lām, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (وهنوا); the clause (أصابهم) is the ṣila (relative clause); and (في سبيل الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. You may also make (ما) maṣdariyya, the maṣdar formed from (ما) and what falls within its scope being genitive by the lām. (وَما ضَعُفُوا وَمَا اسْتَكانُوا): conjoined to «ما وهنوا». (وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الصَّابِرِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (يحب الصابرين) is the khabar.

* Benefits:
(كَأَيِّنْ) has the meaning of (كم) in interrogation and in declaration. It is compounded of the kāf of comparison and the interrogative (أي), and after the compounding there arose in it the meaning of multitude understood from declarative (كم). The two parts are not attached to anything, because they have become like a single word; for that reason Abū Ḥayyān held that «كأين» is a simple, uncompounded word, and I have not found anyone who supports him, though his view is fine and easy. It agrees with declarative (كم) in five things: 1- vagueness; 2- the need for a tamyīz; 3- indeclinability (bināʾ); 4- the obligation to come at the head of the clause; 5- conveying multitude — or multitude at times and interrogation at other times [Translator's note: the source reads «إفادة التكثير أو التكثير تارة والاستفهام تارة أخرى», which appears garbled; translated as written.]. Ubayy said to Ibn Masʿūd: "How many verses (كأين) do you read Sūrat al-Aḥzāb as?" He said: "Seventy-three." It differs from (كم) in five things: 1- it is compounded, while (كم) is simple; 2- its tamyīz is usually genitive with (من), so much so that some claimed it is obligatory, but that is refuted by what Sībawayh and Yūnus related, that they heard someone say "كأي رجلا"; 3- it does not occur as an interrogative according to the majority; 4- it does not occur in the genitive, so you do not say "بكأين تبيع هذا؟" ("For how much do you sell this?"), though some allowed it; 5- its khabar does not occur as a single word. Zuhayr said:
وكائن ترى من صامت لك معجب ... زيادته أو نقصه في التكلم
(How many a silent man you see who pleases you — his excess or his deficiency shows when he speaks.)
Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh said: it is «أي», upon which the kāf of comparison entered and remained fixed with it, so that after the compounding it came to mean (كم). It was written in the Muṣḥaf with a nūn because it is a word transferred from its origin, so its form was changed because its meaning changed. The Arabs treated it freely with metathesis and elision, so that it has four dialectal forms, all of which have been read: first, «كائن», as in the saying of Zuhayr; second, كأيّ, like كعيّن, which is the origin; third, كأين, like كعين; and fourth, كيئن, with a quiescent yāʾ followed by a hamza with kasra.

dervis-irab:102-103.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَاعْتَصِمُوا): al-iʿtiṣām is taking refuge and holding fast. One says: "I hold fast (muʿtaṣim) to so-and-so", "I seek protection (mustaʿṣim) with him", "I hold fast to his rope", and "we are in the protection (ʿiṣma) of Allah"; and everything by which a thing is ʿuṣima — i.e. guarded and preserved — is an ʿiṣām. The ʿayn and the ṣād, when they are the first and second radicals of a word, have wonderful linguistic properties: they indicate strength and impregnability and what is in their sense, such as guarding and refusal. So one says: فلان لا تعصب سلماته ("so-and-so's salam trees are not bound up"), i.e. he is not overpowered. Al-Kumayt ibn Zayd said:
ولا سمراتي يبتغيهن عاضد ... ولا سلماتي في بجيلة تعصب
(No lopper seeks out my samura trees, nor are my salam trees bound up among Bajīla.)
And: "so-and-so is maʿṣūb of frame", i.e. compact, firm of flesh. When they made someone a chief, they bound him with a turban (ʿaṣabūhu). "This is a day ʿaṣīb and ʿaṣabṣab", i.e. severe. "So-and-so is partisan (yataʿaṣṣabu) for his people." ʿAṣr (pressing) is well known, and force must be used in pressing. "This is a matter by which youth has been pressed (taʿaṣṣarat) and has reached full strength upon it." Al-muʿṣirāt are the clouds that rain down water. "The wind ʿaṣafat (blew violently)", so it is ʿāṣif and muʿṣifa, which is stronger; "time ʿaṣafa with them", i.e. destroyed and annihilated them. ʿAdī ibn Zayd said:
ثم أضحوا عصف الدهر بهم ... وكذاك الدهر حالا بعد حال
(Then they became such that time swept them away; and such is time, state after state.)
And "He made them like eaten straw (ʿaṣf maʾkūl)" is well known. It is said of a hungry person: "the sparrows (ʿaṣāfīr) of his belly cried out", which is a colloquial expression that is good Arabic, i.e. they made a strong noise. The sparrow (ʿuṣfūr) was so called because it never ceases chirping. Al-Nuʿmān gave al-Nābigha a hundred of his ʿaṣāfīr, which were fine-bred camels of his; they came to an end [Translator's note: so in the source, «انتهت»; possibly a misprint for انتُهِبت, "were plundered"] on the Day of Dārat Maʾsal. Dhū al-Rumma said:
نجائب من ضرب العصافير ضربها ... أخذنا أباها يوم دارة مأسل
(Fine-bred camels of the ʿaṣāfīr stock; their sire we took on the Day of Dārat Maʾsal.)
Had we wished to be exhaustive, we would have let you hear the most astonishing things, but what has preceded is enough for us.
(شَفا): al-shafā is the edge of the pit, [used] as masculine and feminine. More discussion of it will come in the Benefits section.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقاتِهِ): resumptive speech, brought for what contains the believers' perfecting of themselves. The i'rab of the vocative has preceded, so renew your acquaintance with it. اتقوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); الله is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and حق تقاته is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). The annexation here is of the type of annexing the adjective to what it qualifies; the original is "the true taqāh" (التقاة الحق), and التقاة is a maṣdar (verbal noun) whose analysis has preceded. (وَلا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; تموتن is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is an attached pronoun in the position of a nominative as the fāʿil; the doubled nūn is for emphasis and has no grammatical position. إلا is a particle of restriction; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مسلمون the khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ جَمِيعاً وَلا تَفَرَّقُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; اعتصموا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; بحبل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) اعتصموا; جميعا is a ḥāl. لا is prohibitive; تفرقوا is an imperfect verb, one of whose two tāʾs has been dropped optionally — its original is تتفرقوا — jussive by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn. (وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; اذكروا is an imperative verb conjoined to اعتصموا; نعمة الله is the mafʿūl bihi, and عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نعمة. (إِذْ كُنْتُمْ أَعْداءً فَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِكُمْ): إذ is an adverb for past time attached to اذكروا, and the clause كنتم is in the position of a genitive by annexation to it. كنتم is an incomplete past verb and its noun, and أعداء is its khabar; the fāʾ is a conjunction; ألف is a past verb, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to Allah; بين is an adverb attached to ألف, and قلوبكم is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ بِنِعْمَتِهِ إِخْواناً): the fāʾ is a conjunction; أصبحتم is an incomplete past verb and the tāʾ is its noun; بنعمته is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, and إخوانا is the khabar of أصبحتم. (وَكُنْتُمْ عَلى شَفا حُفْرَةٍ مِنَ النَّارِ فَأَنْقَذَكُمْ مِنْها): conjoined to what preceded. كان and its noun; على شفا حفرة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar; من النار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of حفرة; فأنقذكم is conjoined to كنتم, and منها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنقذكم. (كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آياتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq or ḥāl, as has preceded many times. يبين الله is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and آياته is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. لعلّ and its noun, and the clause تهتدون is its khabar; the clause of hope is circumstantial.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) in holding fast to the rope of Allah: trust in Allah and reliance on His protection are likened to the state of one who grasps a firm rope let down from a high place, so that he is safe from its breaking or snapping. By the rope here He meant the Noble Qur'an, because of the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «The Qur'an is the firm rope of Allah; its wonders never end, and it does not wear out from much repetition. Whoever speaks by it speaks the truth, whoever acts by it is rightly guided, and whoever holds fast to it is guided to a straight path.»
2- The antithesis (ṭibāq) between أعداء (enemies) and إخوان (brothers).

* Benefits:
1- Al-shafā is originally masculine, but the pronoun refers back to it in the verse as feminine [in منها], because it acquired the feminine through its annexation to الحفرة. The regular rule is that a masculine muḍāf may acquire femininity from a feminine muḍāf ilayhi, and vice versa; the condition for this in both cases is that the muḍāf can be dispensed with in favour of the muḍāf ilayhi with the meaning remaining sound. Of the first is the saying of al-Aghlab:
طول الليالي أسرعت في نقضي ... نقضن كلي ونقضن بعضي
(The length of the nights has hastened in undoing me; they have undone all of me and undone part of me.)
He made «أسرعت» feminine although it is a predicate about a masculine [طول], because it acquired the feminine from «الليالي». On this basis the saying of Majnūn Laylā is explained:
وما حب الديار شغفن قلبي ... ولكن حب من سكن الديارا
(It is not love of the dwellings that has smitten my heart, but love of the one who dwelt in the dwellings.)
And of the second form is the saying of another:
إنارة العقل مكسوف بطوع هوى ... وعقل عاصي الهوى يزداد تنويرا
(The illumination of the mind is eclipsed by obedience to passion, while the mind of one who disobeys passion grows ever brighter.)
He made «مكسوف» masculine although it is a predicate about a feminine, namely «إثارة» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has إنارة], because it acquired the masculine from its annexation to العقل. This is an important topic, so reflect on it.
2- (أصبح) is used for the qualified one's having a quality at the time of morning, and it is used in the sense of صار ("became"), in which case the time of morning is not considered, but rather mere transition and becoming from one state to another. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Ḍabuʿ said:
أصبحت لا أحمل السلاح ولا ... أملك رأس البعير إن نفرا
(I have become unable to bear arms, nor can I hold the camel's head if it bolts.)

dervis-irab:104-105.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلْتَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ): speech conjoined to what precedes it, of the type of conjoining the specific to the general, brought to explain the chief of good deeds. The wāw is a conjunction, though you may make it resumptive, the clause then being resumptive, brought to explain what preceded. The lām is the lām of command, and it is made quiescent after wāw, fāʾ and thumma. تكن is an incomplete imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of تكن, and أمة is its postponed noun; the clause يدعون إلى الخير is in the position of a nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of أمة. It is also permissible for the clause يدعون to be the khabar, with منكم a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt that was fronted before what it qualifies and so is parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial). إلى الخير is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يدعون. (وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ): the two clauses are conjoined to the clause يدعون إلى الخير. (وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ): its i'rab has preceded many times. (وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُوا): the wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; تكونوا is an incomplete imperfect verb, jussive by لا, and the wāw is its noun; كالذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar. You may make the kāf a noun in the sense of مثل ("like"), so that it is the khabar, and الذين is a relative noun in the position of a genitive by annexation; the clause تفرقوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. (وَاخْتَلَفُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّناتُ): the wāw is a conjunction and اختلفوا is conjoined to تفرقوا; من بعد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اختلفوا; ما is maṣdar-forming, interpreted together with جاءهم البينات as a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to بعد; the hāʾ is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and البينات the postponed fāʿil (agent). (وَأُولئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; عذاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ and عظيم a naʿt; the nominal clause is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the demonstrative.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the verse there is the conjoining of the specific [to the general], a topic of subtle approach that seems like a spell of magic; it signals greater attention to the specific. The detail of this is that calling to good is general, and following it with commanding the right and forbidding the wrong signals that these two are singled out for greater attention, and shows their excellence over other good deeds.
2- Contrast (muqābala): He has set in antithesis command and prohibition, and the right and the wrong.

dervis-irab:106-107.t:
* I'rab:
(يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ): the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, implied as: اذكر ("remember"), so the clause is resumptive, brought to explain the state of the two groups. The clause تبيض وجوه is in the position of a genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; وجوه is the fāʿil (agent), and تسود وجوه is conjoined to تبيض وجوه. (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اسْوَدَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ): the fāʾ is for ramification (tafrīʿ) and has a resumptive meaning, so the clause is resumptive. أمّا is a particle of condition and detailing; الذين is a relative noun in the position of a nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause اسودت وجوههم is the ṣila (relative clause). (أَكَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمانِكُمْ): the clause is the object of an omitted saying, [omitted] together with the fāʾ that connects the answer of أمّا, i.e. "so it will be said to them: Did you disbelieve…?" The clause «فيقال» is the khabar (predicate) of الذين and it is the answer of «أمّا». The condition of «أمّا» is not mentioned explicitly; rather they made its omission obligatory. It appears when the meaning is unpacked and expressed with what «أمّا» stands in for, namely مهما; the implied form is: "Whatever be the case, as for those whose faces have blackened, it will be said to them such-and-such." So memorise it and draw analogies from it.
