The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; كفرتم is a verb and its fāʿil; بعد is an adverb attached to كفرتم, and إيمانكم is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (فَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "eloquent" fāʾ), because it discloses what is implied, i.e. "if you know that, then taste the punishment". بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ذوقوا; ما is maṣdar-forming, and it together with what it enters upon is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, i.e. "because of your disbelief"; the clause تكفرون is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كنتم. (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ ابْيَضَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ): its i'rab has preceded. (فَفِي رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): the fāʾ connects the answer of أمّا; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar of الذين; هم is a mubtadaʾ; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خالدون, and خالدون is their khabar; the clause هم فيها خالدون is circumstantial (a ḥāl).

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse there is the device of tadbīj (colour-embroidery), a device of subtle approach, sweet in its manner and elegant in its indication. Its definition is that the poet or prose writer mentions two or more colours, intending thereby metonymy (kināya) or double meaning (tawriya) for the purposes he wants, and sometimes intending nothing but description. White and black are two opposite colours, and opposition means antithesis (taṭābuq); but He used them as a metonymy for two groups of people: whoever was of the people of truth was marked with the whiteness and brightness of colour, and whoever was of the people of falsehood was marked with the blackness of night and its gloom. What there is in that of terrifying effect, and of the disparity of the fate decreed for each of the two groups, is not hidden. Among the delightful instances of tadbīj in poetry, with the metonymy it contains, is the saying of Abū Tammām in his elegy on Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd al-Ṭūsī, the martyr of jihad:
تردى ثياب الموت حمرا فما دجا ... لها الليل الا وهي من سندس خضر
(He put on the garments of death red, and night had not darkened over them before they were green, of fine silk.)
Tadbīj is a tafʿīl from al-dabj, which is engraving and adorning; the origin of dībāj (brocade) is Persian, Arabicised. Among its delightful instances is the saying of Ṣafī al-Dīn al-Ḥillī:
بيض صنائعنا سود وقائعنا ... خضر مرابعنا حمر مواضينا
(White are our good deeds, black our battles, green our pastures, red our sharp blades.)
2- The metaphor in «tasting the punishment»: He likened it to something bitter that is eaten, then omitted what it is likened to and kept one of its concomitants, namely tasting. What there is in it of the sense of bitterness is not hidden; that is by way of the subordinate implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya al-makniyya).
3- The non-metaphorical trope (majāz mursal) in «رحمة الله» (the mercy of Allah), the relation in it being that of the occupant (ḥāliyya), because a person does not dwell in mercy but dwells in its place, which is Paradise.

dervis-irab:147-148.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما كانَ قَوْلَهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to what precedes, to explain their virtues in speech after their virtues in deed had been established. (ما) is negative; (كان) is a defective past verb; (قولهم) is its fronted khabar (predicate), and its noun is the maṣdar-forming (أن) and what falls within its scope. Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read «قولهم» in the nominative, as the noun of (كان), the khabar being (أن) and what falls within its scope. (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and the exception is emptied (mufarragh) from the most general of things. (رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنا ذُنُوبَنا وَإِسْرافَنا فِي أَمْرِنا): (ربنا) is one addressed in the vocative, annexed, with the vocative particle omitted from it; the clause (اغفر) is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); (لنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (اغفر); (ذنوبنا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and (إسرافنا) is conjoined to it; and (في أمرنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (إسرافنا). They attributed excess to themselves only out of self-abasement, and they put the request for forgiveness first, considering it more important to them than anything. (وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدامَنا وَانْصُرْنا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكافِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ثبت) is a verb of supplication; (أقدامنا) is the mafʿūl bihi; (انصرنا) is also conjoined; (على القوم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (انصرنا); and (الكافرين) is a naʿt (adjective). (فَآتاهُمُ اللَّهُ ثَوابَ الدُّنْيا): the fāʾ is a conjunction or resumptive; (آتاهم الله) is a verb, a mafʿūl bihi and the fāʿil (agent); and (ثواب الدنيا) is the second mafʿūl bihi. (وَحُسْنَ ثَوابِ الْآخِرَةِ): the wāw is a conjunction and (حسن) is conjoined to (ثواب). He singled out the reward of the Hereafter for "goodness" only to extol its excellence, and that it is the most worthy thing for a person to count on and seek. (وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause (يحب المحسنين) is the khabar.

dervis-irab:149-151.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرعب), with ḍamma on the rāʾ and with sukūn or ḍamma on the ʿayn — it has been read both ways: fear. One says رعبته, so he is مرعوب (terrified). Its origin is filling: one says رعبت الحوض, i.e. I filled the basin, and سيل راعب, i.e. a torrent that filled the valley. It is transitive by itself and with the hamza.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its parsing has preceded. (إِنْ تُطِيعُوا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): (إن) is conditional; (تطيعوا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الذين) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila (relative clause). The whole clause is resumptive, brought to warn the believers against being deceived by what the hypocrites said to the believers at the time of the defeat: "Return to your religion and your brethren; had Muhammad been a prophet he would not have been killed." It has also been said: [the meaning is] if you submit to Abū Sufyān and his company, they will turn you back to their religion. (يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَلى أَعْقابِكُمْ): (يردوكم) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm); the wāw is the fāʿil and the kāf the mafʿūl bihi; and (على أعقابكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَتَنْقَلِبُوا خاسِرِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (تنقلبوا) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (يردوكم); and (خاسرين) is a ḥāl. (بَلِ اللَّهُ مَوْلاكُمْ): (بل) is a particle of digression and conjunction; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and (مولاكم) the khabar (predicate). The speech is conjoined to what is part of the content of the condition, as if it were said: "They are not helpers to you such that you should obey them; rather, Allah [is your protector]." (الله) has also been read in the accusative, as the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "rather, obey Allah", with (مولاكم) a badal (substitute) of it. (وَهُوَ خَيْرُ النَّاصِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is the mubtadaʾ and (خير الناصرين) its khabar. (سَنُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ): a resumptive statement, brought by way of iltifāt (shift of person) to draw attention to the terror of what He the Exalted will cast into their hearts. The sīn is a particle of the future; (نلقي) is a nominative imperfect verb, its fāʿil being "نحن"; (في قلوب) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نلقي); (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa (genitive construct); the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila, with no grammatical position; and (الرعب) is the mafʿūl bihi of (نلقي). (بِما أَشْرَكُوا بِاللَّهِ ما لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطاناً): in (بما), the bāʾ is a preposition and (ما) is maṣdariyya, interpreted with what follows it as a maṣdar genitive by the bāʾ, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (نلقي), i.e. "because of their associating partners"; or (ما) is a relative noun and the clause is its ṣila. (بالله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أشركوا); (ما) is a relative noun, the object of (أشركوا); the clause (لم ينزل به سلطانا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of «سلطانا»; and (سلطانا) is the object of (ينزل). (وَمَأْواهُمُ النَّارُ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to explain their states in the Hereafter after explaining their states in this world of manifest abandonment. (مأواهم) is the mubtadaʾ and (النار) its khabar; the reverse is also permissible, and perhaps it is preferable. (وَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (بئس) is an inflexible past verb for expressing blame; (مثوى) is the fāʿil, annexed to a noun bearing «ال»; (الظالمين) is a muḍāf ilayhi; and the one specified for blame is omitted, its implied form being "the Fire".

* Rhetoric:
1- Iltifāt (shift of person) in the words of Allah the Exalted «سنلقى» [Translator's note: so spelled in the source, for «سنلقي».]: He shifted from the third person to the first person to show concern for what He the Exalted will cast into their hearts.
2- Metaphor (al-istiʿāra) in the words of Allah the Exalted «سنلقى», because casting (الإلقاء) is only of physical bodies [Translator's note: the source has «الإجرام», evidently for «الأجرام», "bodies".]; so it was borrowed here for terror, by way of embodiment and personification, treating the abstract as the concrete.

dervis-irab:152-153.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَحُسُّونَهُمْ): you kill them in great slaughter and extirpate them; from حسّه يحسّه, of the pattern of نصر, when he destroyed his senses (ḥiss). Jarīr said:
تحسهم السيوف كما تسامى ... عريق النار في الأجم الحصيد
(The swords mow them down as the deep-rooted fire rises in the reaped thicket.)
(تُصْعِدُونَ): with ḍamma on the tāʾ, from أصعد, i.e. he went far into the mountain and into the land. One says: صعد في الجبل (he climbed the mountain) and أصعد في الأرض (he went far off into the land).
(تَلْوُونَ): you turn your faces, and you do not stop for anyone.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ): the wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to detail the battle of Uḥud as the lengthy works have related it. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realization; (صدقكم الله) is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a postponed fāʿil (agent); and (وعده) is accusative by removal of the preposition, because (صدق) takes two objects, one by itself and the other by means of a preposition, i.e. "in His promise". (إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ بِإِذْنِهِ): (إذ) is an adverb for past time, attached (mutaʿalliq) to (صدقكم); the clause (تحسونهم) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's iḍāfa (genitive construct) to it; and (بإذنه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) [Translator's note: the source misprints «حان» for «حال».] from the fāʿil of (تحسونهم), i.e. "permitted to you". (حَتَّى إِذا فَشِلْتُمْ وَتَنازَعْتُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ): it is permissible for (حتى) here to be a particle of limit and of the genitive, meaning "until", so that together with what it enters upon it is attached to (تحسونهم), i.e. "you were killing them up to this time"; al-Zamakhsharī attached it to (صدقكم), i.e. "Allah was true to His promise to you up to the time of your faltering". Both are sound. It is also permissible for it to be inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), entering upon the conditional clause. (إذا) is an adverb for future time, attached to its apodosis; the clause (فشلتم) is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa; and the apodosis of (إذا) is omitted, according to the sound view, the implied form being "He withheld His help from you", or "you were defeated", or "the truth became manifest and clear to you". In (وتنازعتم), the wāw is a conjunction and the clause (تنازعتم) is conjoined to the clause (فشلتم); and (في الأمر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تنازعتم). (وَعَصَيْتُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما أَراكُمْ ما تُحِبُّونَ): conjoined to what precedes. (من بعد) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (عصيتم); (ما) is maṣdariyya, interpreted with the verb after it as a maṣdar to which «بعد» is annexed; (أراكم) is a past verb, its fāʿil being "هو"; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi; (ما) is a relative noun, the second mafʿūl bihi; and the clause (تحبون) is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. (مِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيا وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ): the clause is explicative, with no grammatical position. The meaning is: "until, when all that happened and you were divided into two groups" — then He explained the two groups. (منكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (من) is a relative noun, the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يريد) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (الدنيا) is the mafʿūl bihi; and (ومنكم من يريد الآخرة) is conjoined to the first clause, and in it is the explanation of the second group. (ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ): (ثم) is a conjunction of sequence with delay; the clause (صرفكم) is conjoined to the omitted apodosis of (إذا), i.e. "He withheld His help from you, then He turned you away from them", i.e. turned you back from them, to test your patience and steadfastness. (عنهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (صرف). In (ليبتليكم), the lām is causal and (يبتلي) is an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن) after the lām of cause; and the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to (صرف). (وَلَقَدْ عَفا عَنْكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of realization; (عفا) is a past verb; and (عنكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (عفا). (وَاللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and (ذو فضل) the khabar; and (على المؤمنين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (فضل) or to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of it. (إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ وَلا تَلْوُونَ عَلى أَحَدٍ): (إذ) is an adverb for past time, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember", or to (صرفكم), or to (عفا عنكم), as though it were a case of competition between governors (tanāzuʿ). The clause (تصعدون) is in the position of the genitive by iḍāfa; (ولا تلوون) is conjoined to (تصعدون) — or you may make the wāw circumstantial, so that the clause is accusative as a ḥāl; and (على أحد) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تلوون). (وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ فِي أُخْراكُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial; (الرسول) is the mubtadaʾ and the clause (يدعوكم) the khabar; and (في أخراكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being in your rear" or "in your company". It is a beautiful depiction of the stance of the leader and his steadfastness as he says: "To me, to me, servants of Allah! I am the Messenger of Allah; whoever turns back to the attack shall have Paradise." (فَأَثابَكُمْ غَمًّا بِغَمٍّ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أثابكم) is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi; (غما) may be a second mafʿūl bihi, by (أثابكم) being made to include the meaning of requiting and giving, and it may be parsed as a tamyīz (specification). (بغم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt, i.e. "a grief joined to a grief". (لِكَيْلا تَحْزَنُوا عَلى ما فاتَكُمْ وَلا ما أَصابَكُمْ): the lām is a preposition; (كي) is a particle of cause, of the accusative and of the future; (لا) is redundant (zāʾida) [Translator's note: so in the source; (لا) here is ordinarily parsed as negative.]; (تحزنوا) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (كي); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (أثابكم); (على ما فاتكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تحزنوا); the clause (فاتكم) is the ṣila of the relative noun; and (ولا ما أصابكم) is conjoined to «ما فاتكم». (وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and (خبير) the khabar; (بما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خبير); and the clause (تعملون) is the ṣila of the relative noun.

* Benefits:
(كي): the Arabs have two ways with it:
1- The first is that it governs the verb by itself, in the status of «أن», and together with what follows it is in the status of a noun, just as «أن» is.
2- The second is that it is a preposition in the status of the lām, so that the verb after it is made accusative by a concealed «أن», just as it is made accusative after the lām. When it is in the status of «أن», the lām may enter upon it, as in the verse just mentioned; and when it is a preposition, it may enter upon nouns as a preposition does. Of this is the Arabs' saying: كيمه? ("Why?"). They brought (كي) onto interrogative «ما» just as prepositions enter upon it, as in لم, بم and عمّ; they dropped the alif as they drop it with prepositions, and added the hāʾ of pausing (hāʾ al-sakt) upon pausing, saying: كيمه.

dervis-irab:154-154.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النعاس), with ḍamma on the nūn: the approach of sleep, or its beginning, and a slackening of the senses.

* I'rab:
(ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً نُعاساً): (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (أنزل) is a past verb, and the clause is conjoined to (فأثابكم), while (أثابكم) is conjoined to (صرفكم). (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to (أنزل); (من بعد الغم) is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to (أنزل); (أمنة) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (نعاسا) is a badal (substitute) of (أمنة). It may be a badal of complete correspondence, considering what the two words refer to, or a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because each of them includes the other; the referring pronoun is omitted because it is known, i.e. "in them", and because the speech points to it, as you will see in the section on benefits.
(يَغْشى طائِفَةً مِنْكُمْ): the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of His word «نعاسا»; (طائفة) is the mafʿūl bihi of (يغشى); and (منكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt of (طائفة). They are those who were true to their Lord and whose certainty was firm. (وَطائِفَةٌ قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; (طائفة) is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and beginning with it [though indefinite] is allowed because it is described by an omitted adjective indicated by the context, i.e. "other than you", as evidenced by (يغشى طائفة منكم); the clause (قد أهمتهم أنفسهم) is the khabar (predicate); and the clause is resumptive, brought to explain the state of the hypocrites. (يَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ ظَنَّ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ): the clause (يظنون) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in (أهمتهم); it is also permissible to make «قد أهمتهم أنفسهم» a naʿt, with the clause (يظنون) as the khabar. (بالله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يظنون); (غير الحق) is a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the meaning being: they think of Allah other than the true thought which ought to come over souls [Translator's note: the source misprints «غبر» for «غير».]. (ظن الجاهلية) is a badal of «غير الحق», or accusative as a maṣdar of comparison, i.e. "a thought like the thought of the Jāhiliyya", or accusative by removal of the preposition. On this view no two objects are mentioned for (يظنون), and the bāʾ is of place/containment, as you say "ظننت بزيد" ("I harboured a thought about Zayd"); and when that is so, «ظننت» does not take two objects. The grammarians have stated this explicitly, and upon it is the saying of the poet:
فقلت لهم ظنوا بألفي مدجج ... سراتهم في السابري المسرّد
(I said to them: expect two thousand fully armed men, their chiefs in fine close-woven Sābirī mail.)
(يَقُولُونَ هَلْ لَنا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): the clause (يقولون) is a badal of the clause (يظنون). (هل) is a particle of disapproving interrogation whose meaning is negation, i.e. "we have not". (لنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (من الأمر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt of (شيء), then the naʿt was placed before the thing it describes and so was parsed as a ḥāl; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (شيء) is genitive by (من) in form, in the position of the nominative as the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (قُلْ: إِنَّ الْأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ): the clause is parenthetical. (إن) and its noun; (كله) is tawkīd (emphasis) of «الأمر», because it is divisible; (لله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of (إن); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying. (يُخْفُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ ما لا يُبْدُونَ لَكَ): the clause (يخفون) is a ḥāl from the pronoun of (يقولون), i.e. "they say among themselves, whispering together". (في أنفسهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يخفون); (ما) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi; (لا) is negative; the clause (يبدون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما); and (لك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يبدون). (يَقُولُونَ لَوْ كانَ لَنا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ ما قُتِلْنا هاهُنا): the clause (يقولون) is resumptive, brought to explain what precedes it, and to serve as a fresh beginning of the discourse about them, refreshing the hearer's energy and claiming his attention. (لو) is conditional; (كان) is a defective past verb; (لنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of (كان); (من الأمر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; (شيء) is the postponed noun of (كان); (ما) is negative; (قتلنا) is a passive past verb and (نا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause (ما قتلنا) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. In (هاهنا), the hāʾ is for alerting, and (هنا) is a demonstrative in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place attached to (قتلنا). (قُلْ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ): the clause is resumptive, brought to explain that the terms of life are written, and that had they stayed in Medina, causes would have arisen for them in which they would go out to meet their deaths, and that when their term comes they can neither delay it by an hour nor bring it forward. (لو) is conditional; (كنتم) is (كان) and its noun; (في بيوتكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying. (لَبَرَزَ الَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَتْلُ إِلى مَضاجِعِهِمْ): the lām occurs in the apodosis; (برز الذين) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the clause (كتب عليهم القتل) is the ṣila of (الذين); and (إلى مضاجعهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (برز), i.e. "to the places where they would fall". (وَلِيَبْتَلِيَ اللَّهُ ما فِي صُدُورِكُمْ): the wāw conjoins to something omitted, its implied form being: "He did what He did at Uḥud for many benefits, and so that He might test". In (ليبتلي), the lām is causal; (يبتلي) is an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن) after the lām; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb, i.e. "He did that for benefits of which you are ignorant, and to test what is in the breasts". (ما) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi; and (في صدوركم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element which has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَلِيُمَحِّصَ ما فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ): conjoined to (ليبتلي ما في صدوركم). (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, to emphasize His knowledge, the Exalted, of secrets and hidden things. (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and (عليم) the khabar; and (بذات الصدور) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (عليم).

* Rhetoric:
Were we to wish to expatiate in bringing out the places of eloquence contained in it, space would fail us; it suffices us to touch on them briefly in a way that covers what would require long and extended expression. Among them:
1- Concision (al-ījāz): it appears in many places in it, as follows:
a- In the word (ثم) occurring at its beginning, to indicate that a lapse of time extended after what befell them in the battle of Uḥud in that wondrous event. After they went up into the mountain and turned their faces away from seeing what had happened, from the excess of the bewilderment that afflicted them and the fright and panic that overcame them, Allah followed them up with grief after grief, or upon grief; or because of it [Translator's note: the source's syntax is loose here; translated as written.] the sending down of security came about: drowsiness hovered in the eyelids, heads nodded, joints slackened, and they swayed beneath their ḥajaf, and the swords fell from their hands. Al-ḥajaf, with two fatḥas, is the plural of ḥajafa, a name for the shield or the leather buckler.
b- In the word «أمنة» and the substitution of drowsiness for it is much concision, indicating that security and calm took hold of them as soon as drowsiness hovered and the creeping of slumber seized the corners of their eyelids. Only one who feels secure and whom fear has left becomes drowsy; the fearful one does not sleep, but sees his enemies everywhere. Al-Mutanabbī glimpsed these lofty heights when he said:
وضاقت الأرض حتى كاد خائفهم ... إذا رأى غير شيء ظنه رجلا
(The earth grew so narrow that their frightened one, whenever he saw nothing at all, almost took it for a man.)
c- In the word «شيء» in His words «هل لنا من الأمر من شيء», which contains what pages could not hold, such as victory and prevailing over the enemy after his pressure and ferocity had grown severe.
d- In the omission of the khabar of «طائفة», to keep them [the believers] free of being associated with those who were concerned only for themselves and had no desire left but for their own safety, rather than for the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions — for they did not sleep. As for implying the khabar, it could be implied as: «تعرفهم بسيماهم» ("you know them by their mark"). [Translator's note: earlier in the I'rab the author took «قد أهمتهم أنفسهم» or «يظنون» as the khabar; here he speaks of the khabar as omitted.]
2- Metonymy (al-kināya): He used "beds" (المضاجع) as a metonymy for the places of falling, where they met their deaths and clasped hands with their fates.
3- Variation in the apodosis of (لو): once it came without the lām and once joined to it, and in this is a wondrous secret. He said: «لو كان لنا من الأمر من شيء ما قتلنا هاهنا» [Translator's note: so quoted in the source, with «من شيء»; the verse reads «لو كان لنا من الأمر شيء».], then He said: «لو كنتم في بيوتكم لبرز الذين كتب عليهم القتل». The well-known rule is that when the apodosis of (لو) is negated with (ما), the lām is usually absent, and in the affirmative it is the reverse, because the affirmative has more need of confirmation and firm establishment. This is among the secrets by which the Book of Allah is distinguished, so that it may be the miracle for all time.

* Benefits:
1- This verse gathers all the letters of the alphabet; there is no other in the Qur'an but it and the verse of al-Fatḥ, namely the words of Allah the Exalted «محمد رسول الله» up to His words «وعد الله الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات منهم مغفرة وأجرا عظيما».
2- In the badal of inclusion there must be a referring pronoun linking it to the first. As for His word «نعاسا», what is meant is "drowsiness in it", because the one addressed knows that easily, as has preceded — because each of security and drowsiness includes the other.

dervis-irab:55-57.t:
* I'rab:
(إِذْ قالَ اللَّهُ يا عِيسى) «إذ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for past time, attached to an implied «اذكر» ("remember"), or attached to «مكروا», or it is an adverb of «خير الماكرين». The clause «قال الله» is in the position of a genitive as the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). «يا» is a vocative particle, and «عيسى» is the one addressed, a singular proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied ḍamma on the alif. (إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ) «إن» and its noun; «متوفيك» is its khabar (predicate), and the kāf is a muḍāf ilayhi; «رافعك» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «متوفيك»; «إلي» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «رافعك», because it is an active participle. (وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) «ومطهرك» is conjoined to what preceded; «من الذين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «مطهرك»; the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no grammatical position. (وَجاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) «وجاعل» is likewise conjoined; «الذين» is a relative noun in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «اتبعوك» is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; «فوق» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted element, being the second direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of «جاعل»; «الذين» is a muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila of the relative noun. (إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «جاعل»; that is, this making continues until the Day of Resurrection. (ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ) «ثم» is a conjunction of delay (tarākhī); «إلي» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar, and «مرجعكم» is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (فَأَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction of immediate sequence (taʿqīb); «أحكم» is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and «بينكم» is an adverb of place attached to «أحكم». (فِيما كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ) «فيما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أحكم»; the clause «كنتم» is the ṣila of the relative, with kāna and its noun; «فيه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تختلفون»; the clause «تختلفون» is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of «كنتم»; and the whole sentence is in the position of an accusative as the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl). (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) The fāʾ is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), and the sentence is a new one, introduced to serve as an explanation of the judgement between the two groups. «أما» is a particle of condition and elaboration (tafṣīl); «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position. (فَأُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذاباً شَدِيداً فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ) The fāʾ is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis of «أما»; «أعذبهم» is a verb, an agent (a latent pronoun) and a direct object, and the verbal clause is the khabar of «الذين»; «عذابا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and «شديدا» is its adjective (naʿt); «في الدنيا» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a second adjective; and «الآخرة» is conjoined to «الدنيا». (وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ) The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāl) or resumptive; «ما» is negative; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar; «من» is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and «ناصرين» is genitive in form by «من» and nominative in position, because it is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is circumstantial or resumptive. (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ) Conjoined to the previous verse; «الصالحات» is a direct object, accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. (فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ) The fāʾ is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis of «أما»; «يوفيهم» is an imperfect verb in the nominative, its agent a latent pronoun, implied form "he", and the hāʾ is the first direct object; «أجورهم» is the second direct object, and the clause is the khabar of «الذين». (وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الظَّالِمِينَ) The wāw is resumptive; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «لا يحب الظالمين» is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The commentators differed about His words: «إني متوفيك ورافعك إلي» ("I will take you and raise you to Myself"). Qatāda and others said: this is a case of fronting and postponing (taqdīm and taʾkhīr), and the sense is: "I will raise you to Myself and take you", meaning after that. ʿAlī ibn Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: «متوفيك» means "I will cause you to die". The majority of the commentators say: what is meant here by wafāh is sleep, as the Exalted said: «وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل» ("And it is He who takes your souls by night") – the verse. Some poets have borrowed this meaning in its very wording, saying:
تبارك من توفاكم بليل ... ويعلم ما جرحتم في النهار
(Blessed is He who takes your souls by night ... and knows what you have earned by day.)

dervis-irab:155-155.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اسْتَزَلَّهُمُ) He sought slips from them and led them gradually toward it. «الزلل» (slip) is deviation from the truth and falling into wrongdoings.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا مِنْكُمْ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعانِ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to explain the cause of the defeat of those who were routed and of Satan's causing them to slip, so that they were deprived of strength of heart and steadiness of spirit, which are the equipment of victory. «إن» and its noun; the clause «تولوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «منكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl (circumstantial); «يوم» is an adverb of time attached to «تولوا», and the clause «التقى» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (إِنَّمَا اسْتَزَلَّهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ بِبَعْضِ ما كَسَبُوا) The sentence is the khabar of «إن». «إنما»: «ما» is a restrictive particle (kāffa) and «إن» is restricted by it (makfūfa). «استزلهم الشيطان» is a verb, a direct object and an agent. He repeated «إن» by way of restriction (ḥaṣr), to draw attention to the source of the error and its cause, namely their inclining toward Satan and listening to his caller. «ببعض» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «استزلهم»; «ما» is a relative noun in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «كسبوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun, and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted; that is, by their abandoning the post in which the Messenger had commanded them to stand firm, which drew them into the defeat. (وَلَقَدْ عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ) The wāw is resumptive and the sentence is a new one, introduced to announce pardon for them after they repented and apologised. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of confirmation (taḥqīq); «عفا الله» is a verb and an agent; «عنهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «عفا». (إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ) «إن» and its noun; «غفور حليم» are two khabars of «إن», and the sentence is causal (taʿlīliyya) for His words: «عفا عنهم» ("He pardoned them").

dervis-irab:156-156.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ضَرَبُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ) They travelled in it and went far in their journey, for trade, for fighting or for other purposes.
(غُزًّى) The plural of «غاز» (one who goes on a raid). The regular form would be «غزاة», like «كرام», «رماة», and «ساع» / «سعاة», but they treated the defective root like the sound one.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) Its i'rab has been given before. (لا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) «لا» is a prohibitive particle; «تكونوا» is an imperfect incomplete verb (kāna), jussive by «لا», and the wāw is its noun; «كالذين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, the khabar. You may also take the kāf as a noun meaning "like" (mithl), in which case it is the khabar. «الذين» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila. The prohibitive sentence is resumptive, introduced to warn the believers against imitating the hypocrites and uttering the like of what they said. (وَقالُوا لِإِخْوانِهِمْ إِذا ضَرَبُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ) Conjoined to the ṣila. What is meant by "brotherhood" is sharing the same kind or lineage. «إذا» is merely temporal, intended to relate a past state so as to embody the scene; the adverb is attached to «قالوا», and the clause «ضربوا في الأرض» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, because it comes after the adverb. (أَوْ كانُوا غُزًّى) Conjoined to the clause «ضربوا في الأرض»; «غزى» is the khabar of «كانوا», and the wāw is its noun. (لَوْ كانُوا عِنْدَنا ما ماتُوا وَما قُتِلُوا) The sentence is in the position of an accusative as the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl). «لو» is conditional, with kāna and its noun; «عندنا» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted element, the khabar of «كانوا», that is, "staying with us". The clause «ما ماتوا» has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; and the clause «وما قتلوا» is conjoined to the clause «ما ماتوا». (لِيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ ذلِكَ حَسْرَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ) The lām is the lām of consequence (ʿāqiba) or becoming (ṣayrūra), that is, they said that so as to end up with this outcome. «يجعل» is an imperfect verb with an optionally implied «أن» after the lām of consequence; it and the maṣdar governed by the lām are attached to an omitted verb understood from the context, that is: "they said that and believed it". «الله» is the agent, «ذلك» is the first direct object, «حسرة» is the second direct object, and «في قلوبهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, an adjective of «حسرة». What is pointed to is the speaking aloud and the belief. Al-Zajjāj made it their supposition that, had they not been present, they would not have been killed. (وَاللَّهُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ) The wāw is resumptive; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يحيي» is the khabar; the clause «يميت» is conjoined to the clause «يحيي». (وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ) The wāw is resumptive; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ; «بما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «بصير»; the clause «تعملون» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; and «بصير» is the khabar of «الله».

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse there is a splendid art of rhetoric, namely relating a past state in order to bring the scene to mind, embody the intended meaning and personify what the speaker wishes to present. «إذا» is an adverb for the future, yet it is attached to «قالوا», which is a past verb. The apparent sense of the speech called for «إذ», which indicates the past, but he turned away from it to «إذا» in order to relate the past state and bring it to mind. Its benefit is the continuation of the time that frames the state under discussion up to the time of speaking. Al-Zajjāj elaborated this meaning skilfully with his words: "«إذا» here stands in for the time that has passed and the time that is to come, meaning that it is merely for time, or that continuation is intended by it."
2- The antithesis (ṭibāq) between «يحيي» and «يميت». It is among the most concise and truthful of speech and the furthest in indicating the intended meaning, for He, glory be to Him, sometimes keeps the traveller and the raider alive though they plunge into places of destruction, and then causes the resident and the one who sits at home to die though they take the means of caution and care. Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī aspired to this lofty height of rhetoric with his words:
يقتل العاجز الجبان وقد يعجز عن قطع بخنق المولود
ويوقّى الفتى المخشّ وقد خوّ ... ض في ماء لبة الصنديد
(Translator's note: the text of these two verses is corrupt in the source and cannot be translated word for word; the sense that the author draws from them follows.)
He says: do not be cowardly and do not be greedy for life, for incapacity and cowardice are not among the causes of survival and do not save from death. And may Allah have mercy on Khālid ibn al-Walīd, who said at his death: "There is not a handsbreadth in me but has a blow or a stab in it, and here I am dying as the donkey dies. So may the eyes of the cowards not sleep!"

* Benefits:
(The lām of consequence) or of becoming is the one that indicates the outcome and end of a thing. Its rule in operation is the rule of the lām of causation (taʿlīl) in the optional implying of «أن» after it; examples of it will come.

dervis-irab:157-158.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَئِنْ قُتِلْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَوْ مُتُّمْ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to establish that what you fear happening is not something to be feared, but ought rather to be a spur to you to fight and continue the jihad. The wāw is resumptive; the lām is the one that prepares for an implied oath (muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam); «إن» is conditional; «قتلتم» is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, and it is passive, the tāʾ being the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); «في سبيل الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قتلتم»; «أو متم» is conjoined to «قتلتم», and «متم» is a past verb from «مات يموت», like «قال يقول», so the mīm takes a ḍamma; a kasra is also permitted if it is from «مات يمات», like «خاف يخاف», and both have been read. (لَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَحْمَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ) The lām is the lām of inception (ibtidāʾ); «مغفرة» is a mubtadaʾ, and it is permissible to begin with it although it is indefinite because it is qualified by a preposition and its genitive noun; «رحمة» is conjoined to «مغفرة»; «خير» is the khabar; «مما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خير»; and the clause «يجمعون» is the ṣila of «ما». The lām of inception and what follows it is a clause with no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, according to the established rule that when an oath and a condition occur together, the answer is given to whichever of them comes first. (وَلَئِنْ مُتُّمْ أَوْ قُتِلْتُمْ) Its i'rab has been given before. (لَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُحْشَرُونَ) The lām and what follows it are the answer to the oath; «إلى الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تحشرون»; «تحشرون» is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse and the one before it there is an orderly art in the topic of fronting and postponing (taqdīm and taʾkhīr). Death and killing occur in them three times; death is put before killing in the first and the last of them, and killing is put before death in the middle one, following the fronting of what is more important and more noble.

dervis-irab:25-27.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُولِجُ) means "You make enter", from أولج الشيء, "he made the thing enter". And ولج يلج (of the pattern وعد) ولوجا and ولجة: "he entered".

* I'rab:
(فَكَيْفَ إِذا جَمَعْناهُمْ) This construction is one of the difficult ones. Of the views the i'rab scholars have put forward, it can be summed up in two that deserve consideration: 1- كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a fronted khabar (predicate), and the mubtadaʾ (subject) is omitted, its implied form being "their state" (حالهم); it is then a self-standing sentence, and كيف cannot then be dispensed with, as stated earlier in the rule on كيف.
2- كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of an omitted verb which is the apodosis of إذا, namely "it was established" (استقرت). On the first view, إذا is attached to the "being established" to which كيف is attached, and إذا does not imply the sense of a condition but is purely adverbial of time; on the second view it is an adverbial of future time implying the sense of a condition, attached to the omitted apodosis, which is استقرت. On this view the famous verse is explained:
أشوقا ولمّا يمض لي غير ليلة ... فكيف إذا جد المطي بنا عشرا
(Longing, when but a single night has passed for me? Then how [will it be] when the riding camels press on with us for ten?)
Ibn Hishām and Abū l-Baqāʾ favoured the ḥāl analysis. We consider the first view farther from artificiality, because we see no trace of conditionality in إذا in this strange construction; so reflect. [Translator's note: the source prints «جراب إذا»; «جواب إذا» ("the apodosis of إذا") is evidently meant.] The clause جمعناهم is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and the فاء that precedes كيف is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); the sentence is resumptive, put forward to nullify what deluded them and to depict the dreadful terrors that will befall them. (لِيَوْمٍ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جمعناهم; لا is the lā of generic negation, and ريب is its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of accusative; فيه is attached to an omitted khabar of it. The clause لا ريب فيه is in the position of genitive as an adjective of يوم. (وَوُفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ما كَسَبَتْ) The واو is a conjunction; وفيت is a passive past verb; كل نفس is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); ما is a relative noun, a direct object; and the clause كسبت is the ṣila (relative clause). (وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ) The واو is a ḥāl-waw; هم is the mubtadaʾ; لا is a negative particle; يظلمون is a passive imperfect verb, and the واو is the deputy agent; the clause لا يظلمون is in the position of nominative as their khabar, and the nominal sentence joined with the واو is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مالِكَ الْمُلْكِ) A resumptive speech, put forward to answer the hypocrites who did not believe his saying: "My community will remain manifest." قل is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; اللهم is a vocative, a single proper noun, and the doubled ميم is a replacement for «يا», having no grammatical position; and مالك الملك is a second vocative from which the vocative particle has been omitted, i.e. "O Owner of the Kingdom". It was not made an adjective only because the doubled ميم prevents following (tabaʿiyya), as Sībawayh established when he said: "The ميم has removed this word from the like of it among nouns." Ibn Yaʿīsh said: "Know that Sībawayh does not permit اللهم to be qualified by an adjective, since it is a form that occurs only in the vocative, so it is not qualified." Abū l-ʿAbbās al-Mubarrad disagreed with him and adduced the words of the Exalted: «اللهم فاطر السموات والأرض». Sībawayh takes فاطر السموات as a second vocative, not an adjective; al-Mubarrad said: the ميم is a substitute for «يا», and the one addressed with «يا» is not barred from being qualified, so likewise with what is a replacement for it. (تُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشاءُ) You may make this clause a ḥāl of the one addressed, since he is in the position of a direct object; تؤتي is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; الملك is the first direct object; من is a relative noun, the second direct object; and the clause تشاء is the ṣila. (وَتَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشاءُ) Conjoined to what precedes. (وَتُعِزُّ مَنْ تَشاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَنْ تَشاءُ) Likewise conjoined. (بِيَدِكَ الْخَيْرُ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; الخير is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is also a ḥāl. (إِنَّكَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) A resumptive clause serving as a reason for what precedes. (تُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهارِ) The clause is also a ḥāl. (وَتُولِجُ النَّهارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ) Conjoined to the foregoing clause. (وَتُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ وَتُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ مِنَ الْحَيِّ) Likewise conjoined. (وَتَرْزُقُ مَنْ تَشاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ) Likewise conjoined; من is a relative noun in the position of accusative, a direct object; the clause تشاء is the ṣila; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of ترزق.

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), since by "the living" and "the dead" He meant the Muslim and the disbeliever: the thing likened (al-mushabbah) is omitted and the thing likened to (al-mushabbah bihi) retained. If He meant the sperm-drop and the egg, then the speech runs on the side of the literal, not the figurative.
2- Ikhtifāʾ (suppression by sufficiency) in His saying «بيدك الخير»: He confined Himself to "the good" by way of being content with the opposite, i.e. "and the evil", like His saying: «سرابيل تقيكم الحر» ("garments that protect you from the heat"), i.e. "and the cold"; and because the good is what is desired.
3- Antithesis (muqābala): He contrasts «تؤتي» with «تنزع», «تعز» with «تذل» [Translator's note: the source prints «تغر»; «تعز» is evidently meant], «الليل» with «النهار», and «الحي» with «الميت».
4- Through the interrogative in His saying «فكيف» He departs from its true meaning to the meaning of intimidation and of the horror of what Allah has prepared for them on a harsh day on which sights and insights are bewildered, and hearts and consciences are fixed in dread.

* Benefits:
(اللَّهُمَّ) At times it departs from pure vocative use and then has two meanings:
A- The respondent mentions it to fix the answer in the hearer's mind; so if someone tells you something, you say: اللهم نعم ("O Allah, yes").
B- It is used to indicate rarity and the infrequent occurrence of what is mentioned with it, as when you say to someone who is lazy: "You will succeed, اللهم, if you exert greater effort", while you know that he exerts no effort at all, or that this is unlikely of him; on this basis our writers err in using it before إلا.

dervis-irab:28-28.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُقاةً) Its origin is وقية, with a ḍamma on the واو; the واو was changed to ت and the ياء to ألف because of its being vowelled with what precedes it having a fatḥa. It is thus a maṣdar (verbal noun) of تقية, like رمية.

* I'rab:
(لا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكافِرِينَ أَوْلِياءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) A resumptive speech, put forward to forbid taking them as allies, as we witness today. لا is a prohibitive particle; يتخذ is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا; المؤمنون is the agent; الكافرين is the first direct object; أولياء is the second direct object; and من دون المؤمنين is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent, i.e. "the believers being in a state of passing beyond allegiance to the believers", or of the object, i.e. "the disbelievers being supporters apart from the believers". (وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ فَلَيْسَ مِنَ اللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ) The واو is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), and the whole clause is parenthetical; من is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); يفعل is the protasis, jussive; ذلك is a demonstrative in the position of accusative, a direct object; the فاء links the apodosis; ليس is a defective past verb and its noun is a latent pronoun referring to «من». من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because in origin it was an adjective of الشيء, and when it was fronted it was parsed as a ḥāl; and في شيء is attached to an omitted khabar of ليس. (إِلَّا أَنْ تَتَّقُوا مِنْهُمْ تُقاةً) إلا is a particle of restriction; أن and what is within its scope is a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition with its genitive noun is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The meaning: the believer does not take the disbeliever as an ally for any reason whatever except for precaution (taqiyya). منهم is attached to تتقوا; تقاة is accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the meaning being "that you guard yourselves with a guarding" (تتقوا اتقاء); verbal nouns stand in for one another. It is also permissible that it be a direct object, by way of tadmīn (the verb being given the sense of another verb), «تتقوا» being given the meaning of fear, i.e. "unless you fear from their side something that must be guarded against". (وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ) The واو is resumptive; يحذركم is an imperfect verb and the كاف is a direct object; الله is the agent; and نفسه is the second direct object of يحذركم, because in origin it takes one, and by the doubling (of the middle letter) it gained another. (وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ) The واو is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; and المصير is a postponed mubtadaʾ.

* Rhetoric:
A- In this verse there is a wonderful iltifāt (shift of address) from the third person to the second person. Had it followed the usual course of speech, He would have said: "unless they guard themselves" (إلا أن يتقوا). But He turned from the third person to the second for a secret that is like a spell. For allegiance to the disbelievers and enemies, and to everyone who conspires against the safety of the homelands, is a thing deemed ugly and repugnant, which natural disposition rejects, and it is not fitting to face the chosen and the allies with it; so He brought it in the third person, as though drawing for them a line of clear expression.
Yet this holds only in matters where there is no harm; but as for conspiring against the entity (of the community) and the safety of the believers' lives, precaution is not permitted with enemies who have no concern except the seizing of land and the draining of energies. With these no conciliation is lawful, and it is in no way permissible to conclude any treaty with them, because they do not hesitate to break it. They may exploit it to pounce on those who trusted them and relied on their treaties, as in my own words:
أيّ شأن العهود قطعت ... ثم أضحت ترهات بعد حين
لا تغرنك قصاصات غدت ... شركا ينصب للمستضعفين
(What value have treaties that were concluded, then became idle nonsense after a while? Let not scraps of paper deceive you, which have become a snare set for the weak.)

Beware of the enemy: a historical glance:
Here it is fitting for us to cite what history relates concerning the revelation of this verse. It is related that a group of Muslims used to befriend the Jews, so Allah sent down this verse, forbidding persistence in that. It is also said: ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit had allies from the Jews, and on the Day of the Confederates he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have with me five hundred of the Jews, and I have thought to seek support with them against the enemy."
So this verse was revealed, since allegiance to the ally and allegiance to the enemy cannot be reconciled at one time. He said:
تود عدوي ثم تزعم أنني ... صديقك ليس النّوك عنك بعازب
(You love my enemy, then claim that I am your friend; folly is not far from you.)
2- Muṣākala (verbal correspondence) in His saying: «ويحذركم الله نفسه». Applying that to Him, glory be to Him, the Exalted, is permissible in muṣākala, like His saying also: «تعلم ما في نفسي ولا أعلم ما في نفسك» ("You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself"). It is also said: the speech is a mixed figure (majāz mursal), the meaning being "Allah warns you of His punishment", like «واسأل القرية» ("ask the town"), a majāz mursal, so "self" was put in the place of the implied word; and in that is a severe threat and a great frightening of His servants lest they expose themselves to His punishment by allegiance to His enemies.

dervis-irab:29-29.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ: إِنْ تُخْفُوا ما فِي صُدُورِكُمْ أَوْ تُبْدُوهُ) A resumptive speech, put forward to serve as an explanation of His saying: «ويحذركم الله نفسه». قل is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; إن is conditional; تخفوا is the protasis, and the sign of its jussive is the dropping of the نون, and the واو is the agent; ما is a relative noun in the position of accusative, a direct object; and في صدوركم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما; أو is a conjunction; and تبدوه is conjoined to تخفوا. The conditional clause together with its apodosis, which follows, is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl). (يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ) The apodosis; the هاء is a direct object and الله the agent. (وَيَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) The واو is resumptive; يعلم is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and its agent is "he", referring to Allah. It was brought as a resumption, not as a conjoined clause, because Allah's knowledge does not depend on a condition; so it is a case of mentioning the general after the particular. It is better to supply an omitted mubtadaʾ, so that the clause «يعلم» is its khabar, the implied form being: «وهو يعلم»; and the clause after the واو is resumptive with no grammatical position. ما is a direct object, and في السموات is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of ما; and ما في الأرض is conjoined to «ما في السموات». (وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) The واو is resumptive; الله is the mubtadaʾ; على كل شيء is attached to an omitted element related to قدير [Translator's note: the source prints «بقدير»; read as "attached to قدير" or an omitted element, as printed]; and قدير is the khabar of الله.

dervis-irab:30-30.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الأمد): the goal and the end-point. The difference between it and الأبد is that الأمد is a limited span of time, even if the limit is unknown, whereas الأبد is a span of time that is not limited.

* I'rab:
(يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ما عَمِلَتْ مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُحْضَراً) يوم is an adverbial attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «اذكر» ("remember"), and the clause تجد is in the position of genitive by annexation. «تجد» may be in the sense of "meets and befalls", so it takes one object, and may be in the sense of "knows", so it takes two. كل نفس is the agent of تجد; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; the clause عملت is the ṣila, the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. «عملته»; ومن خير are attached to an omitted ḥāl; and محضرا is a ḥāl on the first view and a second direct object on the second; the whole clause is resumptive with no grammatical position. (وَما عَمِلَتْ مِنْ سُوءٍ) The واو is resumptive; ما is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ, and the clause عملت is the ṣila; and من سوء are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَها وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَداً بَعِيداً) The clause تود is the khabar of ما; and لو that occurs after تود is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), but the entry of a particle upon its like is problematic here, so it is preferable that it remain conditional; أن is a particle resembling the verb, maṣdar-forming; بينها is an adverbial attached to an omitted khabar fronted for أنّ, and بينه is conjoined to the adverbial. The apodosis of «لو» is then omitted, its implied form being: "she would have rejoiced and been at ease"; and أن with what follows it is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "established" (ثابت), or the agent of an omitted verb, its implied form being "it was established" (ثبت). It is noticed that the omissions then become many: the object of تود has been omitted, and the apodosis of لو, and the khabar of أن or the verb of the agent. For that reason treating it as maṣdar-forming would be easier were it not for the technical obstacle, namely the entry of a maṣdar-forming particle upon a similar maṣdar-forming particle. (وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ) Its i'rab was given shortly before; He repeated it so that fear of Allah would be before their eyes. (وَاللَّهُ رَؤُفٌ بِالْعِبادِ) The واو is resumptive; الله is the mubtadaʾ; رؤوف is its khabar; and بالعباد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to رؤوف.

dervis-irab:31-32.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ: إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي) A resumptive speech, put forward to explain the meaning of love of Allah. قل is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; إن is conditional; كان is a defective past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis, and the تاء is its noun, and the clause تحبون الله is its khabar; the فاء links the apodosis; اتبعوني is an imperative verb, the واو is the agent, the نون is for protection (wiqāya), and the ياء is a direct object; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; and the clause إن كنتم is the content of what is said. (يُحْبِبْكُمُ) The reply to a request (jawāb al-ṭalab), jussive, and the كاف is a direct object, (اللَّهَ) the agent. (وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ) Conjoined to يحببكم. (وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) The واو is resumptive; الله is the mubtadaʾ; غفور رحيم are two khabars of the mubtadaʾ. (قُلْ أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ) Also a resumptive speech; the clause أطيعوا is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said. (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْكافِرِينَ) The فاء is resumptive; إن is conditional; تولوا is an imperfect verb from which one of the two تاءs has been dropped, and it is the protasis, and the clause has no grammatical position. It is also permissible that it be a past verb attributed to the third-person pronoun, in which case it is a case of iltifāt from the second person to the third, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the protasis; the فاء links the apodosis; إن and its noun, and the clause لا يحب الكافرين is its khabar; and the clause «فإن الله» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis.

* Rhetoric:
Majāz mursal in the servants' love of Allah the Exalted and His love of them, the relation being "what it comes to be" (mā yakūnu).
As for their love of Him, what is meant is what love results in, namely singling Him out for worship to the exclusion of others; and as for His love of them, what is meant is what it results in, namely satisfaction with them and forgiveness of their sins. And here is a glance at love which cannot be dispensed with:
Love according to the philosophers: the philosophers hold, as Swedenborg the Swede (سويد نبرغ السويدي) [Translator's note: the name is printed thus in the source] reports of them, that love is the life of man, and that Allah alone is the very essence of love, because He is the very essence of life. Love in the language is the inclination of the one characterised by it toward a pleasing thing; and the pleasures that arouse love are divided into those perceived by the senses, such as the pleasure of taste in flavours, the pleasure of sight and touch in beautiful forms, the pleasure of smell in fragrant scents, and the pleasure of hearing in beautiful melodies; and those perceived by the intellect, such as the pleasure of standing, leadership, knowledge, and the like. And if the motives differ, nothing known is more perfect or more beautiful than the true object of worship, and when this love is attained it prompts acts of obedience and conformity.
Love according to the Sufis: the Sufis say that love is the intoxication of contemplation, the courage of the one who gives, the faith of the saint, and the true root of moral realisation and spiritual perception. Al-Thawrī said to Rābiʿa al-ʿAdawiyya: "What is the reality of your faith?" She said: "I did not worship Him from fear of His Fire nor from love of His Garden, that I should be like the bad hireling, but I worshipped Him out of love for Him and longing for Him." And she recited:
أحبك حبين: حب الهوى ... وحبا لأنك أهل لذاكا
فأما الذي هو حب الهوى ... فشغلي بذكرك عما سواكا
وأما الذي أنت أهل له ... فكشفك لي الحجب حتى أراكا
(I love You with two loves: a love of passion, and a love because You are worthy of it. As for the love of passion, it is my being occupied with remembering You to the exclusion of all else. As for the love of which You are worthy, it is Your lifting the veils for me until I see You.)
The discussion would be long; what has preceded is enough for us.

dervis-irab:159-159.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَظًّا) Harsh. «الفظاظة» is coarseness in dealing with people, in word and deed.
Al-Rāghib said: "«الفظّ» is one of disagreeable character, and this is borrowed from «الفظّ», which is the water of the rumen, which is disliked to drink except out of necessity. «الغلظة» is the opposite of gentleness. One says «غلظ» and «غلظ», with kasra and with ḍamma. From harshness (ghilẓa) arises coarseness (fazẓāza); and coarseness was put first for a secret reason, namely the fronting of what is evident to the senses over what is hidden in the heart.

* I'rab:
(فَبِما رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to establish what must be followed in order to win people's affection and draw them to the good. The fāʾ is resumptive; «بما رحمة» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «لنت»; «ما» is redundant for emphasis; «من الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, an adjective of «رحمة»; «لنت» is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and the tāʾ is the agent; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «لنت». (وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ الْقَلْبِ لَانْفَضُّوا مِنْ حَوْلِكَ) The wāw is a conjunction on an implied element, that is: "you were gentle, and had you not been gentle..." «لو» is conditional; «كنت» is the incomplete kāna and its noun; «فظا» is its khabar; «لانفضوا»: the lām falls in the answer to «لو», and «انفضوا» is a verb and an agent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; «من حولك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «انفضوا». (فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ (fāʾ fasīḥa), that is: "if you wish to follow the best way, then pardon them in what concerns you". «اعف» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and its agent is "you"; «عنهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «اعف»; «استغفر» is conjoined to «اعف», that is: in what concerns others than you; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «استغفر». (وَشاوِرْهُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ) Conjoined likewise; «في الأمر» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «شاورهم». (فَإِذا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and you may take it as resumptive, in which case the sentence is a new one, introduced to establish what must be done after consultation. Consultation was put first to indicate that reliance on Allah (tawakkul) does not mean neglecting planning, and to make clear that consultation is among the best of matters; otherwise the command to consult would conflict with the command to rely on Allah and to entrust matters to Allah the Exalted. «إذا» is an adverb for future time, and the clause «عزمت» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; «فتوكل»: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis of «إذا», and «توكل» is an imperative verb; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; «على الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «توكل». (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ) The sentence is causal and has no grammatical position; «إن» and its noun, and the clause «يحب المتوكلين» is its khabar.

* Benefits:
The addition of «ما» (redundant) between the bāʾ, «عن», «من» and the kāf and their genitive nouns is well known in the Arabic tongue and established in the science of Arabic. Some of the grammarians held that «ما» is not redundant but is a complete indefinite noun meaning "something", with «رحمة» a substitute (badal) for it. It seems that those who say this are fleeing from calling it redundant. It was also said: «ما» here is interrogative. Fakhr al-Rāzī said, and this is his text: "The verifiers said: the entry of a word whose placement is meaningless into the speech of the Wisest of the wise is not permissible. Here «ما» may be an interrogative of wonder, the implied form being: «فبأي رحمة من الله لنت لهم» ('by what mercy from Allah were you gentle to them!'). That is because their offence was great, and yet he showed no harshness in speech whatever and no roughness in words; they knew that this could only come about by divine support, and so it was said."
What these verifiers said is sound, but the redundancy of «ما» for emphasis is not denied, in its established places, by anyone with the least touch of taste and attachment to Arabic, let alone by one who engages in interpreting the speech of Allah. «ما» in this place is not what someone might imagine, a meaningless element, such that it would need to be interpreted as an interrogative of wonder. Moreover, his implying «فبأي رحمة» is evidence that he made «ما» a muḍāf to «رحمة», and what he held is mistaken on two counts. One: the interrogative «ما» is not made a muḍāf, nor are interrogative nouns other than «أيّ», without disagreement; and «كم» is disputed. The other: if the idāfa is not sound, its i'rab would be as a badal, and if it were a badal for the interrogative noun, the interrogative hamza must be repeated in the badal, as is established. He would have been spared this confusion and this climbing over the wall by the statement of al-Zajjāj about this «ما»: that it is a filler (ṣila) with the sense of emphasis, by the consensus of the grammarians and the rhetoricians.

An interesting discussion between al-Ghazālī and Ibn al-Athīr:
An interesting discussion took place between al-Ghazālī and Ibn al-Athīr. Al-Ghazālī said, speaking of the divisions of metaphor (majāz): "The twelfth division is addition in speech without benefit, as in His words: «فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم». Here «ما» is redundant, with no meaning, that is: «فبرحمة من الله لنت لهم»." Ibn al-Athīr answered him, saying: "I do not consider this statement correct, and it is open to criticism on two counts. One: this division is not metaphor, because metaphor is the indication of a word to something other than that for which it was set in the root of the language, and this is not found in the verse; rather it indicates the linguistic placement pronounced in the root of the language. The other: even if I granted that this is metaphor, I would deny that the word «ما» is redundant and meaningless; it came, rather, to magnify the matter of the favour by which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became gentle toward them, and it is pure eloquence; and were the speech bare of it, it would not have that grandeur." Until he says: "As for al-Ghazālī, may Allah have mercy on him, he is, to my mind, excused for not knowing that, because it is not his discipline. Whoever holds that there is in the Qur'an a redundant word with no meaning is either ignorant of this statement or lax in his religion and belief. The statement of the grammarians that «ما» in this verse is redundant means only that it does not prevent what precedes it from operating, just as they call it in another place a restrictive (kāffa), that is, it restrains the operating particle from its operation, as in your saying: «إنما زيد قائم», where «ما» has restrained «إن» from operating on «زيد». In the verse it did not prevent operation; do you not see that it did not prevent the bāʾ from operating in the genitive of «الرحمة»?" So consider this discussion, for it is of great beauty.

dervis-irab:160-160.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنْ يَنْصُرْكُمُ اللَّهُ فَلا غالِبَ لَكُمْ) A resumptive discourse, to make reliance on Allah the Exalted and dependence on Him obligatory. «إن» is conditional; «ينصركم» is the protasis, and the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of an accusative as direct object; «الله» is the agent. «فلا»: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis, and «لا» is the lā of generic negation, which operates as «إن» does; «غالب» is its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa. The clause «فلا غالب لكم» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, its khabar. (وَإِنْ يَخْذُلْكُمْ فَمَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَنْصُرُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; «إن» is conditional; «يخذلكم» is the protasis; «فمن»: the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ for the apodosis, and «من» is an interrogative noun of denial (inkārī) in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; «ذا» is a demonstrative in the position of a nominative as the khabar of «من»; «الذي» is a relative noun in the position of a nominative as a badal of the demonstrative; «من بعده» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl; the nominal clause «فمن...» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; and the clause «ينصركم» is the ṣila and has no grammatical position. (وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; «على الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يتوكل»; the fāʾ is to confirm the resumption; the lām is the lām of command; «يتوكل» is an imperfect verb jussive by the lām; and «المؤمنون» is the agent. In confirming the resumption after the denial and negation there is an emphatic urging to rely on Allah after taking the means of caution and care.

dervis-irab:161-163.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غَلَّ) He took secretly, by exploitation and betrayal. Ghulūl (misappropriation of spoils) is an attribute that is incompatible with prophethood. Among the pleasant paronomasia is their saying: «يد المؤمن لا تغلّ وقلب المؤمن لا يغلّ» ("The hand of the believer does not misappropriate and the heart of the believer does not harbour rancour"). The first, with a ḍamma on the ghayn, is from «الغلول»; the second, with a kasra, is from «الغل», that is, rancour.

* I'rab:
(وَما كانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to deny misappropriation of the spoils on the part of the Prophet ﷺ. In one reading it is passive, that is, "that misappropriation be attributed to him"; both readings deny this attribute of the Prophet, because of his infallibility and because ghulūl is forbidden. The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is negative; «كان» is an incomplete past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa; «لنبي» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar; and «أن يغل» is an interpreted maṣdar, its postponed noun. (وَمَنْ يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِما غَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) The wāw is resumptive, and the discourse is a new one, introduced to deter from ghulūl. «من» is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ; «يغلل» is the protasis and «يأت» its apodosis; «بما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يأت»; the clause «غل» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «يوم القيامة» is an adverb of time, also attached to «يأت»; and the clause of the protasis and its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (ثُمَّ تُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ما كَسَبَتْ) «ثم» is a conjunction of order with delay; «توفى» is a passive imperfect verb conjoined to the conditional clause; «كل نفس» is the deputy agent; «ما» is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as second direct object; and the clause «كسبت» is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ) The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «لا يظلمون» is the khabar of «هم»; the clause is resumptive or circumstantial, and we see the resumptive as more likely, because it serves as an explanation of «توفى كل نفس ما كسبت» in the way of justice, so that every person receives his recompense without injustice or deficiency. (أَفَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ رِضْوانَ اللَّهِ) The hamza is interrogative of denial; the fāʾ is a conjunction on an omitted element, the intention being that it come before the hamza. The discussion of this construction has gone before, and the implied element is: "Have I made for you something by which you distinguish between the misguided and the guided? Whoever follows the pleasure of Allah and is guided is not like one who has returned with His anger." The interrogative of denial means negation. «من» is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ; the clause «اتبع» is the ṣila; «رضوان الله» is the direct object of «اتبع»; and the sentence is conjoined to the omitted element, which is resumptive. (كَمَنْ باءَ بِسَخَطٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ) «كمن»: the kāf is a preposition and «من» is a relative noun in the position of a genitive by the kāf; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element, the khabar of «من»; or the kāf is a noun meaning "like", the khabar, and «من» is a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «باء» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «بسخط» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «باء»; and «من الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, an adjective. (وَمَأْواهُ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ) The wāw is a conjunction; «مأواه» is a mubtadaʾ and «جهنم» its khabar; the sentence is conjoined to the ṣila, that is: "and like one whose abode is Hell". You may also take the wāw as resumptive; in either case it has no grammatical position. «وبئس»: the wāw is likewise a conjunction; «بئس» is a rigid past verb for forming blame; «المصير» is the agent; and the specified subject of the blame (makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm) is omitted, that is, «جهنم». (هُمْ دَرَجاتٌ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to show the disparity between the two groups, as will come under rhetoric. «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and «درجات» the khabar; «عند الله» is an adverb attached to an omitted element, an adjective of «درجات»; «والله»: the wāw is resumptive, «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and «بصير» the khabar; «بما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «بصير»; and the clause «يعملون» is the ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses there are diverse arts too many to count; they can be summarised as follows.
1- Emphasis in the prohibition. Emphasis of this form occurs often in the Qur'an, as in the words of the Exalted: «ما كان لنبي أن يكون له أسرى» ("It is not for a prophet to have captives"), and «ما كان للنبي والذين آمنوا ... أن يستغفروا للمشركين» ("It is not for the Prophet and those who believe ... to ask forgiveness for the polytheists").
2- Ghulūl is the more deserving of emphasis, because the picturing of the emphasis takes a form that arouses fear and bars the mind from thinking of it and picturing it, let alone committing it and plunging into its ways. It is fitting for us to cite a hadith containing an artistic embodiment of the picture of ghulūl, or exploitation, or drawing private benefits at the expense of the fighters and those who strive in the way of Allah, even at the expense of dumb animals. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim narrated from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us one day and mentioned ghulūl; he made it grave and made its matter grave, until he said: "Let me not find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a horse on his neck, neighing, and he says: O Messenger of Allah, help me! And I say: I have no power to do anything for you from Allah; I have already conveyed to you." The hadith is long; we have taken from it what precedes.
3- The eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh) in «هم درجات»: He made them the degrees themselves, to emphasise the disparity between them in reward and punishment.
4- The shift of person (iltifāt), which here is turning away from mentioning the particular, the Prophet, to mentioning the general, every soul, to include everyone who earns wrongfully, and to be gentle and kind in establishing ghulūl and its consequences with regard to the Prophet. Do you not see His words: «عفا الله عنك لم أذنت لهم» ("Allah pardon you; why did you permit them?"), where He began with pardon for the Chosen One; had He not begun with it, his heart would have been rent.
5- The antithesis (ṭibāq) between «الرضوان» (pleasure) and «السخط» (anger).

dervis-irab:165-165.t:
* I'rab:
(أَوَلَمَّا أَصابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ) The hamza is interrogative of denial and rebuke; the wāw is a conjunction on what preceded of the story of Uḥud.
