The meaning is: it is not fitting for you to be astonished at your failure, for you know the cause, and when the cause is known, astonishment is void. «لما» is a temporal adverb meaning "when", attached to «قلتم», or it is a linking particle (ḥarf); its rule will come under Benefits. «أصابتكم» is a past verb and a direct object, and «مصيبة» is the agent. (قَدْ أَصَبْتُمْ مِثْلَيْها) The clause is an adjective of «مصيبة»; «قد» is a particle of confirmation; «أصبتم» is a verb and an agent; «مثليها» is a direct object. (قُلْتُمْ أَنَّى هذا) The clause «قلتم» has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; «أنى» is an interrogative noun, a fronted khabar, and «هذا» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative as the content of what is said. The meaning: "From where has this defeat and killing come upon us, while we fight in the way of Allah, the Messenger of Allah is with us, and Allah has promised us victory over them?" (قُلْ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ أَنْفُسِكُمْ) The clause «قل» is the content of the saying; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «من عند أنفسكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, the khabar. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) «إن» with its noun and khabar; «على كل شيء» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قدير»; and the clause is causal and has no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
1- Ibn Hishām cited this verse in the Mughnī as evidence that the hamza enters upon negation as it enters upon affirmation. This is a slip on his part that we did not expect from so intelligent a man, because «لما» here is temporal ("when"), not negative, so it is not suitable as an example of the hamza's entering upon negation. Nor can it be said that the hamza is for denial, which is like negation, so the speech it enters upon is also negated and the example is sound; for we say: the denial here is one of rebuke, so what it governs is established, as you say to one who strikes his father: "Do you strike him when he is your father?" It is better to acknowledge that the word «لما» was confused for Ibn Hishām; perhaps he meant the negative «لما». Al-Suyūṭī noticed this error and said: "It is better to give as the example the poet's words: «فقلت: ألما أصح والشيب وازع»" ("I said: Have I not yet awakened, while grey hair restrains?"). This is one of Ibn Hishām's minor slips that we have recorded against him; and glory to Him who does not err. Al-Damāmīnī said in his commentary on the Mughnī: "It is better to take what the hamza governs as omitted, being what is conjoined to, that is: 'Did you not lament, or did you say, when a calamity struck you...', and the author would be exemplifying the negation mentioned and the omitted element." He said: "If you say, the author does not hold this, as will come, but holds that the hamza that enters upon what the wāw governs was fronted to signal its original claim to the beginning of the sentence, as will come, how then can his words be taken as you mention? I say: the author did not mention this regarding the hamza of denial, as in «أفأمن أهل القرى» and «أفلم يسيروا», or he exemplified according to the view of al-Zamakhsharī and those who followed him."
2- «لَمَّا» has three uses:
a- It is specific to the imperfect, which it jussivises and turns to the past like «لم», but its negation continues up to the present, unlike «لم».
b- It is specific to the past. The grammarians disagreed about it: one group said it is an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīna); another group said it is a particle for linking two clauses, both of which are needed, as in «لما جاءني أكرمته» ("When he came to me I honoured him").
c- It is a particle of exception, entering upon the nominal clause, as in «إن كل نفس لما عليها حافظ» ("There is no soul but has over it a guardian"); the discussion of it will come in its place.
3- «قد» is a particle of expectation, because it is joined to verbs that are expected and asked about. Therefore it is said: when it enters upon the past it is a particle of confirmation, and when it enters upon the imperfect it is a particle of reduction (taqlīl); the meaning of its reduction is bringing it close to the present. From this is the Exalted's saying: «قد يعلم الله المعوقين منكم» ("Allah already knows those among you who hinder others"). It may also depart from its place and come as a noun meaning "enough" (ḥasb); you say «قدك», that is, «حسبك» ("enough for you"). Abū Tammām said:
قدك اتّئب أربيت في الغلواء ... كم تعذلون وأنتم سجرائي
(Enough, be gentle; you have exceeded in excess; how long will you blame me, while you are my companions?)

dervis-irab:33-34.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نوح) A foreign (non-Arabic) proper name with no derivation; it is also said that it is derived from النوح ("wailing"). It is fully declinable in any case, because it is a foreign proper name of three letters with a silent middle letter. (عمران) Also a foreign proper name, a diptote; and even if it is said to be Hebrew, derived from العمر, it is still barred from full declension because of being a proper name and the addition of the ألف and the نون.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفى آدَمَ وَنُوحاً) إن and its noun; and the clause اصطفى آدم ونوحا is the khabar. (وَآلَ إِبْراهِيمَ وَآلَ عِمْرانَ) Conjoined to آدم. (عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اصطفى, and the clause is resumptive. (ذُرِّيَّةً بَعْضُها مِنْ بَعْضٍ) ذرية is a badal (substitute) for آدم and what is conjoined to it, or for the two "families", i.e. the two families are a single progeny; it may also be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the operator in it being «اصطفى».
And بعضها is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and من بعض a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate), and the clause is an adjective of ذرية. (وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ) The واو is resumptive; الله is the mubtadaʾ; and سميع عليم are two khabars for it.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the verse is the art of tawshīḥ (adornment), which, as Qudāma says in Naqd al-Shiʿr, is:
that at the beginning of the speech there is a meaning from which, once known, the rhyme-word is known, if it is poetry, or the saj' (rhymed prose) ending, if it is prose. For the meaning of the choosing of those mentioned in the verse makes the verse-ending known, because those mentioned are a class included within «العالمين».
In this verse there is also the art of barāʿat al-takhalluṣ (skilful transition), for He, glory be to Him, the Exalted, prepared with this verse the way to the narrative of the birth of the Messiah, peace be upon him: He moved on to mention the wife of ʿImrān in order to relate the story of her carrying Maryam and Zakariyyā's guardianship of her, and mention of his son Yaḥyā, and the story of Maryam's carrying the Messiah, and the dazzling signs and profound lessons that came in between.

dervis-irab:35-36.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُحَرَّراً) freed, set apart exclusively for the service of the Holy House (Bayt al-Maqdis). It is related that Ḥanna, which was her name, was barren and had borne no child until she grew old. While she was in the shade of a tree, green and leafy, she caught sight of a bird feeding its chick; her soul stirred toward a child and she longed for one, and she said:
"O Allah, I owe You a vow: if You grant me a child, I will give it in charity to the Holy House, so that it will be among its attendants." Then she conceived Maryam, and ʿImrān died while she was pregnant with Maryam.

* I'rab:
(إِذْ قالَتِ امْرَأَتُ عِمْرانَ) إذ is an adverbial of past time attached to an omitted «اذكر» ("remember"), and the sentence is resumptive, put forward to affirm the choosing of the family of ʿImrān; and the clause قالت امرأة عمران is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it. Some attached it to His saying «سميع عليم», and there is nothing that bars that. (رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لَكَ ما فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّراً) رب is a vocative annexed to the first-person ياء, which is omitted, as shown by the kasra on it; إن and its noun; the clause نذرت is its khabar; and the clause إني نذرت is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl); لك are attached to نذرت; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; في بطني is attached to an omitted element that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; and محررا is a ḥāl of «ما». (فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّي) The فاء is resumptive; تقبل is an imperative verb whose agent is "you"; and مني is attached to تقبل. (إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ) إن and its noun; أنت is either a mubtadaʾ or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position; and السميع العليم is the khabar of إن, or of أنت, in which case the nominal sentence is the khabar of إن; or they are two khabars of إن; and the clause إن with what is in its scope is a causal clause (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. (فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْها قالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعْتُها أُنْثى) The فاء is resumptive; لما is an adverbial of time ("when") or a particle of connection; وضعتها is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; the clause قالت has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; رب is a vocative annexed to the omitted first-person ياء; إن and its noun; the clause وضعتها is the khabar of إن; أنثى is a confirming (muʾakkida) or an explanatory (mubayyina) ḥāl, and the difference between them will come; and the vocative clause is the content of what is said. (وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما وَضَعَتْ) The واو is parenthetical; الله is the mubtadaʾ and أعلم the khabar; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعلم; and the clause وضعت has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما. (وَلَيْسَ الذَّكَرُ كَالْأُنْثى) The واو is a conjunction; ليس is a defective past verb and الذكر is its noun; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar; or the كاف is a noun and is the khabar, and الأنثى is the muḍāf ilayhi. (وَإِنِّي سَمَّيْتُها مَرْيَمَ) The واو is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to the clause «إني وضعتها»; إن and its noun; the clause سميتها is its khabar; the هاء is the first object of سميت and مريم its second object. (وَإِنِّي أُعِيذُها بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَها مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ الرَّجِيمِ) The واو is likewise a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to the clause «إني سميتها»; إن and its noun; the clause أعيذها is the khabar of إن and the هاء is a direct object; بك is attached to أعيذها; وذريتها is conjoined to the هاء, or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment); من الشيطان is attached to أعيذها; and الرجيم is an adjective of الشيطان.

* Rhetoric:
1- The purpose of the report in her saying «إني وضعتها» is lament; she does not mean to inform in its plain sense, because Allah knows what she bore, but rather to show grief over what she missed of fulfilling her promise and keeping what she had bound herself to, and to excuse herself since she brought a child not fit for carrying out what she vowed.
2- إن is repeated four times. In the first three its khabar was a past verb, and in the fourth she turned from the past to the imperfect, saying: أعيذها, for a rhetorical point, namely the continuity of seeking refuge and its renewal without interruption, unlike the earlier reports, which came to an end.
3- What is meant by the report in the saying of the Exalted, relating from Himself, «والله أعلم بما وضعت» is lāzim al-fāʾida (the implied benefit of the report), and the aim is to convey it without explicitly stating what will become of the newborn, whom she did not heed at first, being ignorant of the outcome of the affair of this newborn who will bear the messenger of mercy and peace.
4- What is meant by the report in His saying «وليس الذكر كالأنثى» is the negation of the belief prevailing among people that there is a difference among children, and that this difference which appears at first glance is only a superficial matter that does not hold up under trial and experience; for the unseen is deeper than they can fathom and farther in reach than they can grasp; and how many women have surpassed men and exceeded them in rank. Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī clung to the hem of this wonderful meaning in his words:
ولو كان النساء كمن فقدنا ... لفضلت النساء على الرجال
وما التأنيث لاسم الشمس عيب ... ولا التذكير فخر للهلال
(If women were like those we have lost, women would have been preferred over men. Femininity in the name of the sun is no fault, nor is masculinity a boast for the crescent.)
5- Iṭnāb (elaboration) in His saying: «وإني سميتها مريم». The purpose of stating the naming outright is, first, to draw near to Allah and approach Him through service of the Holy House; second, hope for her protection; and third, to show her resolve to fulfil her promise, as if to say: even if she is not fit for attendance, I hope she will be among the devout, obedient women. For Maryam in their language means "the worshipper". The author of al-Munjid neglected to point that out in his book «المنجد».

* Benefits:
The ḥāl is divided into explanatory (mubayyina) or founding (muʾassisa), which is the one whose meaning cannot be gained without mentioning it, such as جاء علي راكبا ("ʿAlī came riding"), since the meaning of riding is not gained except by mentioning راكبا.
And confirming (muʾakkida), which is the one whose meaning is gained without mentioning it. It is either confirming its operator in wording and meaning, as in «وأرسلناك للناس رسولا» and «فتبسم ضاحكا»; or confirming its owner, as in «لآمن من في الأرض كلهم جميعا», where جميعا is a ḥāl of the agent of آمن, which is the relative «من», confirming it; or confirming the content of a preceding sentence formed of two definite, inert nouns, as in «هو الحق بينا», and the poet's saying:
أنا ابن دارة معروفا بها نسبي ... وهل بدارة يا للناس من عار
(I am the son of Dāra, my lineage being known by her; and is there, O people, any shame in Dāra?)
So if you make «أنثى» a ḥāl of the pronoun, it is confirming; and if you make it a ḥāl of "the soul/person" (النسمة والنفس) understood from the context, it is explanatory.

dervis-irab:37-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كَفَّلَها), with a doubled فاء, i.e. "He made him her guarantor and joined her to him and made him her guardian and the one answerable for her welfare." This meaning is supported by the reading «وأكفلها» (with a hamza), in respect of his being the husband of her maternal aunt, and that by way of drawing lots.
(الْمِحْرابَ) And المحرب is an instrument of war; this is the morphological analogy.
But المحراب has independent meanings that do not enter the derivational analogy. Among its meanings are the front part of a house and its most honoured places; the front of an assembly; the lair of a lion; and the mihrab of a mosque. The scholars of language hold that the mosque's miḥrāb is so called because the worshipper in it fights Satan, which is why it is said that every place of worship has a miḥrāb. The researcher is perplexed and astonished at the case of this noble language: how did it develop? What interactions of time contributed to this development? One who follows its linguistic material marvels at how this dynamic development was prepared for it, one which needs an incalculable span of time. The letters ح and ر originally indicate heat and burning, and if we followed all the other roots we would see that every word beginning with them indicates a meaning almost extracted from this meaning or branching from it.
Let us now survey the root ح-ر-ب: it is burning in every blazing sense; and الحرب with two fatḥas is destruction, which follows from burning and is entailed by it. Abū Tammām said:
لما رأى الحرب رأي العين توفلس ... والحرب مشتقة المعنى من الحرب
(When Tawfalis saw the war with his own eyes... and war is derived in meaning from burning.) [Translator's note: the second hemistich is reproduced as printed in the source, with the two words الحرب (war) and الحرب (spoliation/burning) shown identically.]
And حرث الأرض ("ploughing the land") is splitting it with the ploughshare, and this is related to the original meaning by the closest of connections; الحرج is narrowness; and حرد الرجل, with kasra on the راء, means "the man became angry", so he is حارد and حردان, a colloquial word that is eloquent. And so on to the end of the root, where it ends in this wonderful conclusion.

* I'rab:
(فَتَقَبَّلَها رَبُّها بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ) The فاء is a conjunction; تقبل is a past verb and the هاء a direct object; ربها is the agent; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تقبلها; and حسن is an adjective. (وَأَنْبَتَها نَباتاً حَسَناً) The واو is a conjunction; أنبتها is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; نباتا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and حسنا an adjective. (وَكَفَّلَها زَكَرِيَّا) The واو is a conjunction; كفل is a past verb, the هاء is the first direct object and زكريا the second direct object, i.e. "He made Zakariyyā her guardian and guarantor of her welfare"; and in the reading with a light فاء, Zakariyyā is the agent. Legends have been woven around this guardianship; refer to the longer works for them. (كُلَّما دَخَلَ عَلَيْها زَكَرِيَّا الْمِحْرابَ) كلما is an adverbial of time whose i'rab was given many times, attached to وجد because it is the apodosis. The clause دخل عليها is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it, and المحراب is a direct object by way of extension (ʿalā l-ittisāʿ), or accusative by removal of the preposition. (وَجَدَ عِنْدَها رِزْقاً) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; عندها is an adverbial attached to وجد; رزقا is a direct object; and the conditional clause is resumptive. (قالَ يا مَرْيَمُ أَنَّى لَكِ هذا) The clause is resumptive, and this is the soundest of what has been said about it, despite the severe disagreement which is fruitless. قال is a past verb and the agent is "he"; يا is a vocative particle; مريم is a vocative, a single proper noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma; أنى is an interrogative noun in the sense of كيف, as though a question about manner, i.e. "how was the arrival of this provision to you made possible?" Al-Kumayt said:
أنى ومن أين آبك الطرب ... من حيث لا صبوة ولا طرب
(How, and from where did delight come back to you, from a place where there is neither youthful passion nor delight?)
It is also said that its meaning here is "from where" (من أين). In both cases it is accusative as an adverbial, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; لك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and هذا is a postponed mubtadaʾ. (قالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ) The clause is resumptive; هو is the mubtadaʾ and من عند الله is attached to an omitted khabar. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ) إن and its noun; the clause يرزق is the khabar; من is a relative noun, a direct object; the clause يشاء has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative; بغير حساب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يرزق; and the clause إن الله is also part of the content of what is said, if it is her speech, or else is resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse are arts to which we point as follows:
1- Jinās mughāyir (paronomasia of differing forms) in His saying «فتقبلها ربها بقبول حسن», in His saying «فأنبتها نباتا حسنا», and in His saying «رزقا» and «يرزق».
2- Ishāra (allusion), which is expressing by an overt word the hidden meaning, in «هو من عند الله», i.e. it is a provision that none but Allah brings at that time.
3- Indefiniteness (tankīr) in His saying «رزقا» to convey commonness and abundance, and that it was not of a single kind but of many kinds.

dervis-irab:11-11.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الدأب): a maṣdar of "daʾaba fī al-ʿamal" (of the pattern qaṭaʿa), when he toiled in it; its use came to prevail for habit and state of affairs. Of it is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
كدأبك من أم الحويرث قبلها ... وجارتها أمّ الرباب بمأسل
(Like your habit with Umm al-Ḥuwayrith before her, and her neighbour Umm al-Rabāb, at Maʾsal.)

* I'rab:
(كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ): the kāf is a noun meaning "like", in the nominative position as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "the habit of these is like the habit of those before them". You may also make the kāf a preposition, so that the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of that omitted mubtadaʾ. It is also possible for the position of the kāf and what follows it to be accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq or a ḥāl, as has often preceded. «آل» is a muḍāf ilayhi, and «فرعون» is also a muḍāf ilayhi, genitive with the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote on account of being a proper name and foreign.
(وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction joined to «آل فرعون»; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element which has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun.
(كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا): a verb and agent; «بآياتنا» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «كذبوا»; the clause is explicative, with no position. You may also parse the wāw as resumptive, in which case «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause «كذبوا».
(فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «أخذهم الله» is a verb, direct object and agent; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «أخذهم», in which case the bāʾ is causal, or to an omitted ḥāl, in which case the bāʾ is of accompaniment, i.e. "burdened with their sins".
(وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ): a resumptive clause, brought to affirm the punishment; the wāw is resumptive, «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and «شديد العقاب» is its khabar.

dervis-irab:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): a resumptive clause, brought as a reply to the Jews who became stubborn after the battle of Badr and said to the Prophet ﷺ, who had sought to spare their blood by warning them of the consequences of conceit and recklessness: "Do not think that we are the same as people of no experience in fighting." «قل» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun referring to the Prophet ﷺ, that is, "you". «للذين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قل»; the clause «كفروا» has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun.
(سَتُغْلَبُونَ): the sīn is a particle of futurity; «تغلبون» is a passive imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʾil; the clause is in the accusative position as the content of the saying.
(وَتُحْشَرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the clause «تحشرون» is conjoined to «ستغلبون», falling within the scope of the saying.
(إِلى جَهَنَّمَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تحشرون»; «جهنم» is genitive with a fatḥa because it is a diptote on account of being a proper name and feminine; it will be discussed elsewhere.
(وَبِئْسَ الْمِهادُ): the wāw is a conjunction and the clause is conjoined to what precedes, falling within the scope of the saying. It is also possible that the wāw is resumptive and that the clause is brought to deter them and to make Gehenna fearsome to them. «بئس» is a rigid past verb for the formation of blame; «المهاد» is the agent of «بئس»; and the one specified for blame is omitted, its implied form being "Gehenna", and it was omitted only because the meaning is understood. This supports the position of Sībawayh, which is to parse the one specified for blame or praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the preceding clause; the position of others is that it is a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, to which it is objected that this requires the omission of an entire clause without anything remaining to indicate it, which is categorically impermissible, because omitting a single word is lighter than omitting a clause.

dervis-irab:13-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
al-Fiʾa: a group, with no singular from its own wording; its plural is "fiʾāt", and it may also be pluralised with wāw and nūn to compensate for what is lacking. A group is called "fiʾa" only because one "yufāʾu ilayhā", that is, returns to it in time of hardship. Al-Zajjāj said: al-fiʾa is the division, taken from their saying "faʾawtu raʾsahu bi-l-sayf", meaning I cut his head with the sword.
(العبرة): being admonished (ittiʿāẓ); from it one says "iʿtabara", which is taking evidence from one thing for another that resembles it. Its derivation is from "ʿubūr", which is the passing of one thing to another; of it is "ʿibr al-nahr" (with fatḥa on the ʿayn), which is its bank, and "al-miʿbar", the boat, and "al-ʿibāra", by which meanings are carried across to the one addressed; and "ʿabartu al-ruʾyā" (lightly or with doubling) means that you transferred what you have of its knowledge to the dreamer or to another who does not know it. Taking a lesson (iʿtibār) is thus a movement from the station of ignorance to the station of knowledge. Of it too is "al-ʿabra" (with fatḥa on the ʿayn), which is the tear, because it passes beyond the eye.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ كانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ): the clause falls within the scope of the preceding saying, i.e. "Say to the Jews: you will be overcome", and "Say to them: there has been…". It was also said that it is general and that the address is to all the unbelievers, in which case it is resumptive, or to all the believers, and that the lesson is not restricted to anyone. «قد» is a particle of confirmation; «كان» is a defective past verb; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted preposed khabar of «كان»; «آية» is its postposed noun.
(فِي فِئَتَيْنِ الْتَقَتا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of «آية»; the clause «التقتا» is an adjective of «فئتين»; the tāʾ is the feminine tāʾ, vowelless and given a fatḥa to suit the alif of the dual, which is the agent. That encounter took place on the day of Badr.
(فِئَةٌ تُقاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): «فئة» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "one of them is a group"; «فئة» may also be genitive as a badal from «فئتين», and it is one of the readings. The clause «تقاتل» is an adjective of «فئة», and «في سبيل الله» is attached to «تقاتل».
(وَأُخْرى كافِرَةٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «أخرى» is conjoined to «فئة», and «كافرة» is an adjective. Whoever read the first in the nominative reads it in the nominative, and whoever read the first in the genitive reads it in the genitive.
(يَرَوْنَهُمْ مِثْلَيْهِمْ رَأْيَ الْعَيْنِ): the clause «يرونهم» is an naʿt of the group that fights in the way of Allah, namely the Prophet and his Companions. «يرونهم» is a verb, agent and direct object; the seeing is visual, or equivalent to it because of the closeness of the engagement. «مثليهم» is a ḥāl, and «رأي العين» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq giving emphasis to its operator.
(وَاللَّهُ يُؤَيِّدُ بِنَصْرِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ): the wāw is resumptive; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يؤيد» is the khabar; «بنصره» is attached to «يؤيد»; «من» is a relative noun, direct object; the clause «يشاء» has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun.
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِأُولِي الْأَبْصارِ): the clause is resumptive, brought to urge taking a lesson. «إن» is a particle resembling the verb; «في ذلك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted preposed khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «عبرة» is the postposed noun of «إن»; «لأولي» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of «عبرة», its sign of genitive being the yāʾ because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; «الأبصار» is a muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains the loftiest rhetorical features, among them:
1- Iḥtibāk, which is omission from two opposed statements, each of which indicates what was omitted from the other. In His saying «فئة تقاتل في سبيل الله وأخرى كافرة» there is omission from the two statements, and the implied form is: "a believing group fighting in the way of Allah, and another group, unbelieving, fighting in the way of Satan". Thus He omitted from the first what is understood from the second, and omitted from the second what is understood from the first.
2- Directed speech (al-kalām al-muwajjah): the meaning is either such that only one thing is understood from it, admitting no other, or such that it admits that and another, and that other is either an opposite or not. This verse admitted two differing meanings, and the difference is one of opposites, since the seeing of numerical superiority could be by the Muslims or by the polytheists at one and the same time, and there is nothing to favour one over the other, because either may validly be taken in the verse. An example of directed speech has come in the Hadith, the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «إذا لم تستح فاصنع ما شئت» ("If you have no modesty, do as you wish"). This comprises two opposed meanings: one, that the intent is "if you do not do an act of which you would be ashamed, do as you wish"; the other, that the intent is "if you have no modesty to restrain you from doing what one ought to be ashamed of, do as you wish". These are two opposed meanings, one praise and the other blame.

Al-Mutanabbī and directed speech
Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī caught sight of this lofty sky and exploited it in his panegyrics to Kāfūr, the Ikhshīdid ruler in Egypt. He was compelled to flatter him in order to avoid harm if he confronted him with the contempt he harboured, so he inclined to him in panegyrics whose outward form was praise and whose inner meaning was satire. Of that is his saying about him:
وأظلم أهل الظلم من بات حاسدا ... لمن في نعمائه يتقلب
(The most unjust of the unjust is he who spends the night envying the one in whose bounty he turns about.)
This verse admits two opposed meanings. One is that the one benefited envies the benefactor, which would be praise. He presented it thus to make Kāfūr think that this is what he intended.
The other is that the benefactor envies the one benefited, to establish a reality rooted in this creature whom the decrees cast up to be a king: he bestows on others, then soon envies them for what they received of his bounty. This is among the most wondrous things that have occurred in poetry, and is among the peculiarities of this astonishing poet. Abū al-Ṭayyib often inclined to this kind of poetry in his panegyrics to Kāfūr, and of that is his saying about him from a poem whose opening is:
عدوّك مذموم بكل لسان ... ولو كان من أعدائك القمران
(Your enemy is censured by every tongue, even if the two luminaries were among your enemies.)
Then he said about him:
ولله سر في علاك وإنما ... كلام العدا ضرب من الهذيان
(Allah has a secret in your loftiness, and the talk of enemies is only a kind of raving.)
فما لك تعنى بالأسنة والقنا ... وجدك طعان بغير سنان
(Why then do you trouble yourself with lance-heads and spears, when your good fortune is a thrust without a blade?)
That is: let your enemies say what they wish and conjecture about the causes that made you a king, for that is among Allah's secrets in His creation: He raises the lowly, enriches the dullard, and provides for the stupid fool. Then he says, addressing him: you did not attain what you attained by your effort and concern but by your luck and good fortune, and in this there is no merit, and the fool and the non-fool are equal in it.

dervis-irab:164-164.t:
* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of confirmation; «من الله» is a verb and an agent; «على المؤمنين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «من». The discourse is resumptive, introduced to confirm the purity of the Prophet ﷺ and to show the error of those who attributed ghulūl to him. (إِذْ بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ) «إذ» is an adverb for past time attached to «من»; the clause «بعث» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; «فيهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «بعث»; «رسولا» is a direct object; «من أنفسهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, an adjective of «رسولا». (يَتْلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ آياتِهِ) The clause is a second adjective of «رسولا»; «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يتلو». (وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ) The two clauses are conjoined to «يتلو»; «الكتاب» is the second direct object of «يعلمهم», and «الحكمة» is conjoined to «الكتاب». (وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) The wāw is circumstantial; «إن» is the lightened form of the heavy «إنّ», rendered inoperative (muhmala), with no effect; «كان» and its noun; «من قبل» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl; «قبل» is an adverb indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of a genitive by «من»; «لفي»: the lām is the distinguishing lām (lām fāriqa); «في ضلال» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, the khabar of «كانوا»; and «مبين» is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is a lofty art of rhetoric known as the art of tajrīd (abstraction): the speaker draws out of a thing that has an attribute another thing like it in that attribute, to emphasise its perfection in it, as if that were more eloquent than being described by the attribute. It has many divisions, which can be consulted in the books of rhetoric, but we point to the most important of them.
1- That it be with the preposition «من». Among its rare instances in prose is the sermon of Abū Ṭālib at the marriage of Khadīja to the Prophet ﷺ, which includes: «الحمد لله الذي جعلنا من ذرية إبراهيم وزرع إسماعيل وضئضي معد» ("Praise be to Allah who made us of the descendants of Ibrāhīm, the seed of Ismāʿīl and the stock of Maʿadd").
2- That it be with the abstracting bāʾ, as in the words of Abū Tammām:
هتك الظلام أبو الوليد بعزة ... فتحت لنا باب الرجاء المقفل
بأتمّ من قمر السماء إذا بدا ... بدرا وأحسن في العيون وأجمل
بأجلّ من قيس إذا استنطقته ... رأيا وألطف في الأمور وأجزل
(Abū al-Walīd tore through the darkness with a might that opened for us the locked door of hope; with one more perfect than the moon of the sky when it appears as a full moon, and fairer and more beautiful in the eyes; with one nobler than Qays when you make him speak in opinion, and subtler and more generous in affairs.)
3- That it be with the abstracting «في». The Exalted said: «لهم فيها دار الخلد» ("For them therein is the abode of eternity"), that is, in Hell, so He drew out of it another abode for emphasis. Abū al-Ṭayyib aspired to it and said:
تمضي المواكب والأبصار شاخصة ... منها إلى الملك الميمون طائره
قد حرن في بشر في تاجه قمر ... في درعه أسد تدمى أظافره
(The processions pass, the eyes fixed on them toward the king whose omen is blessed; they have stalled in a handsome man, in whose crown is a moon, in whose coat of mail is a lion whose claws drip blood.)
For the lion is the one praised himself, but he drew out of him another lion to make his matter dreadful and to stress his being described with courage and boldness.
4- Among the divisions of tajrīd is that a person draws out of himself another person like him in the attribute for which the speech is made, and then addresses him, as in al-Mutanabbī's words:
لا خيل عندك تهديها ولا مال ... فليسعد النطق إن لم تسعد الحال
وأجز الأمير الذي نعماه فاجئة ... بغير قول ونعمى القوم أقوال
(You have no horses to give as gifts and no wealth; so let speech help if circumstance does not. And reward the emir whose favours come suddenly without a word, while the favours of others are words.)
And the beautiful words of Abū Nuwās:
يا كثير النّوح في الدمن ... لا عليها بل على السكن
سنة العشاق واحدة ... فإذا أحببت فاستنن
(O you who wail much over the ruins, not over them but over their inhabitants! The way of lovers is one; so if you love, follow the way.)
His intention is addressing himself, and so he said after them:
ظنّ بي من قد كلفت به ... فهو يجفوني على الظّنن
بات لا يعنيه ما لقيت ... عين ممنوع من الوسن
رشأ لولا ملاحته ... خلت الدنيا من الفتن
(The one I am devoted to thought ill of me, and he shuns me on the strength of suspicions; he spent the night unconcerned by what I met, the eye of one barred from sleep. A fawn: were it not for his beauty, the world would be free of trials.)
And Shawqī said in the modern age:
قم ناج جلّق وانشد رسم من بانوا ... مشت على الرسم أحداث وأزمان
(Arise, commune with Jillaq (Damascus) and seek the traces of those who departed; events and ages have passed over the traces.)
He drew out of himself another person who represents him in poetic gift and the ability to commune with immortal Damascus, which has always stood firm against colonialism. This division is frequent at the openings of poems, but its path is hard and fraught with danger, because the poet may address his patron or his beloved or any addressee with something he dislikes or finds ill-omened, as Jarīr did when he opened a poem in praise of ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwān:
أتصحو أم فؤادك غير صاح ... عشيّة هم صحبك بالرّواح
(Do you awaken, or is your heart not awake, in the evening when your companions were about to depart?)
ʿAbd al-Malik said to him: "Woe to you! What have you to do with this question, son of the loose woman!" Just as Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī got himself deliberately into trouble in his praise of Kāfūr:
كفى بك داء أن ترى الموت شافيا ... وحسب المنايا أن يكنّ أمانيا
(It is enough of an illness that you see death as a cure; and it suffices for deaths that they be wishes.)
Among the wonderful poems into whose verses tajrīd has penetrated is the poem of al-Ṣimma ibn ʿAbd Allāh about his beloved Rayyā, which we cite in full, for in it lovers of literature find solace and consolation:
حننت إلى ريا ونفسك باعدت ... مزارك من ريا وشعباكما معا
فما حسن أن تأتي الأمر طائعا ... وتجزع أن داعي الصبابة أسمعا
فقا ودعا نجدا ومن حلّ بالحمى ... وقل لنجد عندنا أن يودّعا
بنفسي تلك الأرض ما أطيب الربا ... وما أحسن المصطاف والمتربّعا
وليست عشيّات الحمى برواجع ... إليك ولكن خلّ عينيك تدمعا
ولما رأيت البشر أعرض دوننا ... وحالت بنات الشوق يحننّ نزّعا
بكت عيني اليسرى فلما زجرتها ... عن الجهل بعد الحلم أسبلتا معا
تلفّت نحو الحي حتى حسبتني ... وجعت من الإصغاء ليتا وأخدعا
وأذكر أيام الحمى ثم أنثني ... على كبدي من خشية أن تصدّعا
(You yearned for Rayyā, though your own self made your visiting place far from Rayyā, with your two mountain paths together. How is it fine to approach the matter willingly and then despair that the caller of passion has made himself heard? Stop, both of you, and bid farewell to Najd and whoever dwells in the protected land, and say to Najd that it be bidden farewell with us. By my life, that land! How sweet its hills, how fair the summer camp and the spring camp! The evenings of the protected land will not return to you, but let your eyes weep. When I saw people turn away from us, and the daughters of longing came yearning and drawing away, my left eye wept; and when I rebuked it for ignorance after forbearance, both streamed together. I turned toward the tribe until I thought I had hurt my neck from listening; and I remember the days of the protected land, then I bend over my liver for fear that it may split.)
(Translator's note: the verses are given in the source with line breaks that fall mid-verse; the glosses above follow the evident sense.)

* Benefits:
The «إنّ» with kasra on the hamza, which resembles a verb, is lightened and rendered inoperative because its specificity ceases; and a lām called the distinguishing lām enters upon the khabar, as in «إن خالد لمسافر», to distinguish it from the negative «إن». If a verb follows it, it is necessarily inoperative, and this verb must be one of the nawāsikh, that is, kāna and ẓanna and their sisters, and this lām must enter upon these verbs. Some Arabs made it operative in the first case, though rarely, so they said it is permissible to say «إن خالدا لمسافر». For this reason al-Zamakhsharī erred and went against his own book al-Mufaṣṣal when he made it operative in the words of the Exalted «وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين», when he implied its noun as an overt noun, that is, «الشأن» or «الحديث» ("the matter" or "the account"). Al-Jalāl and Abū al-Suʿūd followed al-Zamakhsharī in the error; and glory to Him who does not forget.

dervis-irab:14-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(القناطير): plural of "qinṭār", taken from "qanṭara al-shayʾ" when he made it firm; here it means abundant wealth. The qinṭār differs with the times and the countries. The linguists differed over its nūn: one group said it is part of the root and its pattern is "fiʿlāl" like "qirṭās"; it was also said that it is redundant and that its pattern is "finʿāl". The author of al-Munjid blundered over it remarkably. (الْمُسَوَّمَةِ): an adjective of horses, i.e. marked with a sign by which they are recognised. As for "al-khayl" (horses), there are two views: one, that it is a plural with no singular from its own wording, its singular being "faras"; the other, that its singular is "khāʾil", so it is parallel to "rākib/rakb", "tājir/tajr" and "ṭāʾir/ṭayr". Sībawayh classes it with "qawm", "rahṭ" and "nisāʾ" and makes it a collective noun (ism jamʿ), while others make it a broken plural. The derivation of "khayl" is either from "ikhtiyāl", which is vanity, being so called for their strutting in their gait; or, second, from "takhayyul", because they imagine themselves in a form greater than they are.
(الْأَنْعامِ): plural of "naʿam" (with two fatḥas); "al-naʿam" is a collective noun with no singular from its own wording, which is both masculine and feminine, and is applied to camels, cattle and sheep. More of its discussion will come in Sūrat al-Anʿām.
(الْمَآبِ): it may be a sound maṣdar or a noun of place or time; in any case it is of the pattern "mafʿal" (with fatḥa on the ʿayn) from "āba yaʾūbu", meaning he returned, and its origin is "maʾwab", so the vowel of the wāw was moved to the vowelless hamza before it and the wāw was turned into an alif.

* I'rab:
(زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَواتِ): a resumptive statement with no position, brought to show the insignificance of the goods of this world. «زين» is a passive past verb; «للناس» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «زين»; «حب الشهوات» is the nāʾib fāʾil.
(مِنَ النِّساءِ وَالْبَنِينَ وَالْقَناطِيرِ الْمُقَنْطَرَةِ): «من» is explanatory (bayāniyya), and it with what it governs is attached to an omitted ḥāl. As for «والبنين»: the wāw is a conjunction and «البنين» is conjoined to «النساء», genitive, its sign of genitive being the yāʾ because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; «المقنطرة» is an adjective of «القناطير».
(مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْخَيْلِ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ وَالْأَنْعامِ وَالْحَرْثِ): «من» is also explanatory, and it and what it governs are attached to an omitted ḥāl, and what follows is conjoined to it.
(ذلِكَ مَتاعُ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; «متاع الحياة» is the khabar and «الدنيا» an adjective; the clause is also resumptive, brought to show the insignificance of all that, because it is perishing and does not remain.
(وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الْمَآبِ): the wāw is resumptive and what follows is a resumptive statement, brought to indicate that there is no good in what has been enumerated of the outward forms of bounty, and no benefit. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ; the adverbial is attached to an omitted preposed khabar; «حسن المآب» is a postposed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is the khabar of «الله».

* Rhetoric:
The verse contains the art of mutual consideration (murāʿāt al-naẓīr), which is that the poet or prose writer brings together a matter and what suits it, while omitting mention of opposition, so that antithesis (muqābala) and counterpoint (muṭābaqa) are excluded. In this verse He, glory be to Him, brought together most of the means of luxury that lead a person to immersion in temptation and to being driven by the urges of the unruly self; they have been made attractive to people and have enticed them with marvels and allurements, as a trial for them. The theologians have debates and rounds over the adorning of these desires and the one who adorned them, and disagreement erupts between the Sunnis and the Muʿtazilites, which we have no way of mentioning, for it falls outside the scope of our book; but we content ourselves with alluding to it, so that whoever wishes may return to the known sources.

dervis-irab:15-15.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ): an imperative verb whose agent is "you", i.e. "O Muhammad"; the speech is resumptive, brought to affirm and verify the goodness of what is with Allah and its superiority over the desires of this world.
(أَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذلِكُمْ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation; «أنبئ» is a nominative imperfect verb and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; the kāf is a direct object; «بخير» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أنبئكم», standing in the place of the second object, as will come in the section on Benefits; «من ذلكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خير», the reference being to the kinds of desires mentioned above. The interrogative clause is in the accusative position as the content of the saying.
(لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنَّاتٌ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted preposed khabar; the clause «اتقوا» has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; «عند ربهم» is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl from «جنات», because it was originally an adjective of it and, when put before it, was parsed as a ḥāl; «جنات» is a postposed mubtadaʾ. You may attach the adverbial to what «للذين» is attached to, namely "being established", because it is part of the good; and you may make the speech continuous, not pausing at «ذلكم», in which case «للذين» is an naʿt of «الخير» and «جنات» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ.
(تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): the clause is an adjective of «جنات»; «الأنهار» is the agent of «تجري»; «من تحتها» is attached to «تجري».
(خالِدِينَ فِيها): a ḥāl from «الذين اتقوا»; «فيها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خالدين».
(وَأَزْواجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ): «أزواج» is conjoined to «جنات» and «مطهرة» is an naʿt of «أزواج».
(وَرِضْوانٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ): also conjoined to «جنات».
(وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبادِ): the wāw is resumptive; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ; «بصير» is the khabar; «بالعباد» is attached to «بصير».

* Benefits:
(أنبأ and نبأ) are two verbs that take three objects when they are in the sense of knowing. In the verse, however, it is in the sense of informing, so they take only two. The truth is that the verbs that take three objects are two, namely "arā" and "aʿlama"; as for the remaining five, namely "akhbara", "khabbara", "anbaʾa", "nabbaʾa" and "ḥaddatha", they are in some of their uses joined to "aʿlama", which takes three objects. Of it is the saying of al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza al-Yashkurī:
إن منعتم ما تسألون فمن حدّ ... ثتموه له علينا العلاء
(If you refuse what you are asked, then whoever you have told [that] he has superiority over us…)
This is evidence that it takes three objects: the tāʾ is the first object, the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural and the wāw is the extension of the ḍamma of the mīm, the hāʾ is the second object, and the clause «له علينا العلاء» is a nominal clause in the position of the third object. Understand that well, for it is hard to attain. These five verbs are also used as taking one object by themselves, and reaching the contents of the second and third by means of the bāʾ, as in "ḥaddathtuka bi-amr" (I told you of a matter).

dervis-irab:38-41.t:
* Vocabulary:
(العاقر): one who bears no children, whether man or woman. It is derived from العقر, which is "cutting", because of the cutting-off of offspring.
(الحصور), with a fatḥa on the حاء, is of the pattern فعول, converted from فاعل for intensiveness; he is one who does not approach women though he is able to, or one who is prevented from them, or one who does not desire them and does not come near them. It was then used for anyone who does not take part in play, amusement and frivolity. Al-Akhṭal said:
وشارب مربح بالكأس نادمني ... لا بالحصور ولا فيها بسآر
(Many a drinker, flushed with the cup, kept me company: neither abstinent nor one who leaves a remainder in it.)
(العشي): from the time the sun declines until it sets. It is a singular noun, not a plural as al-Jalāl and Abū Ḥayyān imagined.
(الإبكار), with kasra on the hamza, is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of أبكر in the sense of بكر, then used as a noun; it is from sunrise to the time of forenoon.

* I'rab:
(هُنالِكَ دَعا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُ) هنالك is a demonstrative of place in the position of accusative as an adverbial of place, sometimes used figuratively for time; the لام indicates distance and the كاف is for address; the adverbial is attached to دعا; زكريا is the agent of دعا and ربه its object; and the sentence is resumptive, put forward to point to Zakariyyā's change from his belief about birth and barrenness, i.e. when Zakariyyā saw that, and knew that the One able to bring a thing in other than its time is able to bring a child in old age. (قالَ: رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً) A resumptive sentence, put forward to make real what occurred to him of thoughts after the change of mind that came upon him; قال is a past verb whose agent is a latent "he" referring to Zakariyyā; رب is a vocative annexed to the omitted first-person ياء; هب is an imperative verb; لي is attached to هب; من لدنك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; ذرية is a direct object and طيبة an adjective. The adjective is made feminine for the feminine of the described, because no specific person is intended by it; but if a specific person is intended, then regard to the form is barred, as in طلحة and حمزة. The vocative clause is in the position of accusative as the content of what is said. (إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعاءِ) إن with its noun and khabar; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. (فَنادَتْهُ الْمَلائِكَةُ) The فاء is a conjunction; نادته الملائكة is a verb, an object and an agent. (وَهُوَ قائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرابِ) The واو is a ḥāl-waw; هو is the mubtadaʾ and قائم its khabar; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl of the object of the calling; and the clause يصلي في المحراب may be made a second khabar of هو, or you may put it in the accusative as a ḥāl of "standing"; and في المحراب is attached to يصلي. (أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ بِيَحْيى) أن and what is in its khabar are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نادته. It was also read with kasra on the hamza of «إن», supposing an omitted "saying", so that the clause is the content of the saying and the clause of saying is a ḥāl, i.e. "the angels saying". The clause يبشرك is its khabar and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يبشرك; يحيى is a diptote, because of being a proper name and foreign, if it is foreign, and if it is Arabic, because of being a proper name and the pattern of a verb. (مُصَدِّقاً بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ) مصدقا is a ḥāl, and بكلمة is attached to مصدقا. What is meant by "the word" is ʿĪsā ibn Maryam; he was called a "word" only because Allah the Exalted said to him: "Be", and he was, without a father. There are other opinions about it, for which refer to the longer works. (وَسَيِّداً وَحَصُوراً وَنَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) The three words are conjoined to «مصدقا», and من الصالحين is an adjective of نبيا. (قالَ: رَبِّ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلامٌ) قال is a past verb whose agent is a latent "he" referring to Zakariyyā; رب is a vocative annexed to the omitted first-person ياء; أنّى is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverbial, and the adverbial is attached to an omitted khabar of يكون if it is taken as defective, or is a ḥāl if it is taken as complete; لي is attached to an omitted ḥāl; and غلام is the noun of يكون or its agent; the clause قال is resumptive and the vocative clause is the content of what is said. (وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِيَ الْكِبَرُ) The واو is a ḥāl-waw; قد is a particle of affirmation; بلغني is a past verb, the نون is for protection and the ياء a direct object, and الكبر is the agent; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (وَامْرَأَتِي عاقِرٌ) The واو is likewise a ḥāl-waw; امرأتي is a mubtadaʾ and عاقر a khabar; the clause is a ḥāl from the ياء in «لي», so there are multiple ḥāls; you may also make it a ḥāl from the ياء in «بلغني». (قالَ: كَذلِكَ اللَّهُ يَفْعَلُ ما يَشاءُ) The i'rab scholars and exegetes were unsettled in this verse, and the closest of what appeared to us are two views of equal weight. The first is that the whole sentence is resumptive and the speaker is Allah the Exalted, and «كذلك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "Allah does what He wills of wondrous deeds like that deed", which is the creation of a child from a decrepit old man and a barren old woman; or they are in the position of a ḥāl from the pronoun of the omitted maṣdar of «يفعل», and that is on Sībawayh's school in this question, whose discussion has preceded. الله is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يفعل the khabar; ما is a relative noun in the position of accusative, a direct object; and the sentence is the content of what is said. The second view is that كذلك is attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is thus"; the clause يفعل ما يشاء is in the position of nominative as the khabar of الله; and the clause يشاء has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila. (قالَ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ لِي آيَةً) قال is a past verb and the agent is Zakariyyā; رب is a vocative whose i'rab has preceded; اجعل is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; لي is attached to اجعل; آية is a direct object; the vocative clause and what follows it is the content of what is said, and the clause of saying is resumptive. (قالَ: آيَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ) The clause is resumptive; آيتك is a mubtadaʾ; أن and what is in its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, the khabar; تكلم is an imperfect verb accusative by أن; الناس is a direct object; and the clause is the content of what is said. (ثَلاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلَّا رَمْزاً) ثلاثة أيام is an adverbial of time attached to تكلم; إلا is a particle of discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), the accusative being obligatory because الرمز ("gesture") is not of the genus of speech. You may also consider it of the genus of speech, in which case «رمزا» is an exception from the most general of states or the most general of verbal nouns, i.e. a ḥāl or a mafʿūl muṭlaq; these views are of equal weight in this strange construction. (وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ كَثِيراً) The واو is resumptive; اذكر is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; ربك is a direct object; and كثيرا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq or an adverbial of time, i.e. "much remembrance" or "a long time". (وَسَبِّحْ بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِبْكارِ) The واو is a conjunction; سبح is conjoined to اذكر; بالعشي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to سبح; and الإبكار is conjoined to it.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «رمزا» is the art of ishāra (allusion), whose discussion has been given shortly before, because it points to the stirrings and meanings in the human soul. Poets have clung to the hems of this eloquence. Abū Tammām said:
توحي بأسرارنا حواجبنا ... وأعين بالوصال ترتشق
(Our eyebrows hint at our secrets, and eyes drink in the union.)
And he also said:
كلمته بجفون غير ناطقة ... فكان من ردّه ما قال حاجبه
(I spoke to him with eyelids that do not speak, and his reply was what his eyebrow said.)
And another said:
إذا كلمتني بالعيون الفواتر ... رددت عليها بالدموع البوارد
(When she speaks to me with languid eyes, I answer her with cool tears.)
[Translator's note: in the source, the second Abū Tammām verse and the words «وقال آخر» run together on one line; they are separated here for clarity.]

dervis-irab:42-43.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اصْطَفاكِ): He chose you.
(اقْنُتِي): devote worship purely and maintain obedience.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَتِ الْمَلائِكَةُ) The واو is a conjunction and the sentence is conjoined; for He conjoined the story of the daughter to the story of her mother because of the perfect fit between them. You may conjoin «إذ» to the preceding adverbial and attach it to an omitted «اذكر»; and قالت الملائكة:
a verb and an agent, and the clause is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverbial to it. (يا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفاكِ) يا is a vocative particle; مريم is a vocative, a single proper noun; إن and its noun; the clause اصطفاك is the khabar of إن; and the whole sentence is the content of what is said. (وَطَهَّرَكِ وَاصْطَفاكِ عَلى نِساءِ الْعالَمِينَ) The two verbs are conjoined to اصطفاك; على نساء is attached to اصطفاك; and العالمين is the muḍāf ilayhi. (يا مَرْيَمُ اقْنُتِي لِرَبِّكِ) يا is a vocative particle; مريم is a vocative, a single proper noun; اقنتي is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the dropping of the نون, and the ياء is the agent; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اقنتي. (وَاسْجُدِي وَارْكَعِي مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ) The two imperative verbs are linked to اقنتي; مع is an adverbial of place attached to اركعي; and الراكعين is the muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
1- In these two verses is taqdīm (fronting): prostration, which comes later in the ruling of the prayer, was put first for the sake of giving it importance, and because it shows more humility and worship. This is their habit: putting the more important before the important.
2- In them also is takrīr (repetition): the vocative was repeated to signal that each of the two is put forward for a meaning; the first is a reminder of the favour, serving as a preparation for the second, which is for obligation and encouragement to action.
3- In them also is iṭlāq al-juzʾ wa-irādat al-kull (naming the part and intending the whole), and prostration was put first because it is the most excellent of the pillars of the prayer, as was said before.

dervis-irab:16-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الأسحار): plural of "saḥar", like "faras/afrās": the last parts of the night, so called because of the concealment in them. Saḥar is the time when the night retreats and the day approaches, so it is the breathing of the dawn. The linguists differed over its exact definition. Al-Zajjāj and his group said: it is the time before the rising of dawn; al-Rāghib said in his Mufradāt: saḥar is the mingling of the darkness of the end of the night with the light of day, and then it became a name for that time. As for "saḥr" with sukūn, it is the end of the windpipe's cane. Of it is the saying of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: «The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken between my saḥr and my naḥr» (my lung and my chest). Among the Arabs' figurative usage is their saying "intafakhat masāḥiruh", when he grew weary and cowardly.
(القسط): justice. One says "aqsaṭa", meaning he was just, and "qasaṭa", meaning he was unjust; so it is praise in the quadriliteral form and blame in the triliteral.

* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ): the relative noun may be nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who"; accusative as praise with an omitted verb, i.e. "I praise those who"; or genitive as a badal from the relative noun in the preceding verse, or an naʿt of it. «يقولون» is a nominative imperfect verb through the retention of the nūn, the wāw is the agent, and the clause is a ṣila.
(رَبَّنا إِنَّنا آمَنَّا): the clause is the content of the saying; «ربنا» is the one addressed with the vocative particle omitted; «إن» with its noun, and the clause «آمنا» is its khabar.
(فَاغْفِرْ لَنا ذُنُوبَنا): the fāʾ is for cause, because faith is the cause of forgiveness; «اغفر» is an imperative verb of supplication; «لنا» is attached to it; «ذنوبنا» is a direct object.
(وَقِنا عَذابَ النَّارِ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ق» is an imperative verb of supplication, indeclinable by the dropping of the weak letter, and the wāw of the "mithāl" verb was dropped as is the rule; the agent is "you"; «نا» is an attached pronoun in the accusative position as the first direct object, and «عذاب النار» is the second direct object.
(الصَّابِرِينَ وَالصَّادِقِينَ وَالْقانِتِينَ وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ بِالْأَسْحارِ): «الصابرين» is accusative as praise with an omitted verb, and what follows is conjoined to it. These are originally adjectives cut off from adjectival status by the intervention of the conjunctive wāw between them, to indicate their distinction in the kinds of perfections, as will come in the section on Rhetoric; the clause is resumptive.
(شَهِدَ اللَّهُ): a verb and agent; the clause is resumptive, brought to enumerate the fundamentals of religion and its excellences, about which many hadiths have come.
(أَنَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): «أن» and what follows it are in the accusative position by removal of the preposition, i.e. "bi-annahu"; the preposition and what follows are attached to «شهد». The i'rab of the word of testimony has preceded, so renew your acquaintance with it.
(وَالْمَلائِكَةُ وَأُولُوا الْعِلْمِ): the wāw is a conjunction; «الملائكة» is conjoined to «الله», and «أولو العلم» is also conjoined; it is nominative with a wāw because it is attached to the sound masculine plural.
(قائِماً بِالْقِسْطِ): an inseparable ḥāl from «الله» or from the detached pronoun that falls after «إلا», which is perhaps preferable. The ḥāl may come after two conjoined items when confusion is not feared; if confusion were not safe from, a ḥāl could not come, as in "jāʾa ʿAlī wa-Khālid ḍāḥikan" (ʿAlī and Khālid came laughing), for it is not known who is laughing. It is clear that upholding justice is among the characteristics of Allah the Exalted, so it is a completion of the perfection of acts after the perfection of the Essence. There is an important discussion here which will come in the section on Benefits.
(لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ): its i'rab has preceded.
(الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): two khabars of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "He"; you may also parse them as two badals of «هو».

* Rhetoric:
1- The entry of the wāw upon the attributes although the one described is one is a magnification of the one described, because it is a notification that each attribute independently stands for praise of the one described; and further, the one described is not one, as it appears to the hasty glance.
2- In the last verse there is "returning the end to the beginning" (radd al-ʿajuz ʿalā al-ṣadr): «العزيز» is returned to His uniqueness in oneness, which requires might, and «الحكيم» is returned to justice, which is al-qisṭ; so He the Exalted is wise, and no injustice or deviation touches Him.

* Benefits:
1- The "mithāl" verb whose first radical is a weak letter, when an imperative is formed from it, loses its wāw or yāʾ; so you say of "waʿada": "ʿid". If it is a "lafīf mafrūq", that is, its first and last radicals are weak letters, it becomes a single letter because both letters are dropped; so you say of "waʿā": "ʿi", of "waqā": "qi", of "wafā": "fi", and of "waʾā": "ʾi". On this basis the well-known riddle is explained, with which junior parsers amuse themselves:
إن هند المليحة الحسناء ... وأي من أضمرت لخل وفاء
(In, Hind, the pretty, the beautiful, and wa-ʾi, one who harboured faithfulness toward a friend.)
Its explanation is as follows: «إن» is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the dropping of the weak letter, and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; its meaning is "ʾi: promise", its verb being "waʾā", i.e. "Promise, O Hind, and promise like a woman who has harboured faithfulness for her friend." «هند» is a singular proper-name vocative with the vocative particle omitted, indeclinable on the ḍamma; «المليحة» is an naʿt in wording, and «الحسناء» is a second naʿt of «هند» in meaning; and «وأي» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. We drew attention to its parsing only to show that the later grammarians have laboured matters that it behoves us to avoid, for they spoil taste and disable the artistic faculty, and they are more like tricks.
[Translator's note: the source numbers the next item "3"; there is no item 2 in the text.]
3- The rule for the ḥāl is that it be transient, not fixed, and it occurs as a fixed attribute in three cases:
(a) That it confirms the content of a preceding clause, as in "Zayd abūka ʿaṭūfan" (Zayd is your father, tender), for tenderness is characteristic of fatherhood, and that is derived from the content of the clause; or confirms its operator, as in «ويوم أبعث حيا», for life is inseparable from resurrection, so its meaning is derived without mentioning it.
(b) That its operator indicates the renewal of the essence of its owner and its coming into being, or the renewal of an attribute of it. The first is like their saying «khalaqa Allāh al-zarāfa yadayhā aṭwala min rijlayhā» (Allah created the giraffe, its forelegs longer than its hind legs): «يديها» is a badal of «الزرافة» (part of a whole), «أطول» is an inseparable ḥāl from «يديها», and «من رجليها» is attached to «أطول» because it is a comparative; the operator of the ḥāl is «خلق». The second is like His saying the Exalted «وهو الذي أنزل إليكم الكتاب مفصلا»: the Book is ancient and the sending down is new, i.e. the newness is in the descent, not in the existence.
(c) That it rests on transmission, as in «قائما بالقسط». Some, however, parsed «قائما» as accusative for praise, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
إذا قلت: هاتي نوليني تمايلت ... عليّ هضيم الكشح ريا المخلخل
(When I said, "Give me, grant me," she leaned toward me, slender of waist, her anklet-place full.)
«هضيم» is accusative with an implied "I praise", not a ḥāl, because it is an inseparable attribute. There remains the apology for its placement after the two conjoined items. Al-Taftāzānī said: it is as if to indicate the high rank of the two, that is, the angels and those endowed with knowledge, since they are joined with Him the Exalted without a separator. So take note of this separation, for it has merit over the separations.

dervis-irab:19-19.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلامُ): the clause is resumptive, confirming the first. «إن» and its noun; «عند الله» is an adverbial of place attached to an omitted ḥāl; «الإسلام» is the khabar of «إن». Abū al-Baqāʾ objected to a ḥāl coming after «إن», but that objection is rejected, because they have allowed «ليت», «كأن» and the hāʾ of alerting to operate on a ḥāl, on account of the meanings of wishing, comparison and alerting that these particles contain; and «إن» is for emphasis, so it may also operate on a ḥāl and does not fall short of the «ها» of alerting, but is more fitting than it, since it is an operator whereas the «ها» of alerting is not, so it is closer to resembling the verb than «ها». You may also make it a ḥāl from «الدين», i.e. "being and established with Allah"; and «الإسلام» is the khabar of «إن».
(وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to explain the cause of the disagreement; «ما» is negative; «اختلف الذين» is a verb and agent; the clause «أوتوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «أوتوا» is a passive past verb, the wāw is the nāʾib fāʾil, which is the first object, and «الكتاب» is the second direct object.
(إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ): «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «من بعد» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «اختلف»; «ما» is a maṣdar particle interpreted with what follows as a maṣdar in the genitive position by annexation, i.e. "after the coming of knowledge to them"; «جاءهم» is a verb and direct object, and «العلم» is its agent.
(بَغْياً بَيْنَهُمْ): a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; «بينهم» is an adverbial of place attached to an omitted adjective.
(وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ): the wāw is resumptive; «من» is a jussive conditional noun in the nominative position as a mubtadaʾ; «يكفر» is the protasis; «بآيات الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يكفر».
(فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; «إن» and its noun; «سريع الحساب» is its khabar; the nominal clause accompanied by the fāʾ is in the jussive position as the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من».

* Rhetoric:
This verse comprises kinds of exaggeration in condemning the Jews, as follows:
(a) Describing them as people of the Book: disagreement is in itself ugly, but after the coming of the Book and knowledge of its appearances it is uglier.
(b) Then he advanced in exaggeration, describing them as having, after receiving a Book, been given another knowledge clarifying to them the path of rectitude; but the nature of obstinacy ingrained in their souls refused anything but persistence in error and riding the back of excess, so the ugliness was greater.
(c) Then he advanced once more in exaggeration, making the disagreement after the appearance of knowledge to them, twice in succession, nothing but wrongdoing (baghy) on their part, which is what people have known of them and for which they have been famous to this day; thereby the exaggeration reached its utmost limit. Glory be to the One alone in eloquence.

dervis-irab:166-167.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما أَصابَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعانِ) The discourse is resumptive, introduced to complete the story of Uḥud. The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ; the clause «أصابكم» is the ṣila; «يوم» is an adverb attached to «أصابكم»; and the clause «التقى الجمعان» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The fāʾ is a linking fāʾ because of the faint scent of condition in the relative noun; «بإذن الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "it is by Allah's leave"; and the nominal clause is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the relative noun. «وليعلم»: the wāw is a conjunction and the lām is causal; «يعلم» is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن»; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to what «بإذن» is attached to; the conjunction is of the type of conjoining a cause to a cause. You may also attach them to an omitted verb, the implied form being "He did that so that He might know". «المؤمنين» is a direct object. (وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ نافَقُوا) Conjoined to «ليعلم»; «الذين» is a relative noun, direct object; and the clause «نافقوا» is the ṣila. (وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعالَوْا قاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَوِ ادْفَعُوا) A resumptive discourse, introduced to report that they were commanded either to fight or to defend. You may also make it conjoined to «نافقوا», entering within the scope of the relative noun, that is: "and that He might know those among whom hypocrisy and the said utterance occurred". «قيل» is a passive past verb; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قيل»; the clause «تعالوا» is the content of what is said, and so is the clause «قاتلوا»; both clauses are the deputy agent of «قيل». No conjunction came between them because each of the two clauses is meant to be mentioned in itself. «في سبيل الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قاتلوا»; «أو» is a conjunction; «ادفعوا» is conjoined to «قاتلوا». The object of «ادفعوا» is omitted because it is known, namely the enemy, and repelling him is only by increasing the numbers of the Muslims; the "numbers of the Muslims" (sawād) means their gathering. (قالُوا لَوْ نَعْلَمُ قِتالًا لَاتَّبَعْناكُمْ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive, introduced to express their pretext, their persistence in obstinacy and their riding on the back of error and misguidance. «لو» is conditional; Sībawayh called it "a particle of what was going to happen because of the occurrence of something else". The clause «لو نعلم قتالا» is the content of their saying, because the opinion of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy was to stay in Madīna. The lām falls in the answer to «لو»; «اتبعناكم» is a past verb, an agent and a direct object, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (هُمْ لِلْكُفْرِ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَقْرَبُ مِنْهُمْ لِلْإِيمانِ) The clause is resumptive, introduced to settle their case. «هم» is a mubtadaʾ; «للكفر» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أقرب»; «يوم» is an adverb of time annexed to another adverb, and it is attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl; «أقرب» is their khabar; «منهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أقرب»; and «للإيمان» is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to «أقرب». This is one of the properties of the elative noun (ism al-tafḍīl): two prepositions identical in form and meaning, and another one that is not identical, can be attached to one governing element, because it is equivalent in force to two governors; it indicates two things, the root of the verb and the excess in it, and each of them governs one of the two. (يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ ما لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ) The clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «أقرب», so the meaning is "they were nearer to disbelief in the state of saying this saying". «بأفواههم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يقولون». He stated the preposition and its genitive noun although saying is only by the mouths, because "saying" is applied to the tongue and to the body, so restricting it with «بأفواههم» restricts one of its two possibilities; and it was said that it is merely for emphasis. «ما» is a relative noun, direct object; the clause «ليس في قلوبهم» is the ṣila of «ما»; and «في قلوبهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, the khabar of «ليس». (وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يَكْتُمُونَ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to establish that He the Exalted knows what they conceal of hypocrisy, or what they were plotting in secret; you may also take it as circumstantial. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and «أعلم» the khabar; «بما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أعلم»; and the clause «يكتمون» is the ṣila of «ما».

dervis-irab:168-168.t:
* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ قالُوا لِإِخْوانِهِمْ وَقَعَدُوا) «الذين» is a relative noun, for whose i'rab you have equally valid options. Among them: you may parse it as a badal of the relative noun in the preceding verse, that is, «الذين نافقوا», or of the wāw in «نافقوا»; or you may make it accusative for censure (dhamm) by an omitted verb, the implied form being «أذمّ» ("I censure"), which is common in their speech and indicates embodiment and depiction; or you may make it nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, in which case the sentence is resumptive. The clause «قالوا» is the ṣila; «لإخوانهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قالوا». The wāw may be circumstantial or a conjunction; the clause is either circumstantial from the wāw in «قالوا» with an implied «قد», or conjoined to the clause «قالوا». (لَوْ أَطاعُونا ما قُتِلُوا) «لو» is conditional; «أطاعونا» is a past verb, an agent and a direct object; «ما» is negative; «قتلوا» is a passive past verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent; the clause «ما قتلوا» has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; and the clause «لو أطاعونا» is in the position of an accusative as the content of what is said. (قُلْ فَادْرَؤُا عَنْ أَنْفُسِكُمُ الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) The clause is resumptive. «قل» is an imperative verb; the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, that is, "if your claim is sound, then ward off from yourselves", meaning repel; «عن أنفسكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ادرؤوا»; «الموت» is a direct object; «إن» is conditional; «كنتم» is an incomplete past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, the tāʾ being its noun, and «صادقين» the khabar of «كنتم». The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, that is: "ward off death if you are truthful in your claim that staying behind saves the one who does it". It cannot be said that a person repels the accident from himself before the arrival of the appointed term if he takes the means of protection; that is alarmist talk, which does not agree with the saying of the Exalted: «فإذا جاء أجلهم لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون» ("When their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour nor advance it").

* Benefits:
(لَوْ) in speech is of two kinds: maṣdariyya (verbal-noun forming) and shartiyya (conditional).
a- The maṣdariyya is the one in whose place the maṣdar-forming «أن» would be good; it most often occurs after «ودّ» or what has its sense, as in the saying of the Exalted: «يود أحدهم لو يعمر ألف سنة» ("Each of them wishes he might live a thousand years").
b- The conditional is for suspension in the past, as «إن» is for the future. It follows necessarily from the suspension being in the past that its condition is one whose occurrence is negated, for if it were established the answer would be so too. As for its answer: if it is equal to the condition in generality, as in your saying «لو كانت الشمس طالعة كان النهار موجودا» ("If the sun were rising, the day would be present"), its negation is also necessary; and if it is more general than the condition, as in your saying «لو كانت الشمس طالعة لكان الضوء موجودا» ("If the sun were rising, light would be present"), then the portion of it equal to the condition must be negated. For this reason you hear the grammarians say: «لو» is a particle of impossibility due to impossibility (ḥarf imtināʿ li-imtināʿ), that is, it indicates the impossibility of the answer because of the impossibility of the condition; yet they do not hold that it indicates the impossibility of the answer absolutely, since it can fail, as in «لو ترك العبد سؤال ربه لأعطاه» ("Had the servant left asking his Lord, He would have given him"). They mean only that it indicates the negation of the part of its answer that is equal to the condition. It is better to say: «لو» is a particle of condition that requires the negation of that whose establishment entails the establishment of something else; so it points out that it requires one thing to follow from another and that the thing entailing is negated, without touching on the negation of the entailed absolutely or on its establishment, because that does not follow from its meaning. An interesting discussion will come at His words: «ولو أن ما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام والبحر يمده من بعده سبعة أبحر ما نفدت كلمات الله» ("If all the trees on earth were pens and the sea, with seven more seas to add to it, ... the words of Allah would not run out"); so wait and read the wonders of this noble language.

dervis-irab:169-170.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْواتاً) A resumptive discourse, introduced to inform the Prophet ﷺ and his community of the destinies of the martyrs. Although the speech is specific to the martyrs of Uḥud, generality is not excluded from it; what was said about the martyrs of Badr and what was revealed concerning them, namely His words «ولا تقولوا لمن يقتل في سبيل الله» (the verse), has already gone before. The wāw is resumptive; «لا» is prohibitive; «تحسبن» is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and it is in the position of a jussive by the prohibitive «لا»; its agent is a latent pronoun, implied form "you"; «الذين» is a relative noun, the first direct object; «أمواتا» is the second direct object. (بَلْ أَحْياءٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ) «بل» is a conjunction that conjoins a clause to a clause; «أحياء» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are living".
