It is not the «بل» that conjoins a single word to a single word, because the meaning would be disturbed, as it would become "do not think them living, but ..."; the purpose is rather to announce their life, to encourage jihad and urge it. «عند ربهم» is an adverb attached to «يرزقون»; it is permissible to attach it to an omitted element as a second khabar, and permissible to attach it to an omitted element as an adjective; these options are equally weighted. The clause «يرزقون» is in the position of a nominative as a third or second khabar. (فَرِحِينَ بِما آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ) «فرحين» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يرزقون»; «بما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «فرحين»; the clause «آتاهم الله» is the ṣila of the relative «ما»; «من فضله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «آتاهم»; you may also regard «من» as partitive (tabʿīḍiyya), attaching it with its genitive noun to an omitted element, a ḥāl. (وَيَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ) The clause is conjoined to «فرحين» in sense, so it is a ḥāl, because the resembling adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha) resembles the imperfect; «بالذين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يستبشرون»; the clause «لم يلحقوا بهم» is the ṣila of «الذين»; and «من خلفهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl from the wāw in «لم يلحقوا». (أَلَّا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) «أن» is the lightened form of the heavy «أنّ», and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the interpreted maṣdar of «أن» and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, «بأن لا خوف عليهم», and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «الذين», that is: "and they rejoice at what has become clear to them of the state of those they left behind in the world alive among the believers". The kindling of desire for jihad in this rejoicing is not hidden. «لا» is the lā of generic negation, inoperative; «خوف» is a mubtadaʾ; «عليهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, the khabar; and «ولا هم يحزنون» is conjoined to it. The i'rab of its like has already been given, so we have contented ourselves with what went before.

* Rhetoric:
1- The antithesis (ṭibāq) between «أموات» and «أحياء». It is an antithesis that reached the utmost in depicting the martyrs of the battle of Uḥud and the martyrs who die in the din of jihad. The inflection differs between the two conjoined words in appearance, to indicate that death is an accidental matter followed by stillness, extinction and no renewal of remembrance, whereas the nominative, and making it a nominal sentence, is more eloquent in indicating permanence and the arising and renewal of remembrance every day. Hadiths have been narrated embodying this splendid situation.
2- Murāʿāt al-naẓīr (observing the like), a beautiful and splendid art, which the scholars of rhetoric varied in naming: some called it tanāsub and tawfīq, others called it iʾtilāf and muʾākhāt. Its definition is that the poet or prose writer joins a thing with what suits it, whether the suitability is in wording or in meaning. He the Exalted matched «فرحين» with «يستبشرون», and the absence of fear with the absence of grief, and favour (niʿma) with bounty (faḍl).

dervis-irab:171-172.t:
* I'rab:
(يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ) The verb is repeated for emphasis, and the clause is resumptive, introduced for emphasis; you may also make it an emphasis (tawkīd) of the preceding one or a badal of it. «بنعمة» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يستبشرون»; «من الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, an adjective of «نعمة»; and «فضل» is conjoined to «نعمة». (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; «أن» and its noun; and the clause «لا يضيع» is its khabar. (الَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِلَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ) The relative noun is a mubtadaʾ; you may also make it accusative by an omitted verb for praise, or genitive as an adjective of «المؤمنين». The clause «استجابوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «لله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «استجابوا»; and «الرسول» is conjoined to «الله». (مِنْ بَعْدِ ما أَصابَهُمُ الْقَرْحُ) «من بعد» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl; «ما» is maṣdariyya; «أصابهم القرح» is a verb, a direct object and an agent; and the maṣdariyya «ما» and what is within its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar annexed to «بعد». (لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا مِنْهُمْ وَاتَّقَوْا أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ) «للذين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar; the clause «أحسنوا» is the ṣila; «منهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl; «اتقوا» is conjoined to «أحسنوا»; «أجر» is a postponed mubtadaʾ and «عظيم» an adjective; and the clause «للذين...» is the khabar of «الذين» in His words «الذين استجابوا», if you parse «الذين» as a mubtadaʾ, or it is circumstantial.

The expedition of Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad:
Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger are those who went out with the Prophet ﷺ; they are the believers who took part in the war in the battle of Uḥud. History says: Ḥamrāʾ al-Asad is eight miles from Madīna on the left of the road if you want Dhū al-Ḥulayfa. This expedition was on the morning of Sunday, the sixteenth, or eight days remaining, of Shawwāl, at the head of thirty-two months from the Hijra, in pursuit of their enemy of the day before. The caller of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ announced that no one should go out with us except one who was present with us yesterday, that is, who witnessed the battle of Uḥud. So all who had witnessed it of the sincere believers went out with him, and they were six hundred and thirty. He ﷺ stayed there on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday. They had been struck by the wound because of what befell them at Uḥud, so they hastened, driven by love of vengeance, and strained themselves so as not to miss the reward and so as to achieve the hoped-for aim. Terror seized the polytheists, so they did not rise to fight and did not come out into the field, but remained in Makka, clinging to the hems of fear and escape. Then the Prophet and his Companions returned to Madīna on Friday; his advance against the polytheists took no more than five days.
(Translator's note: in the source, "sixteen days past or eight remaining" is as written; the dating is reproduced as given.)

dervis-irab:179-179.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يذر) and (يدع) are two imperfect verbs whose past forms the Arabs let die out, so only the imperfect and the imperative occur of them; their meaning is "to leave". The scholars of Arabic said: the words ذر and دع both mean leaving, except that دع is a command to the one addressed to leave a thing before knowing it, whereas ذر is a command to leave it after he has come to know it. It is related that one of the imams asked Imam al-Rāzī about the words of Allah the Exalted: «أتدعون بعلا وتذرون أحسن الخالقين» — why was it not said وتدعون أحسن الخالقين, which would be closer to eloquence because of the paronomasia between the two? The Imam said: Because they took the idols as gods and left Allah after they knew that Allah is their Lord and the Lord of their forefathers, out of arrogance; therefore it was said to them وتذرون and not وتدعون. Furthermore, a verbal noun of يدع occurs in the noble hadith, which says: «لتنهين أقوام من ودعهم الجمعات», that is, "from their leaving them (the Friday prayers)".
(يَمِيزَ) is the imperfect of ماز, that is, to set this apart from that.
(يَجْتَبِي) means: chooses and selects.

* I'rab:
(ما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ) A resumptive clause, introduced to explain that Allah the Glorified knows everything and does not leave His servants in their present state of confusion of affairs and obscurity in what they undergo. ما is negative; كان is a defective past verb; الله is its subject (ism); the lām in ليذر is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), which is the one preceded by a negated kawn; it was mentioned earlier. يذر is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an obligatorily implied أن after the lām of denial, which is a preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted predicate of كان, the implication being: "Allah did not intend to leave them in a state of confusion and obscurity". المؤمنين is a direct object (mafʿūl bihi). (عَلى ما أَنْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يذر; أنتم is the subject (mubtadaʾ) and عليه its predicate (khabar); the clause أنتم عليه is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative ما. (حَتَّى يَمِيزَ الْخَبِيثَ مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ) حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; يميز is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after حتى; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted predicate, i.e. "intending to leave them"; الخبيث is a direct object, and من الطيب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يميز. (وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُطْلِعَكُمْ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ) Its i'rab has preceded. (وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْتَبِي مِنْ رُسُلِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ) The wāw is a conjunction; لكن is a particle resembling the verb, meaning rectification (istidrāk); الله is its ism and the clause يجتبي its khabar; من رسله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يجتبي; من is a relative noun, a direct object, and the clause يشاء is the ṣila of the relative. (فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ); آمنوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا, and رسله is conjoined to الله. The clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, namely the one in whose apodosis the fāʾ occurred. (وَإِنْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَتَتَّقُوا فَلَكُمْ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ) The wāw is resumptive; إن is conditional; تؤمنوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and تتقوا is conjoined to تؤمنوا; فلكم: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted predicate; أجر is a postponed mubtadaʾ and عظيم an adjective; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis.

dervis-irab:180-180.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ) A resumptive clause, introduced to begin the censure of miserliness and to establish the recompense of the miserly; you may also make the wāw a conjunction, so that the speech is connected to what precedes. لا is prohibitive; يحسبن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive after لا; الذين is a relative noun, the fāʿil; the clause يبخلون is the ṣila of the relative. (بِما آتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ هُوَ خَيْراً لَهُمْ) بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يبخلون; the clause آتاهم الله is the ṣila of the relative ما; من فضله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آتاهم. The first object of يحسبن is omitted, indicated by the context, namely "the miserliness"; هو is an attached pronoun [Translator's note: the text says "attached", although هو is a detached pronoun] with no position; خيرا is the second object of يحسبن; ولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خير. A pleasing discussion of the reading تحسبن will come in the section on Benefits. (بَلْ هُوَ شَرٌّ لَهُمْ)
بل is a particle of rejection and conjunction; هو is the mubtadaʾ and شر the khabar; ولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شر. (سَيُطَوَّقُونَ ما بَخِلُوا بِهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) The clause is explicative of His words هو شر لهم; you may also make it resumptive, serving as a justification. The sīn is a particle of futurity giving emphasis; يطوقون is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; ما is a relative noun, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with what they were miserly with"; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بخلوا; يوم القيامة is an adverb of time attached to يطوقون, and you may attach it to an omitted ḥāl. (وَلِلَّهِ مِيراثُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) The wāw is resumptive; ولله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ميراث السموات is a postponed mubtadaʾ and الأرض is conjoined to السموات. (وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ) The wāw is resumptive; الله is the mubtadaʾ; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خبير; the clause تعملون is the ṣila of the relative, and خبير is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse:
1- Antithesis (ṭibāq) between خير and شر and between السموات and الأرض; the speech is thus a contrast (muqābala).
2- Shift of person (iltifāt): He moved from the third person to the second in His words تعملون, to increase the deterrence and to confirm the threat and the warning.

* Benefits:
1- It was read ولا تحسبن with tāʾ, in which case nothing is omitted from the speech, because الذين is the first object and خيرا the second. An objection arises against this: the original of the two objects of حسب and its sisters is a mubtadaʾ and a khabar, and that does not appear in the verse because the predication does not hold. The answer to this objection is that the verse is concise, and the implication is: "Do not think that the miserliness of those who are miserly with what Allah has given them, by displaying it, is better for them", and so the speech is completed.
2- Omission of one of the two objects of the verbs of the heart is done for brevity when there is an indication of it. The majority have permitted it and have cited the verse as evidence, and also the words of ʿAntara al-ʿAbsī:
ولقد نزلت فلا تظنّي غيره ... مني بمنزلة المحب المكرم
(You have alighted with me, so think nothing else of me, in the station of the honoured lover.)
The implication is: فلا تظني غيره مني واقعا ("so do not think anything else of me to be occurring"), so the second object was omitted. Some have forbidden it and said: the second direct object is his words مني, which نزلت and تظنّي contend over. In the fifth chapter of Mughnī al-Labīb there is a delightful discussion, which we summarise as follows: It is the habit of the grammarians to say: the direct object is omitted for brevity (ikhtiṣār) and for restriction (iqtiṣār); by ikhtiṣār they mean omission with an indication, and by iqtiṣār omission without an indication, and they exemplify it with كلوا واشربوا, i.e. "perform these two acts", and with the saying of the Arabs:
«من يسمع يخل» that is, "may some suspicion arise in him". The verified position is to say: sometimes the aim is to announce merely the occurrence of the act without specifying who performed it or upon whom it was performed, so its verbal noun is brought, predicated to a general verb of existence, and one says: "a fire occurred" or "a plunder occurred"; and sometimes the aim is to announce merely that the agent performed the act, so one restricts oneself to the two and neither mentions the object nor intends it, since the intended is like the established, and it is not called omitted, because the verb is placed, for this purpose, in the position of one that has no object. Of this are «ربي الذي يحيي ويميت», «وهل يستوي الذين يعلمون والذين لا يعلمون» and «كلوا واشربوا ولا تسرفوا». Until the end of this discussion; refer to it.

dervis-irab:44-46.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَقْلامَهُمْ) الأقلام is the plural of قلم, which is of the pattern فعل in the sense of مفعول, i.e. "cut" (مقلوم). القلم is cutting; likewise القبض and النقض in the sense of "what is seized" and "what is undone".
(الْمَسِيحُ): a title among the noble titles that suggest eminence, like الصديق and الفاروق. In Hebrew it is المشيح, meaning "the blessed". It is said he was called المسيح because of his much travelling; it is also said because his feet were smooth (masīḥ al-qadamayn) with no arch; and it is also said because whenever he stroked someone afflicted with an infirmity, he was healed.
(عِيسَى): an Arabicised form of Īshūʿ; and it is said to be derived from العيس, which is whiteness with a flush of red above it.

* I'rab:
(ذلِكَ مِنْ أَنْباءِ الْغَيْبِ) ذلك is a demonstrative, the mubtadaʾ (subject), and من أنباء الغيب is its khabar (predicate); the sentence is resumptive, put forward to report that all of that, from the tidings of Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā, Maryam and ʿĪsā, peace be upon them, is of the news of the unseen. (نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ) An imperfect verb whose agent is "We", with the هاء a direct object, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to نوحيه; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or likewise resumptive. (وَما كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ) The واو is a ḥāl-waw or resumptive; ما is a negative particle; كان and its noun; and لديهم is an adverbial of place attached to an omitted khabar of كنت, i.e.:
"present with them". (إِذْ يُلْقُونَ أَقْلامَهُمْ) إذ is an adverbial of past time, and its entering upon the imperfect is to relate a past situation; it is attached to whatever «لديهم» is attached to, namely the omitted "being established". Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: the operator in «إذ» is «كنت». That has been objected to on the basis of what he himself established when he said: the defective «كان» is stripped of the indication of the event and left bare for time, so neither the adverbial nor the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to it. The clause يلقون is in the position of genitive by annexation, and أقلامهم is a direct object. (أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ مَرْيَمَ) The clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, by supposing a verb, i.e. "they asked one another"; it is unlikely to make it the agent of an omitted verb because of the artificiality in that, as al-Jalāl did. أي is a mubtadaʾ, the هاء is a muḍāf ilayhi, and the ميم is the sign of the masculine plural; the clause يكفل مريم is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (وَما كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ) The واو is a conjunction; ما is a negative particle; كان and its noun; لديهم is an adverbial of place attached to an omitted khabar of كنت; إذ is an adverbial of past time attached to the omitted "being established"; and the clause يختصمون is in the position of genitive by annexation. (إِذْ قالَتِ الْمَلائِكَةُ) The adverbial is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "remember"; قالت الملائكة is a verb and an agent, and the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation; and the clause of the adverbial and what it is attached to is resumptive, put forward to begin the story of ʿĪsā, peace be upon him. (يا مَرْيَمُ) يا is a vocative particle and مريم a vocative, a single proper noun. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ) The clause is the content of what is said; إن and its noun, and the clause يبشرك is its khabar. (بِكَلِمَةٍ) attached to يبشرك. (مِنْهُ) an adjective of كلمة. (اسْمُهُ الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ) اسمه is a mubtadaʾ and المسيح a khabar, and the clause is a second adjective of كلمة; عيسى is a badal (substitute) for المسيح, and ابن مريم is a badal or an adjective. Maryam is mentioned although she is the one being addressed, to signal that ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, is distinguished by being born without a father, as the custom goes. (وَجِيهاً فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ) وجيها is a ḥāl from كلمة, even though it is indefinite, because it is qualified; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to وجيها, so they are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (وَيُكَلِّمُ النَّاسَ فِي الْمَهْدِ) The واو is a conjunction; يكلم is an imperfect verb and the agent is "he"; the clause is conjoined to «وجيها», so it is also a ḥāl; it turned to the verbal form for renewal; الناس is a direct object; and في المهد is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of «يكلم». (وَكَهْلًا وَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ) Conjoined to His saying «في المهد», i.e. "as a child and as a middle-aged man"; and من الصالحين is conjoined to وجيها, thus completing the four attributes of «كلمة».

* Rhetoric:
Kināya (metonymy) in His saying: «يلقون أقلامهم» for casting lots.

* Benefits:
(إِذْ) occurs in three ways:
[Translator's note: the source prints the numbering as "2-", then a fragment, then "2-" again; the first item (apparently إذ as an adverbial of time) is missing from the printed text, and only the fragment "after it an imperfect verb, so it relates the past situation" survives.]
... after it an imperfect verb, so it is for relating a past situation.
2- It is for causation, and this is a particle in the position of the لام of causation, as in the saying of al-Farazdaq:
فأصبحوا قد أعاد الله نعمتهم ... إذ هم قريش وإذ ما مثلهم بشر
(They found that Allah had restored their favour, since they are Quraysh, and since there is no man like them.)
Adverbial sense is here stripped away and is in no way sound, because the meaning would be spoiled, i.e. "Allah restored their favour at the time of their being Quraysh", which would mean that their being of Quraysh is something that befell them incidentally.
3- It is for surprise (mufājaʾa), and this is the one occurring after «بينا» and «بينما», as in his saying:
استقدر الله خيرا وارضين به ... فبينما العسر إذ دارت مياسير
(Ask Allah to decree good, and be content with it; for while hardship was there, behold, ease came round.)
And then it is preferable that it be a particle.
(أي) occurs in five ways:
1- A jussive-governing conditional noun, parsed according to its position.
2- A relative noun, parsed according to its position, except when it is annexed and the beginning of its ṣila is omitted, in which case it is indeclinable on the ḍamma: «ثم لننزعن من كل شيعة أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا».
3- An interrogative noun, as in the preceding verse, and its ruling is that of the relative.
4- It occurs as an adjective of an indefinite noun or as a ḥāl after a definite noun, to indicate the meaning of completeness and perfection, as in the saying of Abū l-ʿAtāhiya:
إن الشباب والفراغ والجده ... مفسدة للمرء أيّ مفسدة
(Youth, leisure and wealth are a corruption to a man, and what a corruption!)
5- It serves as a means to the vocative of what has «ال»: يا أيها الناس.
(العلم) The proper name (ʿalam) is divided into ism (given name), kunya and laqab (title). When the ism and the laqab are combined, the laqab is put after the ism, and perhaps it is put before it, as in the verse. This is regular when the laqab is better known than the ism; there is no ordering in the kunya. The second is parsed as a badal of the first, and it is permissible to annex the laqab to the ism if they are both single words, like هرون الرشيد and محمد المهديّ.

dervis-irab:47-50.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الأكمه): one who was born blind. It is said كمه كمها (of the pattern تعب), so he is أكمه and the woman كمهاء, like أحمر and حمراء; it is blindness that a person is born with, and perhaps it is incidental.
(الأبرص): one afflicted with البرص, with two fatḥas, a well-known disease that befalls a person. The Arabs shrank from nothing as they shrank from it, so they used to describe a great man when he was afflicted with it as "the radiant" (الوضّاح), and they said Judhayma al-Waḍḍāḥ, who was one of the famous kings of the Arabs. The moon is called أبرص for the intensity of its whiteness, and the gecko is called سام أبرص for its whiteness.

* I'rab:
(قالَتْ: رَبِّ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي وَلَدٌ) Its i'rab was given shortly before, word for word, so renew your acquaintance with it. (وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ) The واو is a ḥāl-waw; لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; يمسسني is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, the نون is for protection and the ياء is a direct object; بشر is the agent; and the clause is a ḥāl. (قالَ كَذلِكِ اللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ) The clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, or a ḥāl; some attached them to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; الله is the mubtadaʾ and the clause يخلق the khabar; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; the clause يشاء has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative; and the clause الله يخلق is the content of what is said. (إِذا قَضى أَمْراً) إذا is an adverbial of future time; the clause قضى is in the position of genitive by annexation; and أمرا is a direct object. (فَإِنَّما يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ) The فاء links the apodosis of إذا; the clause إنما يقول has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional; له is attached to يقول; كن is a complete imperative verb and the clause is the content of what is said; the فاء is resumptive; and يكون is a complete imperfect verb in the nominative with a ḍamma, the agent being "he", and the clause is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «فهو يكون», and the sentence is resumptive. This is Sībawayh's view and it is the sound one. Ibn ʿĀmir read «فيكون» in the accusative, on the basis that the فاء is of causation (sababiyya); and what makes this reading problematic is that futurity is then removed from it. (وَيُعَلِّمُهُ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَالتَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ) The واو is resumptive; you may conjoin it to «وجيها», as if He said: "eminent and a teacher". It was also read «ونعلمه», in which case the clause is the content of an omitted saying because it would be from the speech of Allah. يعلمه is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; الكتاب is the second direct object, and what comes after it is linked to it. (وَرَسُولًا إِلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ) The واو is a conjunction; رسولا is a direct object of an omitted verb, i.e. "and He makes him a messenger", that is, by way of reporting unseen matters. Al-Zamakhsharī and others permitted parsing رسولا as a ḥāl, as if He conjoined it to يعلمه in meaning; and إلى بني إسرائيل is attached to an omitted adjective of «رسولا». (أَنِّي قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِآيَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) أن and what is in its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «بأني قد جئتكم»; it has already been said that this is regular before أنّ and أن. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «رسولا» because it implies the sense of speaking, i.e. "and a messenger speaking that I have come to you". Interpretations of these expressions are many, which is why al-Zamakhsharī made them among the "baffling difficulties". It is also said that the باء is for accompaniment (mulābasa), and it with what it governs is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, the meaning being: "I am Allah's messenger to you, being in the state of accompanying my coming with signs". The clause قد جئتكم is the khabar of أن; بآية is attached to جئتكم; and من ربكم is attached to an omitted adjective of آية. (أَنِّي أَخْلُقُ لَكُمْ مِنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ) أن and what is in its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, a badal of آية, because what he does cannot but be among the proofs of his dazzling signs; you may also make it the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose implied form is "it", and the meaning is one. In one reading, with kasra on the hamza of إن, إن and what follows it is resumptive and the clause أخلق is the khabar of إن; لكم is attached to an omitted element in the position of accusative in the sense of causation, i.e. "for the sake of your guidance", or in the sense of ḥāl, i.e. "guiding you"; من الطين is attached to أخلق; and in كهيئة the كاف is a noun in the sense of "like", so it is in the position of accusative as a direct object, or a particle, in which case it with what follows is in the position of accusative as an adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "something like the form of a bird"; هيئة is a muḍāf ilayhi if it (the كاف) is a noun, and الطير is a muḍāf annexed to هيئة. (فَأَنْفُخُ فِيهِ) The فاء is a conjunction; أنفخ is conjoined to أخلق; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنفخ. (فَيَكُونُ طَيْراً بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) The فاء is a conjunction; يكون is a defective imperfect verb conjoined to أخلق; طيرا is the khabar of يكون and its noun is latent; بإذن الله is attached to يكون according to the view of those who permit a preposition and its genitive noun and an adverbial to attach to defective verbs, or to an omitted ḥāl; the first is closer to the meaning. (وَأُبْرِئُ الْأَكْمَهَ وَالْأَبْرَصَ) Conjoined to أخلق; الأكمه is a direct object. (وَأُحْيِ الْمَوْتى بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) Likewise conjoined to what precedes; and بإذن الله is attached to أحيي. (وَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما تَأْكُلُونَ) Likewise conjoined; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنبئكم, standing in for the two objects; and the clause تأكلون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (وَما تَدَّخِرُونَ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ) The واو is a conjunction; ما is conjoined to the preceding «ما»; the clause تدخرون has no grammatical position; and في بيوتكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تدخرون. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) إن is a particle resembling the verb; في ذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar of إن,
and the لام is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آية is its postponed noun; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of آية; and the clause إن with what is in its scope is either from the speech of ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, so it is within the scope of the saying, or it may be from the speech of Allah the Exalted, in which case it is resumptive.
إن is conditional and كنتم is in the position of jussive as the protasis; كان is a defective past verb, the تاء is its noun and مؤمنين its khabar; the apodosis is omitted, the implied form being "if you are believers, you will benefit from this sign"; and the conditional clause is resumptive. (وَمُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ) The واو is a conjunction; مصدقا is a ḥāl of an omitted verb, i.e. «وجئتكم مصدقا»; or you may conjoin it to the position of «بآية»; in لما the لام is a preposition and ما a relative noun governed by the لام, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «مصدقا»; بين is an adverbial attached to an omitted element having no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما; يديّ is a muḍāf ilayhi, its genitive sign the ياء because it is a dual, and the ياء is a muḍāf ilayhi; and من التوراة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَلِأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ) The واو is a conjunction; the لام is for causation; أحل is an imperfect verb accusative by an optionally implied أن after the لام of causation; the لام and what it governs are attached to an implied «جئتكم». It is not permissible to conjoin it to «مصدقا» because that is a ḥāl while «لأحل» is a reason; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أحل; بعض is a direct object; الذي is a relative noun, a muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause حرم عليكم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (وَجِئْتُكُمْ بِآيَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) The واو is a conjunction, and the clause جئتكم is conjoined to the preceding «جئتكم», repeated for emphasis (tawkīd); بآية is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, so the باء is for accompaniment, the meaning being: "I am a messenger to you, being in the state of accompanying my coming (with it)". You may also attach it to جئتكم; and من ربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of آية. (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ) The فاء is the fāʾ fasīḥa (eloquent fāʾ), i.e. "if you know that, after these dazzling favours with which I have favoured you, it is not permissible for you to be lax in obeying Allah, then fear Allah". اتقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the dropping of the نون, and the واو is the agent; أطيعون is conjoined to اتقوا, and the first-person ياء is omitted to respect the verse-endings.

dervis-irab:51-54.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْحَوارِيُّونَ): the plural of حواري, which is the pick of a man and his purest part; hence settled women (ḥaḍariyyāt) are called ḥawāriyyāt, for the purity of their complexions, their allure and their softness. He said:
فقل للحواريات يبكين غيرنا ... ولا تبكنا إلا الكلاب النوابح
(Say to the fair women: let them weep for others than us; none will weep for us except the barking dogs.)
This relational form (nisba) is almost regular, like الحوالي, which means "the very resourceful".
The author of al-Munjid claimed that the word is Ethiopic, but we prefer that it is purely Arabic.
For in Asās al-Balāgha: "a woman ḥawāriyya and women ḥawāriyyāt" means white women. Al-Akhṭal said:
حوارية لا يدخل الذمّ بيتها ... مطهرة يأوي إليها مطهر
(A fair woman into whose house no blame enters, pure, to whom a pure man repairs.)
Beautiful legends have been woven around the Ḥawāriyyūn, needing a skilful storyteller to fashion from them the most splendid tales.
(المكر) in the language is concealment. It is said مكر الليل, i.e. "the night grew dark and concealed in its darkness what is in it". Its derivation is from المكر, a tangled tree, as though they imagined that guile wraps up the one tricked. And a woman is said to be ممكورة البطن, i.e. "wrapped (of belly)"; then they specialised it to wickedness and deception.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ) A resumptive speech, put forward to establish the root of the religion that follows from belief in what he brought. إن and its noun; ربي is its khabar and ربكم is conjoined to ربي. فاعبدوه: the فاء is the fāʾ fasīḥa, i.e. "if you desire a good destination, then worship Him"; اعبدوه is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the dropping of the نون, the واو is the agent and the هاء a direct object; the clause اعبدوه has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (هذا صِراطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ) The clause may be resumptive or explicative, and in both cases has no grammatical position. هذا is the mubtadaʾ, صراط the khabar and مستقيم an adjective of صراط. (فَلَمَّا أَحَسَّ عِيسى مِنْهُمُ الْكُفْرَ) The فاء is conjoined to an omitted element whose implied form is "so they denied him", because it is a saying arranged upon this omitted element. It may also be parsed as resumptive; لما is an adverbial of time ("when") or a connective, mentioned many times before; the clause أحس عيسى is in the position of genitive by annexation of the adverbial to it, or has no grammatical position if we parse it as a connective. أحس is a past verb and عيسى the agent; منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أحس; and الكفر is a direct object; they may also be attached to an omitted ḥāl from الكفر, i.e. "it proceeding from them". (قالَ مَنْ أَنْصارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ) The clause قال has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional, namely لما; من is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ, and أنصاري its khabar; إلى الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the ياء in أنصاري, the meaning being "who are my helpers while I am proceeding to Allah's way, engaged in contending for it and supporting it?" Al-Zamakhsharī has an interesting view on this preposition and genitive noun, for he made them part of the ṣila of أنصاري, with the sense of annexation implied, as if he said: "who are those who attach themselves to me, helping me as I am helped (by Allah)?" (قالَ الْحَوارِيُّونَ: نَحْنُ أَنْصارُ اللَّهِ) A resumptive clause, put forward to affirm the answer to his question. قال الحواريون is a verb and an agent, and the clause نحن أنصار الله, of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is the content of what is said. (آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ) آمنا is a verb and an agent; بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنا; and the clause is a second khabar of نحن. (وَاشْهَدْ بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ) The واو is resumptive; اشهد is an imperative verb; in بأنا the باء is a preposition, and أن and its noun; مسلمون is its khabar. أن and what is in its scope are a maṣdar in the position of genitive by the باء, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أشهد. This is better than making it a conjunction, so as not to require conjoining an inshāʾ (non-assertive) sentence to a khabar (assertive) one, which is the weaker view. They asked for his testimony to their submission only as a confirmation of their faith. (رَبَّنا آمَنَّا بِما أَنْزَلْتَ) ربنا is a vocative muḍāf; the clause آمنا is a third khabar of نحن; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنا; and the clause أنزلت has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (وَاتَّبَعْنَا الرَّسُولَ) Conjoined to the clause آمنا; and الرسول is a direct object. (فَاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ) The فاء is the fāʾ fasīḥa, i.e. "if the matter is as above, then write us down"; you may also make it resumptive; مع is an adverbial of place attached to اكتبنا; and الشاهدين is a muḍāf ilayhi. (وَمَكَرُوا وَمَكَرَ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْماكِرِينَ) The واو is resumptive; مكروا is a verb and an agent; مكر الله is conjoined to مكروا; والله: the واو is a ḥāl-waw; الله is the mubtadaʾ and خير الماكرين its khabar; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- Allegorical metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) in أحس, for only what is embodied is sensed, and disbelief is not sensed; it is only known and perceived like the knowledge of what is perceived by the senses.
2- The art of muṣākala (verbal correspondence), to which reference has been made. Its reality is mentioning a thing in the wording of another because it occurs in its company, so that it is as if He said: "and He seized them for their scheming", because to Allah the Exalted and Holy no word that suggests ugliness is applied. It is frequent and widespread in the Qur'an, so know it. Among its instances in poetry is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm:
ألا لا يجهلن أحد علينا ... فنجهل فوق جهل الجاهلينا
(Let no one act ignorantly against us, lest we act more ignorantly than the ignorant.)
i.e. "we repay him for his ignorance"; so he put the word فنجهل in the place of فنجازيه for muṣākala. Among the delightful instances of muṣākala is the saying of Abū Tammām al-Ṭāʾī:
والدهر ألأم من شرقت بلؤمه ... إلا إذا أشرقته بكريم
(Time is the meanest of those whose meanness I have choked on, unless I make it choke on a noble man.)
i.e. "I triumphed over it with a noble man"; so he said أشرقته for muṣākala.

dervis-irab:20-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَاجُّوكَ): they disputed with you. One says "ḥājjahu ḥijājan wa-muḥājja", meaning he disputed with him and argued with him.

* I'rab:
(فَإِنْ حَاجُّوكَ فَقُلْ): the fāʾ is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, brought to tighten the noose upon the Jews who had begun to embarrass the Prophet and to plot against him. «إن» is conditional; «حاجوك» is a past verb in the jussive position as the protasis, the wāw is the agent and the kāf the direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis; «قل» is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "you"; the clause accompanied by the fāʾ is in the jussive position as the apodosis. (أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّهِ): the clause is in the accusative position as the content of the saying; «أسلمت» is a verb and agent, «وجهي» is a direct object, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «أسلمت».
(وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِ): the wāw is for conjunction or for accompaniment; «من» is a relative noun conjoined to the tāʾ in «أسلمت» or a mafʿūl maʿahu; the clause «اتبعن» is the ṣila of the relative noun; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the first person has been dropped in pause and in connected speech, in agreement with the orthography. What made that fine is that it is a rhyme-ending (fāṣila) and the head of a verse. Its like will come, such as «أكرمن» and «أهانن». Some grammarians said: it is dropped only with the protective nūn, and if there is no nūn there, retaining it is more frequent. This yāʾ is, however, retained in some of the seven readings.
(وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «قل» is an imperative verb; «للذين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قل»; the clause «أوتوا الكتاب» is a ṣila, the wāw is the nāʾib fāʾil and «الكتاب» is the second direct object.
(وَالْأُمِّيِّينَ): conjoined to «الذين أوتوا الكتاب», genitive with the sign of genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. By them is meant the polytheists of the Arabs, even though they wrote and read, because no book had yet been sent down to them.
(أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ): the interrogative clause is in the accusative position as the content of the saying, and the meaning of the question is censure and reproach, as will come in the Rhetoric.
(فَإِنْ أَسْلَمُوا فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا): the fāʾ is resumptive; «إن» is conditional; «أسلموا» is a past verb in the jussive position as the protasis; the fāʾ links the apodosis; «قد» is a particle of confirmation; «اهتدوا» is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and the wāw is the agent; the accompanied clause is in the jussive position as the apodosis.
(وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّما عَلَيْكَ الْبَلاغُ): the clause is conjoined to the first clause; «إنما» is a restraining particle and what is restrained; «عليك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted preposed khabar; «البلاغ» is a postposed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is in the jussive position as the apodosis.
(وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبادِ): the wāw is resumptive; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ, «بصير» a khabar, and «بالعباد» is attached to «بصير».

* Rhetoric:
1- Mursal metonymy (al-majāz al-mursal) in His saying «أسلمت وجهي», expressing the whole by its noblest part, the face; the relation here is totality.
2- The interrogative in His saying «أأسلمتم» means censure and reproach, as if he had exhausted his effort in advising them and left no means unused to make them understand, yet they did not understand. In this kind of interrogative there is a charge of feeble-mindedness against their minds and a degrading of their understanding, as though proofs had become with them no proofs at all, and demonstrations the most wasted things they have; so nothing remained for him but to ask them in reproach: "Have you submitted after all this? Or is there no use in striking cold iron?"

dervis-irab:21-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَبِطَتْ): went in vain and was ruined; it is from figurative usage. The original sense of "ḥubūṭ" or "ḥabṭ" (with sukūn) is that cattle eat green fodder, find it unwholesome and perish. Of it is "ḥabiṭa damu al-qatīl" (with kasra on the bāʾ), i.e. the blood of the slain was shed with impunity and rendered void.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ): a resumptive statement, brought to speak of the Jews who lived in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, whose fathers had killed the prophets before, and who today try to imitate their earlier fathers and approve of their deed, and so watch for opportunities to kill the Prophet ﷺ; but Allah nullified their deeds. «إن» and its noun; the clause «يكفرون» is the ṣila of the relative noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يكفرون».
(وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ): the wāw is a conjunction; «يقتلون» is an imperfect verb conjoined to «يكفرون»; «النبيين» is a direct object, accusative with the yāʾ; «بغير حق» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "wrongfully". He restricted the killing in this way although the killing of prophets is never otherwise, to add to the denunciation of them.
(وَيَقْتُلُونَ الَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْقِسْطِ مِنَ النَّاسِ): conjoined to what precedes; «من الناس» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being of them".
(فَبَشِّرْهُمْ بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ): the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis of the relative noun because of the scent of condition in it; the entry of «إن» upon the relative noun does not affect its being a subject for a khabar, so the clause is the khabar of «إن», because the meaning has not changed but has increased in emphasis; that is common in the Qur'an and in Arabic poetry. He said:
فو الله ما فارقتكم قاليا لكم ... ولكن ما يقضى فسوف يكون
(By Allah, I did not leave you out of hatred of you, but what is decreed will surely come to be.)
But if «ليت» or «لعل» enters upon «الذي», the entry of the fāʾ is barred because the khabar quality is abrogated and the speech turns to a performative that admits neither truth nor falsehood, as is established in the science of ʿilm al-maʿānī; and an important discussion of the secrets of the letters will come in the section on Benefits. «بشرهم» is an imperative verb, the hāʾ is a direct object and the agent is "you"; «بعذاب» is attached to «بشرهم» and «أليم» is an adjective; and the clause accompanied by the fāʾ is in the nominative position as the khabar of «إن».
(أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ): the clause is explicative of «الذين يقتلون», with no position; «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ and «الذين» is the khabar; the clause «حبطت أعمالهم» is the ṣila of the relative noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «حبطت».
(وَما لَهُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is negative; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted preposed khabar; «من» is a preposition redundant in wording; «ناصرين» is genitive in wording and nominative in position because it is a postposed mubtadaʾ.

* Benefits:
The grammarians and parsers have been accustomed to speak of the redundancy of some letters, and by their redundancy they do not mean that they came as idle or in vain; rather, for them they are redundant for emphasis. But we wish to lift the veil from something to which all of these were inattentive, which they repeated without grasping its import until it became among the self-evident dicta. You have so far met, and will meet, many of the letters they declared redundant, and yet they restricted their operation to the form and not the meaning. His saying «وما لهم من ناصرين» cannot dispense with the «من» redundant in wording: the khabar by its nature and original linguistic placing admits truth and falsehood, and it is «من» that transferred it from its first original placing to the signification of categorical negation and decisive denial. The reader will find in our book what will astonish him of the secrets of these letters, which the grammarians pass by hastily, saying they are redundant and leaving the student in a wilderness of perplexity, because the Book of Allah is not approached by falsehood from before it or from behind it.

dervis-irab:23-24.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيباً مِنَ الْكِتابِ): a resumptive statement, brought to express wonder at their state and the badness of their conduct. The hamza is for the interrogative of wonder; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; «تر» is an imperfect verb jussive through «لم», its sign of jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is "you"; «إلى الذين» is attached to «تر»; the seeing here is visual; the clause «أوتوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun, the wāw is the nāʾib fāʾil and «نصيبا» is the second direct object; «من الكتاب» is attached to an omitted adjective of «نصيبا».
(يُدْعَوْنَ إِلى كِتابِ اللَّهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ): the clause «يدعون» is a ḥāl; «يدعون» is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw is the nāʾib fāʾil; «إلى كتاب الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يدعون»; the lām of «ليحكم» is for cause and «يحكم» is an imperfect verb in the accusative through an implied «أن» after the lām of cause; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يدعون»; «بينهم» is an adverbial of place attached to «يحكم».
(ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّى فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ): «ثم» is a conjunction of order with delay; «يتولى» is a nominative imperfect verb; «فريق» is the agent; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective.
(وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ): the wāw is for ḥāl; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and «معرضون» a khabar; and the clause is in the accusative position as a ḥāl.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قالُوا): «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause is resumptive; the reference is to turning away from the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ; «بأنهم»: the bāʾ is a preposition, and «أن» with what it governs is in the genitive position through the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar, i.e. "that turning away is because of their saying"; the clause «قالوا» is the khabar of «أن».
(لَنْ تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّاماً مَعْدُوداتٍ): the clause is in the accusative position as the content of their saying; «لن» is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; «تمسنا» is an imperfect verb in the accusative through «لن», and «نا» is an attached pronoun in the accusative position as direct object; «النار» is the agent of «تمسنا»; «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «أياما» is an adverbial attached to «تمسنا»; «معدودات» is an adjective, its sign of accusative being the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural.
(وَغَرَّهُمْ فِي دِينِهِمْ ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; «غرهم» is a verb and direct object; «في دينهم» is attached to «غرهم»; «ما» is a relative noun in the nominative position as agent; the clause «كانوا يفترون» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «كان» and its noun, and the clause «يفترون» is its khabar.

dervis-irab:173-175.t:
* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ قالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ) «الذين» is a badal or a second adjective of «الذين استجابوا». But this i'rab is problematic, since those who responded to Allah and the Messenger are those who were present at the battle of Uḥud, whereas these to whom the said statement was addressed are believers in general, so badal or adjective status is unworkable. To avoid this difficulty we see it as preferable to parse the relative noun as accusative by an omitted verb for praise, the implied form being «امدح» ("praise"). The clause «قال» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قال»; and «الناس» is the agent. (إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ فَاخْشَوْهُمْ) The sentence is the content of what is said. «إن» and its noun; «قد» is a particle of confirmation; the clause «جمعوا» is the khabar of «إن»; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «جمعوا»; the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ; «اخشوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the agent and the hum the direct object. (فَزادَهُمْ إِيماناً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; «زاد» is conjoined to «قال», and the agent is a latent pronoun understood from «قال لهم», that is, the saying increased them; «إيمانا» is the second direct object, and it may also be parsed as tamyīz. (وَقالُوا: حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ) «وقالوا» is conjoined to «زادهم»; «حسبنا» is a fronted khabar and the nā a muḍāf ilayhi; «الله» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; «ونعم»: the wāw is circumstantial, and you may make it resumptive; «نعم» is a rigid past verb for forming praise; «الوكيل» is the agent; and the one specified for praise (makhṣūṣ bil-madḥ) is Allah the Exalted. (فَانْقَلَبُوا بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and the clause «انقلبوا» is conjoined to an implied element understood from the context, that is: "and they went out with the Prophet, and returned"; «بنعمة» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «انقلبوا» or to an omitted element, a ḥāl; «من الله» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, an adjective; and «فضل» is conjoined to «نعمة». (لَمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوءٌ) The clause is circumstantial; «يمسسهم» is an imperfect verb jussive by «لم», the hāʾ is the direct object, and «سوء» is the agent. (وَاتَّبَعُوا رِضْوانَ اللَّهِ) The clause is conjoined to the clause «انقلبوا». (وَاللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَظِيمٍ) The wāw is resumptive; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ, «ذو فضل» the khabar, and «عظيم» an adjective. (إِنَّما ذلِكُمُ الشَّيْطانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَوْلِياءَهُ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to identify the speaker. «إنما»: «ما» is a restrictive and «إن» is restricted; «ذلكم» is a mubtadaʾ; «الشيطان» is a second mubtadaʾ; the clause «يخوف» is the khabar of «الشيطان», and the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of the demonstrative. It is also permissible to parse «ذلكم» as a mubtadaʾ and «الشيطان» as a badal of «ذلكم», with the clause «يخوف» as the khabar of «ذلكم»; and it is also permissible to parse «ذلكم» as a mubtadaʾ and «الشيطان» as its khabar, with the clause «يخوف أولياءه» resumptive or a ḥāl. (فَلا تَخافُوهُمْ وَخافُونِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, that is, "if you are confident of this, then do not fear them"; «وخافون» is conjoined to «لا تخافوهم», the wāw is the agent and the nūn is the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya); the yāʾ of the first person is dropped optionally, in agreement with the seven readers in the script; «إن» is conditional; «كنتم» is kāna and its noun, the protasis in the position of a jussive by «إن»; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it; and «مؤمنين» is the khabar of «كنتم».

* Rhetoric:
1- Generality and particularity: the mention of "the people" in general after mentioning the particular group, namely those who shared in the expedition of Uḥud. This is a case of using the general term while intending the particular.
2- Ordered laff and nashr (the "folding and unfolding" figure) in His words «بنعمة من الله وفضل», with the folded and unfolded items left unmentioned: namely safety of the bodies, which goes back to «النعمة» (favour), and the profit from trade, which goes back to «الفضل» (bounty).

dervis-irab:176-176.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَحْزُنْكَ) With fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the zāy, it is a dialect form of «أحزنه»; both were read. Likewise «فتنه» and «أفتنه»: both are widespread dialect forms, since they are established through mass transmission (tawātur).

* I'rab:
(وَلا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ) A resumptive discourse, introduced to go to great lengths in consoling him ﷺ. The wāw is resumptive; «لا» is prohibitive; «يحزنك» is an imperfect verb jussive by «لا», the kāf is the direct object; «الذين» is the agent; the clause «يسارعون» is the ṣila of the relative noun; and «في الكفر» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يسارعون», because it includes the sense of "fall into". (إِنَّهُمْ لَنْ يَضُرُّوا اللَّهَ شَيْئاً) The sentence is causal and has no grammatical position, to signal that their harming the Prophet ﷺ is like harming Him, glory be to Him; in this is consolation for him and a cause for him to cast off grief altogether. It is the right of the Messenger to grieve at the hypocrisy of one who is hypocritical and the apostasy of one who apostatises, and this is a weighty lesson in self-esteem, confidence, preserving one's personality and composure when calamity descends. «إن» and its noun; the clause «لن يضروا الله» is its khabar; and «شيئا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, that is, "any harm at all". (يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَلَّا يَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ حَظًّا فِي الْآخِرَةِ) The clause is resumptive. «يريد الله» is a verb and an agent; «أن» and what is within its scope are an interpreted maṣdar, direct object of «يريد»; «حظا» is the first object of «يجعل»; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, the second direct object; and «في الآخرة» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, an adjective. (وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ) The clause is also resumptive, to go to lengths in their humiliation; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, a fronted khabar; «عذاب» is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and «عظيم» is an adjective of «عذاب».

* Rhetoric:
The indefiniteness (tankīr) in His words «شيئا»: the tanwīn increases the indefinite noun in generality and indefiniteness, and in smallness and insignificance, and that is to confirm the smallness, insignificance and meagre standing in which they are.

dervis-irab:177-178.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نُمْلِي لَهُمْ) We leave them to their affair. «أمليت له في الأمر» means "I delayed"; and «أمليت للبعير في القيد» means "I loosened and gave slack to the camel in the fetter".

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الْكُفْرَ بِالْإِيْمانِ) A resumptive discourse, to generalise the ruling to the disbelievers and apostates after it had been specific to the hypocrites. «إن» and its noun; the clause «اشتروا» is the ṣila of the relative noun; «الكفر» is a direct object; and «بالإيمان» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «اشتروا». (لَنْ يَضُرُّوا اللَّهَ شَيْئاً) Its i'rab has gone before, letter for letter, and the clause is the khabar of «إن». (وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) Its i'rab has gone before. (وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) The wāw is a conjunction on His words «ولا يحزنك», or resumptive, and perhaps the latter is preferable, to generalise the ruling. «لا» is prohibitive; «يحسبن» is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of a jussive by «لا»; «الذين» is the agent; and the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila. (أَنَّما نُمْلِي لَهُمْ خَيْرٌ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ) «أن» is a particle resembling the verb, and «ما» is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with the verb after it as a maṣdar which is the noun of «أن», that is, "that our granting respite..."; it may also be a relative, in which case it is its noun. By rights it should have been written separated from «أن», but the manner of the muṣḥaf is to write it joined to it. «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نملي»; «خير» is the khabar of «أن»; «لأنفسهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خير»; and «أن» and what follows it stand in the place of the two objects of «يحسبن». (إِنَّما نُمْلِي لَهُمْ لِيَزْدادُوا إِثْماً) The clause is resumptive, serving as a justification of the preceding one, being the reason for the granting of respite. «نملي» is an imperfect verb; «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «نملي»; the lām is the lām of causation; «يزدادوا» is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām of causation, and the wāw is the agent; «إثما» is tamyīz; and the preposition and its genitive noun («the lām of causation and the interpreted maṣdar») are attached to «نملي». (وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ) Its i'rab has gone before.

* Rhetoric:
1- The implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) in buying disbelief with belief; the discussion of this has gone before.
2- The explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya) in «الإملاء»: their being given respite and the rope being left slack on their withers is likened to the horse for which the rope is slackened so that it runs by its natural bent and goes up as it pleases. He omitted the thing likened (al-mushabbah), which is the granting of respite and leaving alone, and retained the thing to which it is likened (al-mushabbah bihi), which is the slackening.

dervis-irab:189-191.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) The wāw is a conjunction; ولله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ملك is a postponed mubtadaʾ; السموات is a muḍāf ilayhi and الأرض is conjoined to السموات. (وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) The wāw is a conjunction; الله is the mubtadaʾ; على كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قدير, and قدير is the khabar. (إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) A resumptive clause, introduced to explain His power, the Glorified, His existence and His knowledge. إن is a particle resembling the verb; في خلق السموات والأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of إن. (وَاخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ) Conjoined to خلق. (لَآياتٍ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ) The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات is the postponed ism of إن; ولأولي الألباب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of آيات. (الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ قِياماً وَقُعُوداً وَعَلى جُنُوبِهِمْ) الذين is an adjective of أولي الألباب; the clause يذكرون الله is a ṣila; قياما and قعودا are two ḥāls; and على جنوبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is:
"lying down"; the meaning is: they remember Him in all states, standing, sitting and lying down. The jurists have skilful inferences and allusions here, and among al-Shāfiʿī's curious arguments is that he used it as evidence for laying a sick person on his side in prayer. (وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) You may make the wāw a conjunction, so that the clause is conjoined to the preceding one and thus falls within the scope of the ṣila; or you may make the wāw circumstantial, so that the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (رَبَّنا ما خَلَقْتَ هذا باطِلًا) ربنا is a muḍāf one addressed (vocative); it is necessary to imply a saying, that is:
"they say: Our Lord"; so the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. ما is negative; خلقت is a verb and agent; هذا is a direct object; and باطلا is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with falsehood", or an adjective of an omitted verbal noun, i.e. "a vain creation", or a ḥāl from هذا; Abū Ḥayyān preferred this last view over the others. In our view they are equal in preponderance. (سُبْحانَكَ فَقِنا عَذابَ النَّارِ) سبحانك is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, and together with its omitted verb it is a parenthetical clause with no position. فقنا: the fāʾ is a conjunction of sequence, i.e. "we declare You transcendent, so protect us". You may also make it the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, with the sense of an implied recompense, i.e. "if You will our recompense, then protect us". قِ is an imperative verb; نا is the first direct object; and عذاب النار is the second direct object.

* Rhetoric:
1- Antithesis (ṭibāq): it combined the three states of man in prayer, which are standing, sitting and lying on the side, as al-Shāfiʿī says, or lying on the back, because it is lighter, as Abū Ḥanīfa says.
2- Synecdoche/figurative trope (majāz mursal) with the relation of locality: He mentioned the heavens and the earth, and meant by them the great bodies in them, marvellous in their making and fit to be exploited for the sake of comprehensive human benefit.
3- Concision (ījāz) in His words: ويتفكرون في خلق السموات والأرض, for under this concision is folded everything that science has brought forth of wonderful discoveries and marvellous inventions. In the hadith: «There is no worship like reflection.»

Descartes' philosophy of ideas:
We cannot here avoid pointing out that the philosophy of the Frenchman Descartes became known in the modern age as the philosophy of clear and distinct ideas, as they called it in the seventeenth century. That philosophy wanted to free thought from the weight of authorities of whatever kind, so it accepted no proof of truth except rational self-evidence, that is, the self-evidence of the reason, which the philosopher regards as the most equitably distributed of things among people, people's shares of it being equal, so there is no difference between one people and another and no superiority of one race over another. Descartes had the merit of building the edifice of the modern rationalist school when he laid down his famous rule:
I must never accept anything as true unless it has become evident to me by the self-evidence of reason that it is so, and I must not judge things except by what my mind represents with clarity and distinctness, such that every path to doubt is removed.
Between Descartes and Muḥammad ʿAbduh:
The effect of this philosophy appeared in the work of the Master, the Imam Muḥammad ʿAbduh, in the first years of this twentieth century, for it is no secret that the call which the Imam Muḥammad ʿAbduh rose to undertake for the reform of Muslim society in general rests on adopting Descartes' method of "clear and distinct ideas", on his giving the judgement of reason priority over the judgements of whim and emotion, and on his adopting certainty and self-evidence as the criterion for the soundness of reports or their fabrication.

Descartes' Meditations:
It is useful to summarise Descartes' six meditations, which are:
1- The self-evidence of reason, for the philosopher, is the criterion of certainty, that is, the distinguishing mark of sound knowledge.
2- The perishing of the human body is possible and easy, whereas the mind remains by its nature.
3- The idea of a perfect being in us includes a measure of objective reality, that is, it shares in conception in a degree of the grades of existence and perfection, such that it must proceed from an absolutely perfect cause.
4- All the things that you conceive very clearly and very distinctly are all true, and connect with the rational truths that can be known by the help of the natural light alone.
5- In the fifth meditation he speaks of the essence of material things, then returns to speak of Allah and His existence, relying on the criterion of self-evidence.
Since Descartes was a mathematician, and the first model of self-evidence for him was that of mathematical self-evidence, he looks at the clear idea we have in our minds of Allah and finds that its status is like that of the triangle, and he ends by saying:
The two propositions "the sum of the angles of a triangle equals two right angles" and "Allah exists" are two propositions equal in certainty.
6- In the sixth meditation Descartes ended by distinguishing the act of understanding from the act of imagination, saying: "I describe the marks of distinction, and in it I show that the soul of man is truly distinct from the body, and that it is nevertheless joined to it with a joining and united with it with a union that makes it and the body one thing; and in it I set out all the kinds of error arising from the senses, showing the means of avoiding them. And finally I adduce all the proofs from which the existence of the material world can be inferred, not because I see great benefit in them for establishing what I have established — I mean that the world exists, that people have bodies, and the like, things which no man of sound mind has ever doubted — but because close examination of them informs us that they have not attained, in firmness and self-evidence, the rank of the proofs that lead us to the knowledge of Allah and the knowledge of the soul; and in this respect the latter proofs are the most reliable and clear knowledge that can occur to the human mind."
4- [Translator's note: the numbering returns to 4 here in the source, and the item belongs to the Rhetoric list:] Multiple correspondence, so that it is called contrast (muqābala): he matched the heavens with the earth, the night with the day, and standing with sitting.

dervis-irab:192-193.t:
* I'rab:
(رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ مَنْ تُدْخِلِ النَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ) A resumptive clause, introduced to complete the tender and splendid supplications that began at the close of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān. ربنا is a muḍāf one addressed; وإنك: إن and its ism; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of accusative, a fronted direct object; تدخل is the protasis; النار is accusative by removal of the preposition, or a second direct object by extension; فقد: the fāʾ links the apodosis, because the apodosis is joined with قد; أخزيته is a verb, agent and direct object; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the whole sentence is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إن. (وَما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصارٍ)
The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; ما is negative; وللظالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; من is a redundant preposition, and أنصار is genitive in form by من and nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ. You may make ما the Ḥijāzī ما, acting like ليس, because they permitted the fronting of the khabar when it is an adverb or a preposition and its genitive noun. (رَبَّنا إِنَّنا سَمِعْنا مُنادِياً يُنادِي لِلْإِيمانِ) ربنا is a muḍāf one addressed; إن and its ism; the clause سمعنا is its khabar; مناديا is the object of سمعنا; the clause ينادي is an adjective; and للإيمان is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينادي. [Note: it is observed that the first-person pronoun «نا» is used in its three cases: the genitive by annexation to «ربّ», the accusative because it is the ism of إن, and the nominative as agent.] The whole clause is resumptive, introduced to complete the supplications. (أَنْ آمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ فَآمَنَّا) أن is a maṣdar particle and آمنوا an imperative verb; أن and what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ينادي. It is also possible that أن is the explicative one, which occurs after a sentence that has the meaning of saying without its letters; then the clause has no position. بربكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا; فآمنا: the fāʾ is a conjunction of sequence and immediacy, signalling the hastening of compliance with the call and of belief without delay, because the caller is Muḥammad or the Qur'an, and both are a spur to obedience and belief. (رَبَّنا فَاغْفِرْ لَنا ذُنُوبَنا وَكَفِّرْ عَنَّا سَيِّئاتِنا) He repeated the vocative, finding the arrangement sweet and adding to the appeal and the supplication. The fāʾ in His words «فاغفر» is a conjunction signalling that forgiveness follows upon belief in Him, the Exalted, and acknowledgement of His lordship; and there is nothing that more calls for forgiveness than that. ولنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اغفر; ذنوبنا is a direct object; كفّر is conjoined to اغفر; عنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كفر; and سيئاتنا is a direct object. (وَتَوَفَّنا مَعَ الْأَبْرارِ) Conjoined to what precedes; توفَّ is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the weak letter, and نا is its object; مع is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl; and الأبرار is a muḍāf ilayhi.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is prolixity (iṭnāb), which is adding wording to the meaning for a benefit, in several ways, among them:
a- Mentioning the specific after the general, to draw attention to the excellence of the specific. Among its examples in the Qur'an is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها»; He mentioned the mountains after the earth, though they are a part of it, as a prolixity intended for magnification and awe, in view of the fact that the mountains awe us with their loftiness and firmness, and yet they shrank from bearing the trust.
b- Mentioning the general after the specific. Among its examples is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «رب اغفر لي ولوالديّ ولمن دخل بيتي مؤمنا وللمؤمنين والمؤمنات», and these are two general words, within whose generality fall those mentioned before. The purpose is to convey inclusiveness while attending to the specific, which He mentioned twice, once alone and once included under the general.
c- Clarification after vagueness. Among its examples is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وقضينا إليه ذلك الأمر: أنّ دابر هؤلاء مقطوع»; His words «أن دابر هؤلاء مقطوع» clarify the vagueness contained in the word الأمر.
d- Repetition, to which reference has already been made, as in the saying of al-Ḥusayn ibn Muṭayr lamenting Maʿn ibn Zāʾida:
فيا قبر معن أنت أول حفرة ... من الأرض خطّت للسماحة موضعا
ويا قبر معن كيف واريت جوده ... وقد كان منه البرّ والبحر مترعا
(O grave of Maʿn, you are the first pit of the earth marked out as a place for generosity. / O grave of Maʿn, how did you cover his generosity, when land and sea were filled with it?)
The aim of it is to fix the meaning in the soul, and that is the original purpose. It may also be for warning, as occurs in the sermons of preachers, or for regret, as the lamenters do, or for savouring, as the love poets do.
e- Parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ): this is to bring, in the midst of speech or between two parts of speech connected in meaning, a clause with no grammatical position, for a secondary benefit, such as the supplicatory clause in the verse of ʿAwf ibn Muḥallim al-Khuzāʿī: إن الثمانين، وبلغتها ... قد أحوجت سمعي إلى ترجمان
(Eighty years — and may you reach them — have made my hearing need an interpreter.)
His words وبلغتها are a supplicatory clause that turns the heart of the one praised and is gentle in mentioning the intended point, which is that he is deaf and cannot hear his speech, so that he should raise his voice. Reference to this has already been made.
And precaution (iḥtirās), which is any addition that comes to ward off what the speech might suggest of something not intended, as in the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
إني أصاحب حلمي وهو بي كرم ... ولا أصاحب حلمي وهو بي جبن
(I keep company with my forbearance when it is generosity in me, and I do not keep company with my forbearance when it is cowardice in me.)
In the verse there is prolixity by precaution in two places: the first in the first hemistich, by mentioning «وهو بي كرم», and the second in the second hemistich, by mentioning «وهو بي جبن», to ward off what forbearance by itself might suggest. There are other purposes to which reference will be made in the contents of this book. In the verse there is also prolixity by repetition, namely the combination of «مناديا» and «ينادي»; for he mentioned the call first unrestricted, then in the second place restricted to belief, to magnify the status of the caller, because there is no caller greater than one who calls to belief, and he is Muḥammad ﷺ or the Qur'an that was sent down to him. Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī preferred that the caller is the Qur'an, and argued for it that many of those whom Allah described with this description in these verses were not among those who saw the Prophet ﷺ and heard his call to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and his summons, but it was the Qur'an.
2- In the verse there is also the art of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun. The apparent requirement was to say: وما لهم من أنصار or وماله من أنصار, in regard to the meaning or the wording of «من», but He used the overt noun to signal that disgrace is specific to them.

* Benefits:
Abū Ḥayyān said: «سمع», if it enters upon something heard, takes one object, as in سمعت كلام زيد, like other verbs. If it enters upon a person and after it comes a verb or a noun with its sense, as in سمعت زيدا يتكلم and سمعت زيدا يقول كذا, there is a dispute on this question: some held that this verb or noun, if preceded by an indefinite, is an adjective of it, or if by a definite, a ḥāl from it; and some held that this verb or noun is in the position of the second object of «سمع», making «سمع» a verb that takes one object if it enters upon something heard and two if it enters upon a person.

dervis-irab:194-195.t:
* I'rab:
(رَبَّنا وَآتِنا ما وَعَدْتَنا عَلى رُسُلِكَ) Speech conjoined to the supplications that preceded. ربنا is a muḍāf one addressed; آتنا is conjoined to the preceding verbs of supplication; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative, the first direct object; ما is a relative noun, the second direct object; the clause وعدتنا is the ṣila of the relative; and على رسلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to وعدتنا. A muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "upon the tongues of Your messengers" or "upon the confirmation of Your messengers". You may also attach them to an omitted ḥāl, i.e.
"sent down upon Your messengers" or "carried upon Your messengers", because the messengers are made to carry that. (وَلا تُخْزِنا يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تخزنا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative, a direct object; and يوم القيامة is an adverb of time attached to تخزنا. (إِنَّكَ لا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعادَ) The clause is a justification, with no position, justifying their petition; this is one of the doors of taking refuge with Allah, since otherwise Allah does not break the promise. إن and its ism, and the clause «لا يخلف الميعاد» is the khabar of إن. (فَاسْتَجابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ أَنِّي لا أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عامِلٍ مِنْكُمْ) The fāʾ is resumptive; استجاب is a past verb; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استجاب; ربهم is the fāʿil; وأني: أن and its ism are an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to استجاب to show the cause, as though He said: "their Lord answered them because I do not let go to waste"; the clause لا أضيع is the khabar of أن; عمل عامل is a direct object; and منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of عامل. (مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى بَعْضُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl from عامل after its qualification, i.e. "whose state, being from a male or a female, is settled among you", or a second adjective of عامل. Abū al-Baqāʾ parsed it as an identical badal of منكم, which is also acceptable. بعضكم is a mubtadaʾ and من بعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive, introduced to show women's partnership with men in the reward. Some made it parenthetical, and I do not think it far-fetched, since it occurs between His words «عمل عامل» and what elaborates the work of the workers, so it is sound that it falls between two connected parts of speech; al-Zamakhsharī preferred it. (فَالَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا وَأُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ) The fāʾ is resumptive, of consequence, indicating that the reward is only for one who combines these several attributes; so the clause is resumptive with no position. الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause هاجروا is the ṣila; أخرجوا is conjoined to هاجروا; and من ديارهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخرجوا. (وَأُوذُوا فِي سَبِيلِي وَقاتَلُوا وَقُتِلُوا) The whole clause is conjoined and falls within the scope of the ṣila. (لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ) The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; أكفرن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the oath clause is the khabar of الذين. Here an objection must be answered, one who says: the clause that comes as the answer to an oath has no position, so how is it permissible for it to be a khabar here? The answer is summarised in that what is intended is the oath and its answer together.
وعنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أكفرن; and سيئاتهم is a direct object. (وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ) The wāw is a conjunction; لأدخلنهم is conjoined to لأكفرن; the hāʾ is a direct object; جنات is accusative by removal of the preposition, or a second direct object by extension; and the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is an adjective of جنات. (ثَواباً مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ) ثوابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb giving emphasis; they permitted parsing it as a ḥāl from جنات, i.e. "rewarded with them", or from the pronoun that is a direct object, i.e. "while they are rewarded", and that is permissible. And من عند الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of ثوابا. (وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الثَّوابِ) The wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; عنده is an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar; حسن الثواب is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is the khabar of «الله».

* Rhetoric:
