1- In this verse there is an unparalleled art that may be called "recording" (al-isjāl), and its definition is that the speaker aims at one of the purposes and brings words that establish that purpose: the Lord, the Glorified, recorded on the tongues of His servants the realisation of what He promised on the tongue of His Messenger; consider the word «ما وعدتنا» and you will find that this promise has become binding, with no undoing of its binding. Among the curious examples of it in poetry is the saying of Ibn Nubāta al-Saʿdī:
جاء الشتاء وما عندي له عدد ... إلا ارتعادي وتصفيقي بأسناني
فإن هلكت فمولانا يكفنني ... هبني هلكت فهبني بعض أكفاني
(Winter has come and I have no equipment for it but my shivering and the chattering of my teeth. / If I perish, our master will shroud me: suppose I have perished — then grant me some of my shrouds.)
The recording is clear in his establishing "suppose I have perished", and how beautiful is the paronomasia between هبني meaning "reckon me" and هبني meaning "give me a gift".
2- Shift of person (iltifāt) in His words «فاستجاب لهم ربهم»: it shifted from the third person to the first person, to show the perfection of care for the issuing of the answer, to honour the supplicants, to equate men and women, and the partnership of women with men in work and in its recompense, after woman had been wronged in her right in the Jāhiliyya.
It is related that Umm Salama said: "O Messenger of Allah, I hear Allah the Exalted mention men in the hijra and not mention women", and so the verse was revealed.

dervis-irab:196-200.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النزل), with two ḍammas or with ḍamma and sukūn: what is prepared for the one who alights, or the guest's food. Abū al-Shaʿwāʾ al-Ḍabbī said:
وكنّا إذا الجبار بالجيش ضافنا ... جعلنا القنا والمرهفات له نزلا
(When the tyrant came to us as a guest with his army, we made the lances and the sharp swords his hospitality.)
(رابِطُوا) means: they stayed on the frontier; the origin is that these and those tie their horses, lying in wait, ready for raiding. And ribāṭ al-khayl is keeping them tied. He said:
فينا رباط جياد الخيل معلمه ... وفي كليب رباط الذلّ والعار
(Among us is the tethering of marked thoroughbred horses, and among Kulayb the tethering of humiliation and shame.)

* I'rab:
(لا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي الْبِلادِ) A resumptive clause, introduced to forbid the Prophet ﷺ from being deceived; in reality it is a prohibition to his Companions and followers against being deceived by what they see of the expansiveness of the disbelievers and the oppressive tyrants in the land and their plunging into power and prosperity, as is seen today. لا is prohibitive; يغرنك is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of jussive after لا; the kāf is a direct object; تقلب is the fāʿil; الذين is a relative noun, a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause كفروا is a ṣila; and في البلاد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تقلب because it is a verbal noun. (مَتاعٌ قَلِيلٌ ثُمَّ مَأْواهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ) متاع is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ and قليل an adjective, i.e. "it is a meagre enjoyment, of no regard, and however long it extends it is bound to vanish"; the clause is resumptive. ثم is a conjunction of delay; مأواهم is a mubtadaʾ and جهنم a khabar. (وَبِئْسَ الْمِهادُ) The wāw is circumstantial; بئس is a defective past verb to express censure; المهاد is the fāʿil of بئس; the one specified for censure is omitted, i.e. "Jahannam"; and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (لكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ) لكن is the lightened, inoperative one, merely for rectification (istidrāk); الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause اتقوا ربهم is the ṣila; ولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; جنات is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين; and the clause of لكن is resumptive. (تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها)
The clause is an adjective of جنات; من تحتها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجري; الأنهار is the fāʿil; خالدين is a ḥāl; and فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خالدين. (نُزُلًا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ) نزلا is a ḥāl from جنات, and if you make it a verbal noun it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; and من عند الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of «نزلا». (وَما عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لِلْأَبْرارِ) The wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; ما is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; عند الله is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of ما; خير is the khabar; وللأبرار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خير; and the clause is resumptive or circumstantial. (وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ لَمَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ) The wāw is resumptive; إن is a particle resembling the verb; من أهل الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of إن; ولمن: the lām is the shifted lām and من is a relative noun, the postponed ism of إن; the clause يؤمن بالله is the ṣila; and بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤمن. (وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ خاشِعِينَ لِلَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is a relative noun conjoined to الله; the clause أنزل إليكم is a ṣila; and ما أنزل إليهم is likewise conjoined; خاشعين is a ḥāl from the pronoun in يؤمن; and لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خاشعين. (لا يَشْتَرُونَ بِآياتِ اللَّهِ ثَمَناً قَلِيلًا) The clause لا يشترون is circumstantial; بآيات الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يشترون; ثمنا is a direct object and قليلا an adjective. (أُولئِكَ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ) The clause is resumptive; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; ولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; أجرهم is a postponed mubtadaʾ; عند ربهم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "settled with their Lord"; and the clause is the khabar of «أولئك». (إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ) A resumptive clause; إن with its ism and khabar. (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) Its i'rab has often preceded. (اصْبِرُوا وَصابِرُوا وَرابِطُوا) Verbs of supplication [Translator's note: the source says «أفعال دعاء»; the verbs are imperatives]. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ) Likewise conjoined. (لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ) لعل and its ism; the clause is its khabar; and the clause of hope is circumstantial.
[Note: page footer in the source: "م 10 - I'rab al-Qur'an" (volume/page marker)]

* Rhetoric:
The close of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān came out very beautifully. Just as the close of Sūrat al-Baqara came to include supplication, the close of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān came to include a number of beneficial counsels, and this is the beauty of the ending, so that it remains firmly fixed in the ears, and this is the beauty of exposition.

dervis-irab:181-182.t:
* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا) A resumptive clause, introduced to show examples of the Jews' lies, falsehood and fabrications against Allah. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of verification; سمع is a past verb and الله its fāʿil; قول is its object; الذين is a relative noun, a muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause قالوا is the ṣila of the relative. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ وَنَحْنُ أَغْنِياءُ) The clause is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); إن with its ism and khabar; ونحن: the wāw is a conjunction, نحن is a mubtadaʾ and أغنياء a khabar, and the clause is conjoined to what precedes. (سَنَكْتُبُ ما قالُوا) The speech is resumptive; the sīn is a particle of futurity; ما is a relative noun, a direct object of نكتب; and the clause قالوا is a ṣila with no position. It is also possible that it is a maṣdar particle, i.e. "their saying", and perhaps that is preferable, the clause being the ṣila of the particle-maṣdar. (وَقَتْلَهُمُ الْأَنْبِياءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ) The wāw is a conjunction; قتل is conjoined to ما or to the interpreted maṣdar; the hāʾ is a pronoun in the position of genitive by annexation; الأنبياء is a direct object of the maṣdar, which is al-qatl; and بغير حق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted word, in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (وَنَقُولُ ذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ) The wāw is a conjunction; the clause ذوقوا is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying; and عذاب الحريق is the object of ذوقوا. (ذلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ) The clause is resumptive with no position; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; the clause قدمت is the ṣila of the relative; and أيديكم is the fāʿil of قدمت. (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ) The wāw is a conjunction, and أن with what is within its scope is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the khabar; أن and its ism, and the clause of ليس is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أن; the ism of ليس is a latent pronoun; and بظلام: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and ظلام is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ليس. You may make the wāw resumptive, and the clause of أن and what follows it in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and the matter is that Allah ... etc."; and that is good.

* Rhetoric:
1- The implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) in His words ذوقوا عذاب الحريق, whose letters were pointed out earlier.
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq) between فقير and أغنياء.
3- The figurative trope (majāz mursal) in أيديكم, since what is meant is "your evil deeds", and the relation is causality, because the hand is the cause of the deeds that man commits.

dervis-irab:183-183.t:
* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ قالُوا: إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَهِدَ إِلَيْنا) الذين is a badal from the preceding relative in His words: «لقد سمع الله قول الذين», or an adjective of it, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, in which case the clause is resumptive; the clause قالوا is the ṣila of the relative; the clause إن الله etc. is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying; إن and its ism; the clause عهد is its khabar; and إلينا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عهد. (أَلَّا نُؤْمِنَ لِرَسُولٍ) أن is the maṣdar particle, and it with what is within its scope is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "He commanded us in the Torah not to believe a messenger"; and لرسول is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نؤمن. (حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنا بِقُرْبانٍ تَأْكُلُهُ النَّارُ) حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; يأتينا is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied أن after حتى; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative, a direct object; بقربان is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأتينا; and the clause تأكله النار is an adjective of قربان; the al in النار is for familiarity, i.e. the one known to them to descend from heaven; the details are to be consulted in the longer works. (قُلْ: قَدْ جاءَكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِي) The speech is resumptive, introduced to rebuke them for lying and fabrication; قل is an imperative verb whose agent is "you"; the clause قد جاءكم is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying; رسل is the fāʿil; and من قبلي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of رسل. (بِالْبَيِّناتِ وَبِالَّذِي قُلْتُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جاءكم; بالذي is conjoined to His words بالبينات; and the clause قلتم is the ṣila of the relative. (فَلِمَ قَتَلْتُمُوهُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; the lām is a preposition, and the interrogative ما, its alif omitted, is in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قتلتموهم; قتلتموهم is a verb, agent and direct object, and the wāw is for the lengthening of the vowel of the mīm; إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis, the tāʾ being the ism of كان and صادقين its khabar; and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then why did you kill them?"

dervis-irab:184-185.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَتاعُ الْغُرُورِ): al-matāʿ is everything a person enjoys, of wealth and other things; and al-ghurūr is the verbal noun of gharra, i.e. to deceive; al-ghurūr is also falsehood.

* I'rab:
(فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كُذِّبَ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ) A resumptive clause, introduced to console him ﷺ. The fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; كذبوك is a verb, agent and direct object, in the position of jussive as the protasis; فقد: the fāʾ links the apodosis, قد is a particle of verification, كذب is a passive past verb, رسل is the nāʾib fāʿil, and من قبلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of رسل. (جاؤُ بِالْبَيِّناتِ وَالزُّبُرِ وَالْكِتابِ الْمُنِيرِ) The clause is an adjective of رسل; بالبينات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جاءوا, and what follows is conjoined to it; and المنير is an adjective of الكتاب. (كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ) A resumptive clause, introduced as a completion of his consolation ﷺ; كل نفس is a mubtadaʾ and ذائقة الموت its khabar. (وَإِنَّما تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; إنما is the restricting particle (kāffa) and the restricted (makfūfa); توفون is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; أجوركم is a second direct object; and يوم القيامة is an adverb of time attached to توفون. (فَمَنْ زُحْزِحَ عَنِ النَّارِ وَأُدْخِلَ الْجَنَّةَ فَقَدْ فازَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ; زحزح is a past verb in the position of jussive, the protasis, and it is passive, its nāʾib fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; عن النار is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to زحزح; أدخل is conjoined to زحزح, the nāʾib fāʿil being latent; الجنة is accusative by removal of the preposition; the fāʾ links the apodosis; قد is a particle of verification; فاز is a past verb; and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من». (وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا إِلَّا مَتاعُ الْغُرُورِ) The wāw is resumptive; ما is negative; الحياة is a mubtadaʾ; الدنيا an adjective; إلا is a particle of restriction; and متاع الغرور is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is an eloquent simile (tashbīh baligh): He likened the world to the commodity with which its seller deceives the one who seeks it until he is taken in and buys it. The Glorified brought the speech out with this simile in the manner of denunciation of one who makes it his habit to be deluded by the world and to savour its dregs, while in reality there is no benefit in it and nothing of substance beneath it; and what benefit can be hoped for from a thing that is beset by perishing?!

dervis-irab:186-186.t:
* Vocabulary:
(عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ): that is, the things resolved upon (maʿzūmātihā); so the verbal noun was made to have the sense of a passive participle.

* I'rab:
(لَتُبْلَوُنَّ فِي أَمْوالِكُمْ وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ) The lām prepares for the oath; تبلون is an imperfect verb in the nominative, its sign of the nominative being the persistence of the nūn, which was omitted because of the succession of like letters, and the plural wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative, the nāʾib fāʿil [Translator's note: the source says "fāʿil"]; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; في أموالكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تبلون; and أنفسكم is conjoined to أموالكم. The clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an implied oath, and the oath clause is resumptive, introduced to begin consoling the Prophet ﷺ and the believers with him for the hardships they will be targeted with; and the benefit of consolation is to accustom the soul to bearing hardships when they occur and to prepare for the consequences, whatever they may be. (وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction and the lām the answer to an implied oath also; تسمعن is parsed like تبلون; من الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تسمعنّ; the clause أوتوا is a ṣila, and the wāw in أوتوا is a nāʾib fāʿil; الكتاب is a second direct object; and من قبلكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا أَذىً كَثِيراً) ومن الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun conjoined to «من الذين أوتوا الكتاب», both attached to تسمعن; أذى is a direct object of تسمعن and كثيرا an adjective. (وَإِنْ تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا فَإِنَّ ذلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ) The wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; تصبروا is the protasis; تتقوا is conjoined to تصبروا; فإن: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and إن is a particle resembling the verb; ذلك is its ism; and من عزم الأمور is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of it. The clause joined with the fāʾ has no grammatical position because it is in the nature of a justification for the omitted apodosis, which it stands in place of, the implication being: "and if you are patient and fear Allah, it is better for you", or "then you have done well", or "you have hit the mark of rightness"; and you may make it the apodosis itself, the reference being to the patience of those addressed.

dervis-irab:187-187.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النّبذ): casting behind the back. It became a proverb for not reckoning with a thing and turning away from it entirely. It was treated fully in Sūrat al-Baqara, as was the statement that some scholars made it one of the verbs of transformation, as will come.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ) A resumptive clause, introduced to show their concealment of the evidences of his prophethood and the signs of his truthfulness. The wāw is resumptive; إذ is an adverb of past time attached to an omitted word, that is: "Remember the time when Allah took the covenant"; أخذ is a past verb and الله its fāʿil; ميثاق الذين is a direct object, and the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation; the clause أوتوا الكتاب is the ṣila of the relative, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil and الكتاب a second direct object. (لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلا تَكْتُمُونَهُ) The lām is the answer to the oath indicated by the taking of the covenant, as though He said to them: "By Allah, you shall make it clear". It was read with yāʾ. تبيننه is an imperfect verb in the nominative, its sign of the nominative being the persistence of the nūn, omitted because of the succession of like letters; counterparts of it have preceded, and the covenant is not old. وللناس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تبينّنه»; ولا تكتمونه: the wāw is a conjunction and the clause is conjoined to تبيننه; you may make the wāw circumstantial, so that the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (فَنَبَذُوهُ وَراءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; نبذوه is a verb, agent and direct object; and وراء ظهورهم is accusative as a second object, as preceded in Sūrat al-Baqara; many parsed it as an adverb, and they did not require the fāʿil to be settled with the adverb. (وَاشْتَرَوْا بِهِ ثَمَناً قَلِيلًا) The wāw is a conjunction; اشتروا is conjoined to نبذوه; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اشتروا; ثمنا is a direct object and قليلا an adjective. (فَبِئْسَ ما يَشْتَرُونَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; بئس is a defective past verb to express censure; ما is a complete indefinite, accusative as tamyīz, and it has specified the fāʿil of بئس. It is also possible that it is a maṣdar particle, interpreted with the verb as a verbal noun that is the fāʿil, i.e. "their purchase", and it has preceded.
The one specified for censure is omitted, i.e. "this".

* Rhetoric:
1- Shift of person (iltifāt): He moved from the third person in His words «وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب» to the second person in His words «لتبيننه», then returned to the third person; the benefit of this is to increase the direct recording against them.
2- The implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) in اشتروا به, which has preceded.

dervis-irab:188-188.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المفازة): the place of success and deliverance; it may also be a mīmī verbal noun. The desert was called mafāza as a good omen of safety and success.

* I'rab:
(لا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِما أَتَوْا) A resumptive clause, introduced to show their heedlessness and their being led along by their delusions. لا is prohibitive; تحسبن is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of jussive after لا, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you"; الذين is a direct object; the clause يفرحون is the ṣila of the relative; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يفرحون; and the clause أتوا has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (وَيُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِما لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا) يحبون is conjoined to يفرحون; أن with what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of accusative, a direct object; بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يحمدوا; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussion; يفعلوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, its sign of the jussive being the omission of the nūn; and the clause is the ṣila of the relative. (فَلا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ بِمَفازَةٍ مِنَ الْعَذابِ) The fāʾ is redundant, to improve the wording; they have cited, for the redundancy of the fāʾ in a construction of this kind, the verse of the poet:
وحتى تركت العائدات يعدنه ... يقلن فلا تبعد وقلت له ابعد
(Until I left the visitors visiting him, saying "Do not go far", and I said to him "Go far".) that is: "do not go far". So the parsers have parsed it, and the commentators followed them.
I see that it is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, which usually precedes a sentence of refreshing the reader's vigour after the omission of the second object of the first تحسبن, i.e. "do not think them saved".
And if you wish to be fully certain of their fate, then "do not think them". And بمفازة is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of second object of تحسبنهم; and من العذاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of مفازة if you regard it as a noun of place, and attached to بمفازة if you regard it as a mīmī verbal noun. (وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) The wāw is resumptive; ولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; عذاب is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and أليم is a naʿt.
